Input

What can I use Langfuse for?

Output

Langfuse is an open‑source AI engineering platform to debug, analyze, and iterate on LLM/agent apps.

What you can use it for

  • Observability & tracing: Capture end‑to‑end traces of LLM calls, tool/retrieval steps, token/cost/latency; inspect timelines, sessions, users, and agent graphs
    • Docs: https://langfuse.com/docs/observability/overview
    • Get started: https://langfuse.com/docs/observability/get-started
  • Monitoring & analytics: Build custom dashboards and set alerts for quality, cost, latency, volume
    • Dashboards: https://langfuse.com/docs/metrics/features/custom-dashboards
    • Alerts: https://langfuse.com/docs/observability/features/alerts
  • Prompt management: Version, label/deploy prompts, attach JSON config (model, schema, tools), test in playground, link prompts to traces
    • Overview: https://langfuse.com/docs/prompt-management/overview
    • Config: https://langfuse.com/docs/prompt-management/features/config
  • Evaluation: LLM‑as‑a‑judge, code/custom evaluators, user feedback, datasets, and experiments for systematic testing in dev and production
    • Overview: https://langfuse.com/docs/evaluation/overview
    • Datasets/experiments: https://langfuse.com/docs/evaluation/features/datasets
  • Cost/latency/user analytics: Track per‑user usage, sessions, environments; analyze trade‑offs over time and by release
    • Users: https://langfuse.com/docs/observability/features/users
    • Environments: https://langfuse.com/docs/observability/features/environments
  • API & data access: Query observations/metrics via SDKs/CLI for pipelines, billing, or external BI
    • SDK querying: https://langfuse.com/docs/api-and-data-platform/features/query-via-sdk
    • CLI: https://langfuse.com/docs/api-and-data-platform/features/cli
  • Integrations & ingest: Python/JS SDKs, OpenTelemetry, 100+ frameworks/providers, and LLM gateways
    • Overview: https://langfuse.com/docs
    • Integrations list: https://langfuse.com/llms-integrations.txt
  • Self‑hosting & enterprise: Open source, self‑hostable, RBAC/SSO/SCIM, export to blob storage
    • Self‑hosting: https://langfuse.com/llms-self-hosting.txt

Quick start

  • Create a free account and explore the example project: https://langfuse.com/cloud
  • Full platform overview: https://langfuse.com/docs

{"type": "text", "text": "# Langfuse\n\n> Langfuse is an **open-source AI engineering platform** ([GitHub](https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse)) that helps teams collaboratively debug, analyze, and iterate on their LLM applications. All platform features are natively integrated to accelerate the development workflow.\n\n## Markdown Access\n\nEvery page on langfuse.com is available as plain Markdown. Append `.md` to any URL, or send an `Accept: text/markdown` header:\n\n```bash\ncurl https://langfuse.com/docs/observability/get-started.md\n```\n\nThe links in the section indexes below already point at the `.md` variants.\n\n## Docs Search API\n\nSemantic search (RAG) over the Langfuse documentation, returning an answer with the relevant pages and excerpts. No authentication required. Use this instead of guessing when a specific page does not answer the question:\n\n```bash\ncurl -sG \"https://langfuse.com/api/search-docs\" --data-urlencode \"query=How do I trace a LangGraph agent?\"\n```\n\n- **Endpoint**: `https://langfuse.com/api/search-docs?query=<question>`\n- **Documentation**: [REST endpoint](https://langfuse.com/docs/docs-mcp#rest-endpoint)\n\nAsk specific, self-contained questions in natural language. This is the same search that backs the `searchLangfuseDocs` MCP tool below.\n\n## Langfuse Docs MCP Server\n\nConnect to the Langfuse Docs MCP server to access documentation directly in your AI editor:\n\n- **Endpoint**: `https://langfuse.com/api/mcp`\n- **Transport**: `streamableHttp`\n- **Documentation**: [Langfuse Docs MCP Server](https://langfuse.com/docs/docs-mcp)\n\nThe MCP server provides tools to search Langfuse documentation, GitHub issues, and discussions. See the [installation guide](https://langfuse.com/docs/docs-mcp) for setup instructions in Cursor, VS Code, Claude Desktop, and other MCP clients.\n\n## Langfuse Skill for AI Coding Agents\n\nInstall the Langfuse skill before implementing anything with Langfuse. The skill provides up-to-date documentation, best-practice workflows for instrumentation, prompt management, and programmatic API access via the Langfuse CLI.\n\nInstall from: [github.com/langfuse/skills](https://github.com/langfuse/skills/tree/main/skills/langfuse)\n\n## Tracing Best Practices\n\nBefore instrumenting an application with Langfuse, read [What does a good trace look like?](https://langfuse.com/docs/observability/best-practices.md) — it covers trace scope, observation naming, meaningful input/output, and the attributes (metadata, tags, users, sessions) {"type": "text", "text": "{\"content\": [{\"type\": \"document\", \"record_type\": \"documentation\", \"url\": \"https://langfuse.com/docs/observability/overview\", \"title\": \"Observability & Application Tracing\", \"source\": {\"content\": [{\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"LLM Observability & Application Tracing (Open Source) - Langfuse\\n[Docs](/docs)\\n[Observability](/docs/observability/overview)\\n[Overview](/docs/observability/overview)\\n# Observability & Application Tracing\\nGenerative AI systems are inherently non-deterministic. Therefore, debugging your application without any observability tool is more like guesswork. Implementing comprehensive AI observability gives you the tools to understand what's happening inside your application and why. It is the foundation for continuously evaluating and improving your system.\\nThe core of this is **application tracing** — structured logs of every request that capture the exact prompt sent, the model's response, token usage, latency, and any tools or retrieval steps in between.\\nHere's an example of a trace in the Langfuse UI:\\n🚀\\nWant to see it in action? [**Create a free account**](/cloud) and explore Langfuse Observability in the [interactive example project](/docs/demo).\\n## Getting Started\\nStart by [setting up your first trace](/docs/observability/get-started), and compare it against our [best practices guide](/docs/observability/best-practices) so you're set up for success. If you're new to AI observability, take a look at the [core concepts](/docs/observability/data-model) too.\\n## Use your traces\\nOnce traces are coming in, the next step is to make sense of them and use what you learn to improve your agent. Read the chapter on [Monitoring in the Langfuse Academy](/academy/monitoring) to learn how to utilize your traces well.\\nFor feature-specific implementation guidance, these are the most common ones to start with:\\n * Track [model usage and cost](/docs/observability/features/token-and-cost-tracking)\\n * Monitor application quality with [scores](/docs/evaluation/scores/overview)\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\n * Analyze cost, latency, volume, and quality in [custom dashboards](/docs/metrics/features/custom-dashboards)\\n * Get notified when a metric crosses a threshold with [alerts](/docs/observability/features/alerts)\\nBrowse the Features section in the sidebar for a complete list of observability features.\\n## FAQ\\nWhat is the difference between observability and tracing?\\n+\\n **Observability** is the broader capability of understanding the internal state of your system from its outputs. It encompasses tracing, metrics, and logging. **Tracing** is a specific observability technique that records the flow of a request through your system, preserving causal relationships between operations. In the context of LLM applications, tracing is the most important observability tool because it captures the full context of each request — prompts, responses, tool calls, and their relationships.\\nWhat is application tracing?\\n+\\nApplication tracing records the complete lifecycle of a request as it flows through your system. Each trace captures every operation — LLM calls, retrieval steps, tool executions, and custom logic — along with timing, inputs, outputs, and metadata. This gives you full visibility into what happened during each request, enabling debugging, performance optimization, and quality monitoring.\\nHow does Langfuse compare to other tracing solutions?\\n+\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\nLangfuse is purpose-built for LLM applications, which means it natively understands LLM-specific concepts like token usage, model parameters, prompt/completion pairs, and evaluation scores. Unlike general-purpose APM tools, Langfuse provides features specific to AI engineering: [LLM-as-a-Judge evaluation](/docs/evaluation/evaluation-methods/llm-as-a-judge), [prompt management](/docs/prompt-management/overview), [experiments and datasets](/docs/evaluation/experiments/datasets), and [custom dashboards](/docs/metrics/features/custom-dashboards). It's also [open source](/self-hosting) and can be self-hosted.\\nDoes Langfuse add latency to my application?\\n+\\nNo. Langfuse SDKs send tracing data asynchronously in the background. Trace events are queued locally and flushed in batches, so your application's response time is not affected. See [queuing and batching](/docs/observability/features/queuing-batching) for details.\\n* * *\\n* * *\\nLast edited 8/28/2026\\n\"}], \"type\": \"content\"}}, {\"type\": \"document\", \"record_type\": \"documentation\", \"url\": \"https://langfuse.com/docs/observability/features/users\", \"title\": \"User Tracking\", \"source\": {\"content\": [{\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\n {\\\"role\\\": \\\"user\\\", \\\"content\\\": \\\"1 + 1 = \\\"}\\n ],\\n temperature=0,\\n )\\n```\\nUse `propagate_attributes()` with the CallbackHandler:\\n \\n \\n```\\nfrom langfuse import get_client, propagate_attributes\\nfrom langfuse.langchain import CallbackHandler\\nlangfuse = get_client()\\nhandler = CallbackHandler()\\nwith langfuse.start_as_current_observation(as_type=\\\"span\\\", name=\\\"langchain-call\\\"):\\n # Propagate user_id to all observations\\n with propagate_attributes(user_id=\\\"user_12345\\\"):\\n # Pass handler to the chain invocation\\n chain.invoke(\\n {\\\"animal\\\": \\\"dog\\\"},\\n config={\\\"callbacks\\\": [handler]},\\n )\\n```\\nUse `propagateAttributes()` with the CallbackHandler:\\n \\n \\n```\\nimport { startActiveObservation, propagateAttributes } from \\\"@langfuse/tracing\\\";\\nimport { CallbackHandler } from \\\"@langfuse/langchain\\\";\\nconst langfuseHandler = new CallbackHandler();\\nawait startActiveObservation(\\\"langchain-call\\\", async () => {\\n // Propagate userId to all observations\\n await propagateAttributes(\\n {\\n userId: \\\"user-123\\\",\\n },\\n async () => {\\n // Pass handler to the chain invocation\\n await chain.invoke(\\n { input: \\\"<user_input>\\\" },\\n { callbacks: [langfuseHandler] }\\n );\\n }\\n );\\n});\\n```\\nNote on Attribute Propagation\\nWe use Attribute Propagation to propagate `userId` across all observations of a trace. We will use all observations with `userId` to create `userId`-level metrics. Please consider the following when using Attribute Propagation:\\n * Values must be **strings ≤200 characters**\\n * Call **early in your trace** to ensure all observations are covered. This way you make sure that all Metrics in Langfuse are accurate.\\n * Invalid values are dropped with a warning\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\n **Learn more:** [Python SDK](/docs/observability/sdk/instrumentation#propagate-attributes) | [TypeScript SDK](/docs/observability/sdk/instrumentation#propagate-attributes)\\n## Deep-linking\\nYou can deep link to this view via the following URL format: `https://<hostname>/project/{projectId}/users/{userId}`\\n## Related Resources\\n * Build [custom dashboards](/docs/metrics/features/custom-dashboards) to visualize user-level metrics such as cost, token usage, and trace counts.\\n * To programmatically query aggregated per-user metrics such as cost, token usage, and trace counts, use the [Metrics API](/docs/metrics/features/metrics-api).\\n## GitHub Discussions\\n[Allow disabling manual signups without affecting SSO](https://github.com/orgs/langfuse/discussions/11557 \\\"Langfuse Ideas: Allow disabling manual signups without affecting SSO\\\")\\n[Adding a unique user count for the period selected](https://github.com/orgs/langfuse/discussions/9523 \\\"Langfuse Ideas: Adding a unique user count for the period selected\\\")\\n[Dashboard: Big number count for total users (and sessions)](https://github.com/orgs/langfuse/discussions/8468 \\\"Langfuse Ideas: Dashboard: Big number count for total users \\\\(and sessions\\\\)\\\")\\n[Dashboard: add chart for unique users (MAU/WAU/DAU)](https://github.com/orgs/langfuse/discussions/3472 \\\"Langfuse Ideas: Dashboard: add chart for unique users \\\\(MAU/WAU/DAU\\\\)\\\")\\n[fetch all users via sdk/api](https://github.com/orgs/langfuse/discussions/2975 \\\"Langfuse Ideas: fetch all users via sdk/api\\\")\\n[Adding access to User's sessions directly](https://github.com/orgs/langfuse/discussions/2919 \\\"Langfuse Ideas: Adding access to User's sessions directly\\\")\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\n[Use Langchain LCEL + Langserve + run time user_id/session_id](https://github.com/orgs/langfuse/discussions/2501 \\\"Langfuse Ideas: Use Langchain LCEL + Langserve + run time user_id/session_id\\\")\\n[Adding userId / author to score (custom metadata)](https://github.com/orgs/langfuse/discussions/2469 \\\"Langfuse Ideas: Adding userId / author to score \\\\(custom metadata\\\\)\\\")\\n[Support querying Users (GET) to support analytics pipeline solutions](https://github.com/orgs/langfuse/discussions/2176 \\\"Langfuse Ideas: Support querying Users \\\\(GET\\\\) to support analytics pipeline solutions\\\")\\n[User-level dashboard](https://github.com/orgs/langfuse/discussions/1794 \\\"Langfuse Ideas: User-level dashboard\\\")\\n[Dedicated user object which can include groups/teams and other attributes](https://github.com/orgs/langfuse/discussions/1154 \\\"Langfuse Ideas: Dedicated user object which can include groups/teams and other attributes\\\")\\n[How to set Individual user_id with batch inference.](https://github.com/orgs/langfuse/discussions/5927 \\\"Langfuse Support: How to set Individual user_id with batch inference.\\\")\\n[How to avoid memory leaks due to LangchainCallbackHandler while using userId and sessionId](https://github.com/orgs/langfuse/discussions/3485 \\\"Langfuse Support: How to avoid memory leaks due to LangchainCallbackHandler while using userId and sessionId\\\")\\n[How to get costs associated with an API call / user?](https://github.com/orgs/langfuse/discussions/3466 \\\"Langfuse Support: How to get costs associated with an API call trace?\\\")\\nGitHubSupportGitHubIdeas\\nUpvotes\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\n[NewGitHub](https://github.com/orgs/langfuse/discussions/new/choose)\\n * [1votesHow to set Individual user_id \"type\": \"content\"}}, {\"type\": \"document\", \"record_type\": \"documentation\", \"url\": \"https://langfuse.com/docs/prompt-management/features/config\", \"title\": \"Prompt Config\", \"source\": {\"content\": [{\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"Config - Langfuse\\n[Docs](/docs)\\n[Prompt Management](/docs/prompt-management/overview)\\n[Features](/docs/prompt-management/features/link-to-traces)\\n[Config](/docs/prompt-management/features/config)\\n# Prompt Config\\nThe prompt `config` in Langfuse is an **optional arbitrary JSON object** attached to each prompt, that can be used by code executing the LLM call. Common use cases include:\\n * storing model parameters (`model`, `temperature`, `max_tokens`)\\n * storing structured output schemas (`response_format`)\\n * storing function/tool definitions (`tools`, `tool_choice`)\\nBecause the config is **versioned together with the prompt** , you can manage all parameters in one place. This makes it easy to switch models, update schemas, or tune behavior without touching your application code.\\n## Setting the config\\nSetting the config can be done both via the Langfuse prompt UI and via the SDKs.\\nUIPython SDKJS/TS SDK\\nTo add or edit a config for your prompt:\\n 1. Navigate to **Prompt Management** in the Langfuse UI\\n 2. Select or create a prompt\\n 3. In the prompt editor, find the **Config** field (JSON editor)\\n 4. Enter your config as a valid JSON object\\n 5. Save the prompt — the config is now versioned with this prompt version\\nPass the `config` parameter when creating or updating a prompt:\\n \\n \\n```\\nfrom langfuse import get_client\\nlangfuse = get_client()\\n///# example config with a model and temperature\\nconfig = {\\n \\\"model\\\": \\\"gpt-4o\\\",\\n \\\"temperature\\\": 0\\n}\\nlangfuse.create_prompt(\\n name=\\\"invoice-extractor\\\",\\n type=\\\"chat\\\",\\n prompt=[\\n {\\n \\\"role\\\": \\\"system\\\",\\n \\\"content\\\": \\\"Extract structured data from invoices.\\\"\\n }\\n ],\\n config=config\\n)\\n```\\nPass the `config` parameter when creating or updating a prompt:\\n \\n \\n```\\nimport { LangfuseClient } from \\\"@langfuse/client\\\";\\nconst langfuse = new LangfuseClient();\\n// example config with a model and temperature\\nconst config = {\\n model: \\\"gpt-4o\\\",\\n temperature: 0\\n}\\nawait langfuse.prompt.create({\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\n name: \\\"invoice-extractor\\\",\\n type: \\\"chat\\\",\\n prompt: [\\n { role: \\\"system\\\", content: \\\"Extract structured data from invoices.\\\" }\\n ],\\n config: config\\n});\\n```\\nYou can test your prompt with its config directly in the [Playground](/docs/prompt-management/features/playground).\\n## Using the config\\nThe example below retrieves the AI model and temperature from the prompt config.\\nAfter fetching a prompt, access the config via the `config` property and pass the values to your LLM call.\\nPython SDKJS/TS SDK\\nThis example uses the [Langfuse OpenAI integration](/docs/integrations/openai/python/get-started) for tracing, but this is optional. You can use any method to call your LLM (e.g., OpenAI SDK directly, other providers, etc.).\\n \\n \\n```\\nfrom langfuse import get_client\\n///# Initialize Langfuse OpenAI client for this example.\\nfrom langfuse.openai import OpenAI\\nclient = OpenAI()\\nlangfuse = get_client()\\n///# Fetch prompt\\nprompt = langfuse.get_prompt(\\\"invoice-extractor\\\")\\n///# Access config values\\ncfg = prompt.config\\nmodel = cfg.get(\\\"model\\\")\\ntemperature = cfg.get(\\\"temperature\\\")\\n///# Use in your LLM call\\nclient.chat.completions.create(\\n model=model,\\n temperature=temperature,\\n messages=prompt.prompt\\n)\\n```\\nThis example uses the [Langfuse OpenAI integration](/docs/integrations/openai/js/get-started) for tracing, but this is optional. You can use any method to call your LLM (e.g., OpenAI SDK directly, other providers, etc.) and still use the config.\\n \\n \\n```\\nimport { LangfuseClient } from \\\"@langfuse/client\\\";\\n// Initialize OpenAI client for this example.\\nimport OpenAI from \\\"openai\\\";\\nimport { observeOpenAI } from \\\"@langfuse/openai\\\";\\nconst client = observeOpenAI(new OpenAI());\\nconst langfuse = new LangfuseClient();\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\n// Fetch prompt\\nconst prompt = await langfuse.prompt.get(\\\"invoice-extractor\\\");\\n// Access config values\\nconst cfg = prompt.config;\\nconst model = cfg.model;\\nconst temperature = cfg.temperature;\\n// Use in your LLM call\\nclient.chat.completions.create({\\n model,\\n temperature,\\n messages: prompt.prompt\\n});\\n```\\n## Example use cases\\n### Structured Outputs\\nWhen you need your LLM to return data in a specific JSON format, store the schema in your prompt config. This keeps the schema versioned alongside your prompt and lets you update it without code changes.\\n**Best practice:** Use `response_format` with `type: \\\"json_schema\\\"` and `strict: true` to enforce the schema. This ensures the model's output exactly matches your expected structure. If you're using Pydantic models, convert them with `type_to_response_format_param` — see the [OpenAI Structured Outputs guide](/docs/integrations/openai/python/structured-outputs).\\n \\n \\n```\\nfrom langfuse import get_client\\nfrom langfuse.openai import OpenAI\\nlangfuse = get_client()\\nclient = OpenAI()\\n///# Fetch prompt with config containing response_format\\nprompt = langfuse.get_prompt(\\\"invoice-extractor\\\")\\nsystem_message = prompt.compile()\\n///# Extract parameters from config\\ncfg = prompt.config\\n///# Example config:\\n///# {\\n///# \\\"response_format\\\": {\\n///# \\\"type\\\": \\\"json_schema\\\",\\n///# \\\"json_schema\\\": {\\n///# \\\"name\\\": \\\"invoice_schema\\\",\\n///# \\\"schema\\\": {\\n///# \\\"type\\\": \\\"object\\\",\\n///# \\\"properties\\\": {\\n///# \\\"invoice_number\\\": { \\\"type\\\": \\\"string\\\" },\\n///# \\\"total\\\": { \\\"type\\\": \\\"number\\\" }\\n///# },\\n///# \\\"required\\\": [\\\"invoice_number\\\", \\\"total\\\"],\\n///# \\\"additionalProperties\\\": false\\n///# },\\n///# \\\"strict\\\": true\\n///# }\\n///# }\\n///# }\\nresponse_format = cfg.get(\\\"response_format\\\")\\nres = client.chat.completions.create(\\n model=\\\"gpt-4o\\\",\\n messages=[\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\n {\\\"role\\\": \\\"system\\\", \\\"content\\\": system_message},\\n {\\\"role\\\": \\\"user\\\", \\\"content\\\": \\\"Extract invoice number and total from: ...\\\"},\\n ],\\n response_format=response_format,\\n langfuse_prompt=prompt, ///# Links this generation to the prompt version in Langfuse\\n)\\n///# Response is guaranteed to match your schema\\ncontent = res.choices[0].message.content\\n```\\n### Function Calling\\nFor agents and tool-using applications, store your function definitions in the prompt config. This allows you to version and update your available tools alongside your prompts.\\n**Best practice:** Store `tools` (function definitions with JSON Schema parameters) and `tool_choice` in your config. This keeps your function signatures versioned and lets you add, modify, or remove tools without deploying code changes.\\n \\n \\n```\\nfrom langfuse import get_client\\nfrom langfuse.openai import OpenAI\\nlangfuse = get_client()\\nclient = OpenAI()\\n///# Fetch prompt with config containing tools\\nprompt = langfuse.get_prompt(\\\"weather-agent\\\")\\nsystem_message = prompt.compile()\\n///# Extract parameters from config\\ncfg = prompt.config\\n///# Example config:\\n///# {\\n///# \\\"tools\\\": [\\n///# {\\n///# \\\"type\\\": \\\"function\\\",\\n///# \\\"function\\\": {\\n///# \\\"name\\\": \\\"get_current_weather\\\",\\n///# \\\"description\\\": \\\"Get the current weather in a given location\\\",\\n///# \\\"parameters\\\": {\\n///# \\\"type\\\": \\\"object\\\",\\n///# \\\"properties\\\": {\\n///# \\\"location\\\": { \\\"type\\\": \\\"string\\\", \\\"description\\\": \\\"City and country\\\" },\\n///# \\\"unit\\\": { \\\"type\\\": \\\"string\\\", \\\"enum\\\": [\\\"celsius\\\", \\\"fahrenheit\\\"] }\\n///# },\\n///# \\\"required\\\": [\\\"location\\\"],\\n///# \\\"additionalProperties\\\": false\\n///# }\\n///# }\\n///# }\\n///# ],\\n///# \\\"tool_choice\\\": { \\\"type\\\": \\\"auto\\\" }\\n///# }\\ntools = cfg.get(\\\"tools\\\", [])\\ntool_choice = cfg.get(\\\"tool_choice\\\")\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\nres = client.chat.completions.create(\\n model=\\\"gpt-4o\\\",\\n messages=[\\n {\\\"role\\\": \\\"system\\\", \\\"content\\\": system_message},\\n {\\\"role\\\": \\\"user\\\", \\\"content\\\": \\\"What's the weather in Berlin?\\\"},\\n ],\\n tools=tools,\\n tool_choice=tool_choice,\\n langfuse_prompt=prompt, ///# Links this generation to the prompt version in Langfuse\\n)\\n```\\nFor complete end-to-end examples, see the [OpenAI Functions cookbook](/guides/cookbook/prompt_management_openai_functions) and the [Structured Outputs docs](/integrations/model-providers/openai-py#structured-output).\\n* * *\\n* * *\\nLast edited 8/10/2026\\n\"}], \"type\": \"content\"}}, {\"type\": \"document\", \"record_type\": \"documentation\", \"url\": \"https://langfuse.com/docs/api-and-data-platform/features/query-via-sdk\", \"title\": \"Query Data via SDKs\", \"source\": {\"content\": [{\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"Query via SDKs - Langfuse\\n[Docs](/docs)\\n[API & Data Platform](/docs/api-and-data-platform/overview)\\n[Features](/docs/api-and-data-platform/features/agent-skill)\\n[Query via SDKs](/docs/api-and-data-platform/features/query-via-sdk)\\n# Query Data via SDKs\\nLangfuse is [open-source](/open-source) and data tracked with Langfuse is open. Use the Python and JS/TS SDKs to query the same public APIs without writing raw HTTP requests.\\nCommon use cases:\\n * Query row-level observations for evaluation pipelines, few-shot examples, or fine-tuning datasets.\\n * Query aggregate cost, usage, latency, volume, and score metrics for dashboards or billing workflows.\\n * Programmatically create [datasets](/docs/evaluation/features/datasets).\\nIf you are new to Langfuse, we recommend familiarizing yourself with the [Langfuse data model](/docs/tracing-data-model).\\nNew data is typically available for querying within 15-30 seconds of ingestion, though processing times may vary at times. Please visit [status.langfuse.com](https://status.langfuse.com) if you encounter any issues.\\n## SDKs\\nVia the [SDKs](/docs/sdk/overview) for Python and JS/TS you can easily query the API without having to write the HTTP requests yourself.\\nThe `api` namespace is auto-generated from the Public API (OpenAPI). Method names mirror REST resources and support filters and pagination.\\nFrom Python SDK v4 and JS/TS SDK v5 onward, the high-performance observations and metrics APIs are the defaults:\\n * `api.observations` (formerly `api.observations_v_2` / `api.observationsV2`)\\n * `api.metrics` (formerly `api.metrics_v_2` / `api.metricsV2`)\\nScores API v3 is available as `api.scores_v3` in Python SDK `4.8.1+` and `api.scoresV3` in JS/TS SDK `5.5.0+`. The `api.scores` v2 reads are deprecated; see [Migration of deprecated APIs](/faq/all/deprecated-api-migration#scores).\"}], \"type\": \"content\"}}, {\"type\": \"document\", \"record_type\": \"site\", \"url\": \"https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pTneXS_m1rk\", \"title\": \"Langfuse Intro - Observability & Tracing Deep Dive\", \"source\": {\"content\": [{\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"Title: \\\"Langfuse Intro - Observability & Tracing Deep Dive\\\"\\n\\nPublished on: August 26, 2025\\nUrl: \\\"www.youtube.com/watch?v=pTneXS_m1rk\\\"\\nDescription:\\n'''In this video our Co-Founder and CEO Marc walks you through the Observability and Tracing product of Langfuse.'''\\nTranscription:\"}], \"type\": \"content\"}}, {\"type\": \"document\", \"record_type\": \"site\", \"url\": \"https://langfuse.com/blog/product-analytics-for-LLM-apps\", \"title\": \"Launch YC - Langfuse Blog\", \"source\": {\"content\": [{\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"---\\n\\n[TypeScript SDK v4 GA →Langfuse TypeScript SDK v4 is here →](/changelog/2025-08-28-typescript-sdk-v4-ga)\\n\\n---\\n\\n[](https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse \\\"GitHub Repository\\\")\\n\\n---\\n\\nJul 19, 2023\\n# Langfuse — Open source product analytics for LLM applications\\nThis is a cross-post of our Launch YC (W23) which explains why we're building Langfuse.\\n\\n---\\n\\n[Clemens](https://twitter.com/rawert)\\n\\n---\\n\\n[Marc](https://twitter.com/marcklingen)\\n\\n---\\n\\n[Max](https://twitter.com/maxdeichmann)\\n\\n---\\n\\n_**TLDR:** Langfuse is building open source product analytics (think ‘Mixpanel’) for LLM apps. We help companies to track and analyze quality, cost and latency across product releases and use cases._\\n\\n---\\n\\nHi everyone,\\nwe’re Max, Marc and Clemens. We were part of the Winter 23 batch and work on Langfuse, where we help teams make sense of how their LLM applications perform.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## 🤯 Problem\\n\\n---\\n\\nLLMs represent a new paradigm in software. Single LLM calls are probabilistic and add substantial latency and cost. Applications use LLMs in new ways via advanced prompting, embedding-based retrieval, chains, and agents with tools. Teams building production-grade LLM applications have new **product analytics** and **monitoring** needs:\\n\\n---\\n\\n * **Quality of outputs** is difficult to measure. Outputs can e.g. be inaccurate, unhelpful, poorly formatted, hallucinated or error.\\n\\n---\\n\\n * **Cost of compute** is a priority again given high inference costs.\\n\\n---\\n\\n * **Latency of responses** matters for synchronous use cases.\\n\\n---\\n\\n * **Debugging is challenging** due to increasingly complex LLM applications (chains, agents, tool usage).\\n\\n---\\n\\n * **Understanding user behavior** is difficult given open-ended user prompts and conversational interactions.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## 🧠 Solution\\n\\n---\\n\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\nLangfuse derives actionable insights from production data. Our customers use Langfuse to answer questions such as: _“How helpful are my LLM app’s outputs? What is my LLM API spend by customer? What do latencies look like across geographies and steps of LLM chains? Did the quality of the application improve in newer versions? What was the impact of switching from zero-shotting GPT4 to using few-shotted Llama calls?”_\\n\\n---\\n\\n#### Metrics\\n\\n---\\n\\n * **Quality** is measured through user feedback, model-based scoring and human-in-the-loop scored samples. Quality is assessed over time as well as across prompt versions, LLMs and users.\\n * **Cost and Latency** are accurately measured and broken down by user, session, geography, feature, model and prompt version.\\n\\n---\\n\\n#### Insights\\n\\n---\\n\\n * Monitor quality/cost/latency **tradeoffs** by release to facilitate product and engineering decisions.\\n\\n---\\n\\n * **Cluster use cases** by employing a classifier to understand what users are doing.\\n\\n---\\n\\n * Break down **LLM usage by customer** for usage-based billing and profitability analysis.\\n\\n---\\n\\n#### Integrations\\n\\n---\\n\\n * [Python](/docs/sdk/python) and [Typescript](/docs/sdk/typescript/guide) SDKs to easily monitor complex LLM apps\\n * [Frontend SDK](/docs/sdk/typescript/guide) to directly capture feedback from users as a quality signal\\n\\n---\\n\\n_Langfuse can be self-hosted or used with a generous free tier in our managed cloud version._\\n\\n---\\n\\n## 🚧 Debugging UI\\n\\n---\\n\\nBased on the ingested data, Langfuse helps developers debug complex LLM apps in production:\\n\\n---\\n\\n * Inspect LLM app executions in a nested UI for chains, agents and tool usage.\\n * Segment by user feedback to find the root cause of quality problems.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## 🙏 Asks\\n\\n---\\n\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\n 1. Star us on [GitHub](https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse) \\\\+ follow along on [Twitter](https://twitter.com/langfuse) & [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/company/langfuse).\\n 2. If you run an LLM app, go ahead and reach out to us, we’d love to see how we can be helpful.\\n 3. Please forward Langfuse to teams building commercial LLM applications.\\n\\n---\\n\\n* * *\\n\\n---\\n\\n## References\\n\\n---\\n\\n 1. [Launch YC](https://www.ycombinator.com/launches/J2s-langfuse-open-source-product-analytics-for-llm-apps)\\n 2. [LinkedIn post](https://www.linkedin.com/feed/update/urn:li:activity:7087446200353783808/)\\n 3. [Twitter thread](https://twitter.com/MarcKlingen/status/1681687868534652928)\\n\\n---\\n\\n[](https://x.com/MarcKlingen/status/1681687868534652928)\\n\\n---\\n\\n[Marc Klingen](https://x.com/MarcKlingen/status/1681687868534652928)\\n[@MarcKlingen](https://x.com/MarcKlingen/status/1681687868534652928)\\n·[Follow](https://x.com/intent/follow?screen_name=MarcKlingen)\\n\\n---\\n\\n[](https://x.com/MarcKlingen/status/1681687868534652928)\\n\\n---\\n\\nProud to launch 🪢 [@langfuse](https://x.com/langfuse) today – open-source product analytics for LLM apps! We help teams building with LLMs turn production data into insight. Quick overview: 1/x\\n\\n---\\n\\n[](https://x.com/ycombinator/status/1681680585516027904)\\nY Combinator\\n@ycombinator\\n\\n---\\n\\nCongrats on the launch, @rawert, @marcklingen & @maxdeichmann! @Langfuse (YC W23) is building open-source product analytics for LLM apps, helping companies to track and analyze the quality, cost, and latency of LLMs, chains & agents in granular detail. ycombinator.com/launches/J2s-l…\\n\\n---\\n\\n[](https://x.com/ycombinator/status/1681680585516027904)\\n\\n---\\n\\n[11:30 AM · Jul 19, 2023](https://x.com/MarcKlingen/status/1681687868534652928)\"}], \"type\": \"content\"}}, {\"type\": \"document\", \"record_type\": \"site\", \"url\": \"https://langfuse.com/blog/2026-03-31-langfuse-march-update\", \"title\": \"Langfuse March Update - Langfuse\", \"source\": {\"content\": [{\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"---\\n\\n[🇯🇵 Langfuse Cloud Japan is live →🇯🇵 Langfuse Cloud Japan is live →](/japan)\\n\\n---\\n\\nCategories\\n\\n---\\n\\n[\\\\+ All [70]\\n](/blog)\\n\\n---\\n\\n[\\\\+ agents [3]\\n](/blog?tag=agents)\\n\\n---\\n\\n[\\\\+ announcement [8]\\n](/blog?tag=announcement)\\n\\n---\\n\\n[\\\\+ architecture [4]\\n](/blog?tag=architecture)\\n\\n---\\n\\n[\\\\+ engineering [11]\\n](/blog?tag=engineering)\\n\\n---\\n\\n[\\\\+ evaluation [4]\\n](/blog?tag=evaluation)\\n\\n---\\n\\n[\\\\+ example [2]\\n](/blog?tag=example)\\n\\n---\\n\\n[\\\\+ guide [20]\\n](/blog?tag=guide)\\n\\n---\\n\\n[\\\\+ integration [6]\\n](/blog?tag=integration)\\n\\n---\\n\\n[\\\\+ launchweek [4]\\n](/blog?tag=launchweek)\\n\\n---\\n\\n[\\\\+ update [19]\\n](/blog?tag=update)\\n\\n---\\n\\nReceive Updates\\nOne email per month with our latest ships and product announcements.\\nSubscribe\\n\\n---\\n\\nMarch 31, 2026\\n# Langfuse March Update\\nAgent Skill, Langfuse CLI, boolean and categorical LLM-as-a-Judge scores, Kiro integration, and more\\nMarc Klingen\\n\\n---\\n\\nThe past months we have been shipping a lot to make Langfuse much easier to use for your coding agents. If you are not using Langfuse through your coding agent yet, we strongly recommend giving it a spin!\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Agent Skill\\n\\n---\\n\\nThe [Langfuse Agent Skill](/docs/api-and-data-platform/features/agent-skill) helps coding agents to use Langfuse effectively. It follows the open [Agent Skills](https://github.com/anthropics/skills) standard and works with Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, and others.\\n\\n---\\n\\nInstall it in one line:\\n\\n---\\n\\n \\n \\n```\\nnpx skills add langfuse/skills --skill \\\"langfuse\\\"\\n```\\n\\n---\\n\\nOr just ask your coding agent to install it from `github.com/langfuse/skills`.\\n\\n---\\n\\nOnce installed, your agent can query traces, create datasets, update prompts, migrate hardcoded prompts to Langfuse Prompt Management, and set up observability — all without leaving your editor. Even if you are already successfully using Langfuse, the Skill can help you improve your workflows and instrumentation.\\n## Langfuse CLI\\n\\n---\\n\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\nThe skill uses the [Langfuse CLI](/docs/api-and-data-platform/features/cli) under the hood. It wraps the entire Langfuse API, auto-generated from our OpenAPI spec so it's always in sync. Every endpoint becomes a CLI command: traces, prompts, datasets, scores, sessions, metrics, and more.\\n\\n---\\n\\nBuilt for agents, but useful for humans too. Script your workflows, automate batch-scoring, or sync prompts across environments in CI/CD.\\n→ [npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/langfuse-cli)\\n## Further reading\\nHere are some pointers for what to do with the Skill and CLI:\\n\\n---\\n\\n * **Getting started with all Langfuse features.** Using the Skill it is incredibly easy to get started using more of the Langfuse platform. Just ask your agent that you would like to test a certain feature and it can propose useful first use cases and start implementing them.\\n * **Automatic prompt improvement.** Annotate a few traces in Langfuse, then let an agent fetch your feedback, analyze patterns, and propose prompt changes. A fast loop from rough to robust. → [Read the guide](/blog/2026-02-16-prompt-improvement-claude-skills)\\n\\n---\\n\\nWe have also learned a lot about building efficient Skills:\\n\\n---\\n\\n * **Evaluating skill quality.** We used Langfuse datasets, tracing, and the Claude Agent SDK to systematically test and improve the Skill itself. Small details matter: a single comment saying \\\"optional\\\" instead of \\\"mandatory\\\" caused consistent agent failures. → [Blog post](/blog/2026-02-26-evaluate-ai-agent-skills)\\n * **Optimizing skills with Autoresearch.** We ran Karpathy's autoresearch on our prompt migration skill. Score went from 0.35 to 0.82. Not all changes were keepers, but the process surfaced failure modes we'd never have found manually. → [Blog post](/blog/2026-03-24-optimizing-ai-skill-with-autoresearch)\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Fixes & improvements\\n\\n---\\n\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\n * Feat: [Boolean Scores in LLM-as-a-Judge](/changelog/2026-04-08-boolean-llm-as-a-judge-scores)\\n\\n---\\n\\n * Feat: [Categorical \"document\", \"record_type\": \"github_discussion\", \"url\": \"https://github.com/orgs/langfuse/discussions/11610\", \"title\": \"How can I use LangFuse to visualize and analyze the trace data like PowerBI (stack bar charts, slicers, etc)\", \"source\": {\"content\": [{\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"Title: How can I use LangFuse to visualize and analyze the trace data like PowerBI (stack bar charts, slicers, etc)\\nCategory: Support\\nAuthor: @Sourav-xd\\nTimestamp: January 19, 2026\\nBody:\\n### Describe your question\\n\\nHow can Langfuse be used to visualize and analyze trace data in a BI-like way, similar to Power BI? Is it possible to create advanced visualizations such as stacked or grouped bar charts using two dimensions (e.g. model × environment, status × time) within a single vertical bar chart? Additionally, are there plans or best practices for applying interactive slicers or global filters (model, environment, metadata, time range, etc.) to dynamically explore trace data across all dashboard visualizations?\\n\\n### Langfuse Cloud or Self-Hosted?\\n\\nSelf-Hosted\\n\\n### If Self-Hosted\\n\\nNew minor version: v3.147.0\\n\\n### If Langfuse Cloud\\n\\n_No response_\\n\\n### SDK and integration versions\\n\\n_No response_\\n\\n### Pre-Submission Checklist\\n\\n- [X] I have checked for existing issues/discussions and consulted Langfuse AI.\\nComments:\\n\\n Comment #1 from @inkeep-ai-assistant on January 19, 2026:\\n\\n \\n\\n Langfuse provides customizable dashboards for visualizing and analyzing trace data directly within the UI[(1)](https://langfuse.com/docs/metrics/features/custom-dashboards). You can create personalized views to track metrics like latency, cost, quality monitoring, and user behavior[(1)](https://langfuse.com/docs/metrics/features/custom-dashboards).\\n\\n## Current Visualization Capabilities\\n\\nLangfuse custom dashboards support multiple chart types including line charts, bar charts, time series, and pie charts[(1)](https://langfuse.com/docs/metrics/features/custom-dashboards). You can create widgets that:\\n\\n- Choose from traces, observations, or evaluation scores as data sources[(1)](https://langfuse.com/docs/metrics/features/custom-dashboards)\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\n- Select metrics to measure (count, latency, cost, scores, etc.)[(1)](https://langfuse.com/docs/metrics/features/custom-dashboards)\\n- Group by dimensions like user, model, time, trace name[(1)](https://langfuse.com/docs/metrics/features/custom-dashboards)\\n- Apply filters to narrow down specific data subsets[(1)](https://langfuse.com/docs/metrics/features/custom-dashboards)\\n\\nThe dashboards support advanced filtering including metadata filters, time-based filters, user properties, model parameters, tags and labels, and score thresholds[(1)](https://langfuse.com/docs/metrics/features/custom-dashboards).\\n\\n## Current Limitations for BI-Like Features\\n\\nBased on the available sources, there are some limitations compared to full BI tools:\\n\\n**Stacked/Grouped Bar Charts**: The documentation mentions bar charts as an available chart type for comparing values across categories[(1)](https://langfuse.com/docs/metrics/features/custom-dashboards), but does not explicitly describe stacked or grouped bar charts with multiple dimensions within a single visualization.\\n\\n**Metadata as Dimensions**: Currently, custom metadata fields cannot be directly selected as dimensions in dashboard widgets[(2)](https://github.com/orgs/langfuse/discussions/7577). This is a known limitation - the feature was initially planned but cut due to complexity in using metadata at scale in dashboards[(2)](https://github.com/orgs/langfuse/discussions/7577).\\n\\n**Interactive Slicers**: The documentation does not describe global filters or interactive slicers that apply across all dashboard visualizations simultaneously.\\n\\n## Alternative Approaches\\n\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\nFor more advanced BI-style analysis, Langfuse provides programmatic access via the Metrics API[(1)](https://langfuse.com/docs/metrics/features/custom-dashboards), which allows you to export dashboard data for integration with external analytics tools[(1)](https://langfuse.com/docs/metrics/features/custom-dashboards). This would enable you to use Power BI or similar tools for advanced visualizations while leveraging Langfuse's data collection and query engine[(3)](https://langfuse.com/blog/2025-05-21-customizable-dashboards).\\n\\n📚 **Sources:**\\n1. [Custom Dashboards](https://langfuse.com/docs/metrics/features/custom-dashboards)\\n2. [Custom Metadata Field as Dimension in Dashboard Widgets](https://github.com/orgs/langfuse/discussions/7577)\\n3. [How we Built Scalable & Customizable Dashboards - Langfuse Blog](https://langfuse.com/blog/2025-05-21-customizable-dashboards)\\n\\n---\\n\\nHave another question? Just tag [@inkeep](https://inkeep.com).\\n\\n Replies to comment #1:\\n\\n Reply #1 to comment #1 from inkeep-ai-assistant on January 19, 2026:\\n\\n Hi @Sourav-xd, inkeep is correct. For use cases not supported in Langfuse yet, you can use the metrics API: https://langfuse.com/docs/metrics/features/custom-dashboards\\n\"}], \"type\": \"content\"}}, {\"type\": \"document\", \"record_type\": \"github_issue\", \"url\": \"https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse/issues/14037\", \"title\": \"Feature request: model transparency fields for OpenAI-compatible gateway traces\", \"source\": {\"content\": [{\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"Github Issue by @UPmeme created on June 04, 2026. The current state of the issue is: closed\\n\\n## Summary\\n\\nFor OpenAI-compatible gateway/proxy setups, it would be useful if Langfuse made model transparency fields easier to capture and query in traces/observations.\\n\\nThis is not meant as guaranteed model identity verification. The goal is to help users audit routing behavior, provider alias drift, usage mismatches, and missing upstream metadata when requests pass through an LLM gateway.\\n\\n## Context\\n\\nWhen applications use an OpenAI-compatible gateway, there can be multiple model identifiers involved:\\n\\n- the model requested by the application\\n- the provider/model resolved by the gateway\\n- the `model` field returned by the upstream provider\\n- model aliases or routing rules applied by the gateway\\n- provider-specific metadata such as `system_fingerprint`, request IDs, or usage fields\\n\\nWhen these values differ or are missing, it is useful to preserve that distinction in observability data.\\n\\n## Suggested fields\\n\\nPossible fields that would help with gateway transparency:\\n\\n- `requested_model`: model value sent by the client/application\\n- `gateway_model` or `resolved_model`: provider/model selected by the gateway after routing/alias resolution\\n- `response_model`: upstream response `model` field, when present\\n- `gateway_base_url` or a redacted provider/gateway identifier\\n- `usage_source`: upstream, estimated, unavailable, or unknown\\n- `system_fingerprint`: when provided by upstream\\n- `model_mismatch`: boolean or enum when requested/resolved/returned model names differ\\n\\nExample mismatch categories:\\n\\n- `requested_vs_resolved_mismatch`\\n- `resolved_vs_response_mismatch`\\n- `response_model_missing`\\n- `usage_missing`\\n- `system_fingerprint_missing`\\n\\n## Why this would help\\n\\nThis would make it easier to answer questions such as:\\n\\n- Did a gateway route my request to the model/provider I expected?\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\n- Did the upstream provider return a different model field?\\n- Are token usage and cost calculations based on upstream values or estimates?\\n- Did a provider alias or gateway rule change affect observed cost/latency/quality?\\n- Can I share a redacted trace for debugging without leaking prompts or tokens?\\n\\nIt would also help downstream audit tools compare gateway traces without having to rely on provider-specific metadata conventions.\\n\\n## Suggested framing\\n\\nThese fields should be treated as observability/audit metadata, not as a security verdict. A black-box API cannot fully prove which model generated a response, but structured transparency fields can still catch configuration mistakes, silent provider changes, and suspicious gateway behavior.\\n\\nIf Langfuse already has a recommended way to represent these fields through metadata, a documentation pointer or small guide for OpenAI-compatible gateways would be helpful.\\n---\\nComment #1 by @HerShin5:\\n\\nThis would be especially useful if Langfuse treated gateway metadata as a first-class trace concern but still kept it provider-neutral.\\n\\nA few fields I’d want to preserve from real OpenAI-compatible gateway traffic:\\n\\n- `requested_base_url` / redacted gateway id, separate from the upstream provider id. Otherwise it’s hard to debug whether the app bypassed the gateway or the gateway routed unexpectedly.\\n- `requested_model`, `resolved_model`, and `response_model` as separate values, exactly as you outlined. I’d also keep a normalized `routing_reason` when available (`explicit`, `alias`, `fallback`, `rate_limit_fallback`, `cost_policy`, etc.).\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\n- `usage_source` plus `pricing_source`: upstream usage can be authoritative while pricing is gateway-estimated, or vice versa.\\n- `fallback_chain`: even a compact array of attempted provider/model ids + status codes would make rate-limit/cost debugging much easier.\\n- A redaction contract for exported traces: endpoint label and request ids are useful, raw API keys / full internal upstream URLs are not.\\n\\nI’d frame this as an observability primitive rather than model verification. It catches the practical failures teams see in production: silent alias changes, fallback to a more expensive model, missing usage fields, and clients accidentally using the wrong base URL.\\n\\nDisclosure: I’m associated with/evaluating KiroForge as an OpenAI-compatible gateway, and these are exactly the fields I’d want visible when comparing gateway-routed traces against direct-provider traces.\\n\\n---\\nComment #2 by @jannikmaierhoefer:\\n\\nHi @UPmeme, please post feature requests here: https://github.com/orgs/langfuse/discussions/categories/ideas\\n\\n\"}], \"type\": \"content\"}}, {\"type\": \"document\", \"record_type\": \"github_issue\", \"url\": \"https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse/issues/8678\", \"title\": \"无法直接通过api获取到测试集的平均分数\", \"source\": {\"content\": [{\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"Github Issue by @l19930105 created on August 22, 2025. The current state of the issue is: closed\\n\\n### Describe the bug\\n\\n I can't get it to work. https://api.reference.langfuse.com/#tag/scorev2/get/api/public/v2/scores doesn't seem to take datasetRunId parameter.\\n\\nI tried this query: f\\\"{LANGFUSE_HOST}/api/public/v2/scores​?datasetRunId=cmdhxi2qv0a3b0u072a9735yz\\\"\\nand get 404\\n\\nAlso it seems like the datasetRunId is only set for scores that are run level. I need a way to get all trace level scores for a specific run. Trace level scores seem to have datasetRunId = None.\\n\\n### Steps to reproduce\\n\\n1\\n\\n### Langfuse Cloud or self-hosted?\\n\\nLangfuse Cloud\\n\\n### If self-hosted, what version are you running?\\n\\n_No response_\\n\\n### SDK and integration versions\\n\\n_No response_\\n\\n### Additional information\\n\\n_No response_\\n\\n### Are you interested in contributing a fix for this bug?\\n\\nNo\\n---\\nComment #1 by @dosubot[bot]:\\n\\n<!-- Answer -->\\n目前 /api/public/v2/scores 并不支持用 datasetRunId 参数直接获取某个测试集（dataset run）下所有 trace-level 的分数，这也是你遇到 404 的原因。trace-level 的 score 没有直接的 datasetRunId 字段，只有 run-level 的 score 才有这个字段，trace-level 的分数只能通过 traceId 关联到 dataset run（间接关联）[代码实现细节](https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse/blob/27d43a7a29f3799f354aabd16881f679e98a910c/web/src/pages/api/public/v2/scores/index.ts)。\\n\\n要获取某个 dataset run 下所有 trace-level 的分数，可以这样操作：\\n\\n1. 通过 API 获取该 dataset run 下的所有 dataset run items（每个 item 都有 traceId）[API 文档](https://langfuse.com/docs/datasets)。\\n2. 用这些 traceId 再去批量查询每个 trace 的 score（trace-level）。\\n3. 在客户端自行聚合这些分数，计算平均值。\\n\\n目前后端已经有 join 查询（getTraceScoresForDatasetRuns）可以一次性拿到所有 trace-level 分数并带上 datasetRunId，但这个功能还没有直接暴露到 public API，只在内部用于聚合和展示[相关 PR](https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse/pull/8207)。\\n\\n所以目前只能用上述 workaround。如果你用 SDK，可以先 fetch dataset run items，再批量 fetch trace scores，然后聚合。\\n\\n相关讨论和实现细节可以参考：\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\n- [API 不支持 datasetRunId 查询 trace-level scores](https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse/blob/27d43a7a29f3799f354aabd16881f679e98a910c/web/src/pages/api/public/v2/scores/index.ts)\\n- [如何通过 dataset run items 间接获取 trace-level scores](https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse/pull/8179)\\n- [后端 join 查询 trace-level scores 的实现](https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse/pull/8207)\\n\\n如需代码示例或 SDK #2 by @l19930105:\\n\\n目前后端已经有 join 查询（getTraceScoresForDatasetRuns）可以一次性拿到所有 trace-level 分数并带上 datasetRunId，但这个功能还没有直接暴露到 public API，只在内部用于聚合和展示https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse/pull/8207。\\n那什么时候可以暴露到 public API，让我们可以用 datasetRunId 参数直接获取某个测试集（dataset run）下所有 trace-level 的分数\\n---\\nComment #3 by inactive for 14 days since being marked as stale. Please reopen if the issue persists.\\n\\n\"}], \"type\": \"content\"}}, {\"type\": \"document\", \"record_type\": \"documentation\", \"url\": \"https://langfuse.com/docs/observability/features/environments\", \"title\": \"Environments\", \"source\": {\"content\": [{\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"Environments - Langfuse\\n[Docs](/docs)\\n[Observability](/docs/observability/overview)\\n[Features](/docs/observability/features/sessions)\\n[Environments](/docs/observability/features/environments)\\n# Environments\\nEnvironments allow you to organize your traces, observations, and scores from different contexts such as production, staging, or development. This helps you:\\n * Keep your development and production data separate while using the same project\\n * Filter and analyze data by environment\\n * Reuse datasets and prompts across environments\\n## Filtering\\nIn the Langfuse UI, you can filter events by environment using the environment filter in the navigation bar. This filter applies across all views in Langfuse.\\nSee our [API Reference](/docs/api) for details on how to filter by environment on our API.\\n## Managing Environments\\nEnvironments are created the first time data is ingested with a given `environment` value and are persistent. They cannot currently be deleted or renamed via the UI.\\nFor guidance on how to structure, separate, and work with multiple environments across projects and stages, see the FAQ: [Managing different environments](/faq/all/managing-different-environments).\\n## Configure environments\\nYou can configure the environment by setting the `LANGFUSE_TRACING_ENVIRONMENT` environment variable (recommended) or by using the `environment` parameter in the client initialization. If both are specified, the initialization parameter takes precedence. If nothing is specified, the default environment is `default`.\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\nIn the Python SDK, you can also set the environment for a specific trace scope with `propagate_attributes(environment=\\\"...\\\")`. This is useful when the environment belongs to the incoming request rather than to the service process itself, for example when one shared LLM proxy handles requests from development, staging, QA, and production. Use `as_baggage=True` to propagate that environment across service boundaries.\\n### Naming constraints\\nThe environment must be a string that follows this regex pattern: `^(?!langfuse)\\n[a-z0-9-_]+$` with at most 40 characters.\\nThis means:\\n * Cannot start with \\\"langfuse\\\"\\n * Can only contain lowercase letters, numbers, hyphens, and underscores\\n### Data Model\\nThe `environment` attribute is available on all events in Langfuse:\\n * Traces\\n * Observations (spans, events, generations)\\n * Scores\\n * Sessions\\nSee [Data Model](/docs/observability/data-model) for more details.\\nPython SDKJS/TS SDKOpenTelemetryOpenAI (Python)OpenAI (JS/TS)Langchain (Python)Langchain (JS/TS)Vercel AI SDK (JS/TS)\\n \\n \\n```\\nfrom langfuse import get_client, observe, propagate_attributes\\nimport os\\n///# Set the environment variable\\n///# Alternatively, set via .env file and load via dotenv\\nos.environ[\\\"LANGFUSE_TRACING_ENVIRONMENT\\\"] = \\\"production\\\"\\n///# Get the client (will use environment variable)\\nlangfuse = get_client()\\n///# All operations will now be associated with the \\\"production\\\" environment\\nwith langfuse.start_as_current_observation(as_type=\\\"span\\\", name=\\\"my-operation\\\") as span:\\n # Your code here\\n pass\\n@observe\\ndef main():\\n return \\\"Hello\\\"\\nmain()\\n///# For request-scoped environments, propagate the environment explicitly.\\n///# This maps to the first-class langfuse.environment field.\\nwith langfuse.start_as_current_observation(as_type=\\\"span\\\", name=\\\"proxy-request\\\"):\\n with propagate_attributes(environment=\\\"staging\\\"):\\n # All child observations created here are associated with staging.\\n pass\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\n```\\nSet the Langfuse Environment via environment variable:\\n \\n \\n```\\nexport LANGFUSE_TRACING_ENVIRONMENT=production\\n```\\nWhen using [OpenTelemetry](/docs/opentelemetry/get-started), you can set the environment using any of these attributes:\\n * `langfuse.environment`\\n * `deployment.environment.name`\\n * `deployment.environment`\\nTo set an environment property globally, you can use resource attributes: `os.environ[\\\"OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES\\\"] = \\\"langfuse.environment=staging\\\"`.\\nAlternatively, you can set the environment on a per-span basis:\\n \\n \\n```\\nfrom opentelemetry import trace\\nfrom opentelemetry.trace import Status, StatusCode\\ntracer = trace.get_tracer(__name__)\\nwith tracer.start_as_current_observation(\\\"my-operation\\\") as span:\\n # Set environment using Langfuse-specific attribute\\n span.set_attribute(\\\"langfuse.environment\\\", \\\"staging\\\")\\n # Or using OpenTelemetry convention\\n span.set_attribute(\\\"deployment.environment.name\\\", \\\"staging\\\")\\n```\\nWhen using the **Python SDK** , the environment provided on client initialization will apply to all event inputs and outputs regardless of the Langfuse-maintained integration you are using.\\nSee the Python SDK tab for more details.\\nWhen using the [OpenAI SDK Integration](/integrations/model-providers/openai-py)\\n \\n \\n```\\nfrom langfuse import Langfuse\\nfrom langfuse.openai import openai\\n///# Either set the environment variable or configure the Langfuse client\\nos.environ[\\\"LANGFUSE_TRACING_ENVIRONMENT\\\"] = \\\"production\\\"\\nlangfuse = Langfuse(environment=\\\"production\\\")\\n///# the integration will use the instantiated client under the hood\\ncompletion = openai.chat.completions.create(\\n model=\\\"gpt-3.5-turbo\\\",\\n messages=[\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\n {\\\"role\\\": \\\"system\\\", \\\"content\\\": \\\"You are a calculator.\\\"},\\n {\\\"role\\\": \\\"user\\\", \\\"content\\\": \\\"1 + 1 = \\\"}],\\n)\\n```\\n.env\\n \\n \\n```\\nLANGFUSE_TRACING_ENVIRONMENT=production\\n```\\n \\n \\n```\\nimport OpenAI from \\\"openai\\\";\\nimport { observeOpenAI } from Optionally, create a deep link to this view in your systems.\\nLLM agents can be visualized as a graph to illustrate the flow of complex agentic workflows.\\nSee quality, cost, and latency metrics in the dashboard to monitor your LLM application.\\nGet notified over Slack, GitHub Actions, or Webhooks when a metric crosses a threshold with [alerts](/docs/observability/features/alerts).\\n## Prompt Management\\n[Prompt Management](/docs/prompt-management/overview) is critical in building effective AI applications. You can customize and self-host it. You can trust for it to be around for the long-haul.\\n 2. **Platform Agnostic** : Langfuse works seamlessly with any model and [integrates](/integrations) with frameworks like Llama Index and LangChain.\\n 3. **Detailed Metrics** : Langfuse provides in-depth [insights and metrics](/docs/metrics/overview) to improve your LLM applications.\\n 4. **Real-time Monitoring and Evals** : Langfuse enables real-time monitoring and [evaluation](/docs/evaluation/overview) to keep track of your models' performance.\\n 5. **Flexible Deployment** : Whether [on-premise](/self-hosting) or in the cloud, Langfuse adapts to your deployment needs.\\n 6. **Scalable** : Built to scale with your projects, Langfuse handles projects of all sizes: from small to enterprise-level needs.\\n 7. **Compliance Ready** : Langfuse is ISO27001 and SOC2 Type 2 certified, GDPR compliant, and offers a HIPAA-ready region. Learn more in our [Security Center](/security).\\n 8. **Customizable Dashboards** : Langfuse lets you create dashboards that suit your requirements.\\n 9. **Easy Integration** : Langfuse is simple to integrate to your existing applications through its large number of [integrations](/integrations).\\n 10. **Community Support** : You will benefit from Langfuse's supportive [open-source community](/support) and continuous updates.\\n* * *\\n* * *\\nLast edited 7/7/2026\\n\"}], \"type\": \"content\"}}]}"}

Langfuse is an open‑source AI engineering platform to debug, analyze, and iterate on LLM/agent apps.

What you can use it for

  • Observability & tracing: Capture end‑to‑end traces of LLM calls, tool/retrieval steps, token/cost/latency; inspect timelines, sessions, users, and agent graphs
    • Docs: https://langfuse.com/docs/observability/overview
    • Get started: https://langfuse.com/docs/observability/get-started
  • Monitoring & analytics: Build custom dashboards and set alerts for quality, cost, latency, volume
    • Dashboards: https://langfuse.com/docs/metrics/features/custom-dashboards
    • Alerts: https://langfuse.com/docs/observability/features/alerts
  • Prompt management: Version, label/deploy prompts, attach JSON config (model, schema, tools), test in playground, link prompts to traces
    • Overview: https://langfuse.com/docs/prompt-management/overview
    • Config: https://langfuse.com/docs/prompt-management/features/config
  • Evaluation: LLM‑as‑a‑judge, code/custom evaluators, user feedback, datasets, and experiments for systematic testing in dev and production
    • Overview: https://langfuse.com/docs/evaluation/overview
    • Datasets/experiments: https://langfuse.com/docs/evaluation/features/datasets
  • Cost/latency/user analytics: Track per‑user usage, sessions, environments; analyze trade‑offs over time and by release
    • Users: https://langfuse.com/docs/observability/features/users
    • Environments: https://langfuse.com/docs/observability/features/environments
  • API & data access: Query observations/metrics via SDKs/CLI for pipelines, billing, or external BI
    • SDK querying: https://langfuse.com/docs/api-and-data-platform/features/query-via-sdk
    • CLI: https://langfuse.com/docs/api-and-data-platform/features/cli
  • Integrations & ingest: Python/JS SDKs, OpenTelemetry, 100+ frameworks/providers, and LLM gateways
    • Overview: https://langfuse.com/docs
    • Integrations list: https://langfuse.com/llms-integrations.txt
  • Self‑hosting & enterprise: Open source, self‑hostable, RBAC/SSO/SCIM, export to blob storage
    • Self‑hosting: https://langfuse.com/llms-self-hosting.txt

Quick start

  • Create a free account and explore the example project: https://langfuse.com/cloud
  • Full platform overview: https://langfuse.com/docs

Follow-up: Do you want to focus on tracing, prompt management, or evaluation first so I can point you to the exact quickstart and a minimal code snippet?

Input

My backend logic is C#, can I use all the features of langfuse?

Output

Short answer: Yes. While there’s no native C# SDK, you can use all Langfuse features from .NET via:

  • Tracing/observability: send OpenTelemetry spans to Langfuse’s OTLP/HTTP endpoint
  • Prompt management: use the Public API to create/fetch prompts
  • Evaluations/scores: use the Scores API
  • Dashboards, alerts, datasets/experiments, users/sessions, etc.: work regardless of your backend language

Docs

  • OpenTelemetry to Langfuse (endpoint, attribute mapping): https://langfuse.com/integrations/native/opentelemetry
  • Use Langfuse from Go/Java/C#/Ruby via OTEL: https://langfuse.com/resources/engineering/opentelemetry-languages
  • Prompt API: https://api.reference.langfuse.com#tag/prompts
  • Scores via API/SDK: https://langfuse.com/docs/evaluation/evaluation-methods/scores-via-sdk
  • Scores API (read v3): https://langfuse.com/docs/api-and-data-platform/features/scores-api
  • OTEL v4 ingestion checklist: https://langfuse.com/integrations/native/opentelemetry/migration-to-v4

Minimal C# examples

  1. Tracing with OpenTelemetry (HTTP/protobuf) to Langfuse
  • Endpoint: https://{region}.cloud.langfuse.com/api/public/otel/v1/traces
  • Auth: Basic (PUBLIC_KEY:SECRET_KEY)
  • Headers: x-langfuse-ingestion-version: 4

using System; using System.Diagnostics; using System.Net.Http; using System.Text; using OpenTelemetry; using OpenTelemetry.Exporter; using OpenTelemetry.Resources; using OpenTelemetry.Trace;

var publicKey = Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable("LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY"); var secretKey = Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable("LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY"); var baseUrl = Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable("LANGFUSE_BASE_URL") ?? "https://us.cloud.langfuse.com"; var otlpEndpoint = $"{baseUrl}/api/public/otel/v1/traces"; var basicAuth = Convert.ToBase64String(Encoding.UTF8.GetBytes($"{publicKey}:{secretKey}"));

{"type": "text", "text": "{\"content\": [{\"type\": \"document\", \"record_type\": \"documentation\", \"url\": \"https://langfuse.com/docs/prompt-management/features/config\", \"title\": \"Prompt Config\", \"source\": {\"content\": [{\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\n name: \\\"invoice-extractor\\\",\\n type: \\\"chat\\\",\\n prompt: [\\n { role: \\\"system\\\", content: \\\"Extract structured data from invoices.\\\" }\\n ],\\n config: config\\n});\\n```\\nYou can test your prompt with its config directly in the [Playground](/docs/prompt-management/features/playground).\\n## Using the config\\nThe example below retrieves the AI model and temperature from the prompt config.\\nAfter fetching a prompt, access the config via the `config` property and pass the values to your LLM call.\\nPython SDKJS/TS SDK\\nThis example uses the [Langfuse OpenAI integration](/docs/integrations/openai/python/get-started) for tracing, but this is optional. You can use any method to call your LLM (e.g., OpenAI SDK directly, other providers, etc.).\\n \\n \\n```\\nfrom langfuse import get_client\\n///# Initialize Langfuse OpenAI client for this example.\\nfrom langfuse.openai import OpenAI\\nclient = OpenAI()\\nlangfuse = get_client()\\n///# Fetch prompt\\nprompt = langfuse.get_prompt(\\\"invoice-extractor\\\")\\n///# Access config values\\ncfg = prompt.config\\nmodel = cfg.get(\\\"model\\\")\\ntemperature = cfg.get(\\\"temperature\\\")\\n///# Use in your LLM call\\nclient.chat.completions.create(\\n model=model,\\n temperature=temperature,\\n messages=prompt.prompt\\n)\\n```\\nThis example uses the [Langfuse OpenAI integration](/docs/integrations/openai/js/get-started) for tracing, but this is optional. You can use any method to call your LLM (e.g., OpenAI SDK directly, other providers, etc.) and still use the config.\\n \\n \\n```\\nimport { LangfuseClient } from \\\"@langfuse/client\\\";\\n// Initialize OpenAI client for this example.\\nimport OpenAI from \\\"openai\\\";\\nimport { observeOpenAI } from \\\"@langfuse/openai\\\";\\nconst client = observeOpenAI(new OpenAI());\\nconst langfuse = new LangfuseClient();\"}], \"type\": \"content\"}}, {\"type\": \"document\", \"record_type\": \"documentation\", \"url\": \"https://langfuse.com/docs/glossary\", \"title\": \"Glossary\", \"source\": {\"content\": [{\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\nAn API key configuration that allows Langfuse to call LLM models in the Playground or for LLM-as-a-Judge evaluations. Supports providers like OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google.\\nRelated:Playground·LLM-as-a-Judge\\n### [LLM-as-a-Judge](/docs/evaluation/evaluation-methods/llm-as-a-judge)\\nEvaluation\\nAn evaluation method that uses an LLM to score the output of your application based on custom criteria. Provides scalable, repeatable evaluations with chain-of-thought reasoning.\\nRelated:Score·Evaluator·Online Evaluation·Offline Evaluation\\n### [Log View](/docs/observability/overview)\\nObservability\\nShows all observations concatenated. Great for quickly scanning through them.\\nRelated:Agent Graph\\n## M\\n### [MCP Server](/docs/api-and-data-platform/features/mcp-server)\\nPlatform\\nA Model Context Protocol server that enables AI-powered tools to interact with Langfuse data. Used for advanced integrations and AI-assisted workflows.\\nRelated:Public API·SDK·Langfuse CLI\\n### [Metrics API](/docs/metrics/features/metrics-api)\\nAPI\\nAn API endpoint for retrieving customized analytics from Langfuse data. Allows specifying dimensions, metrics, filters, and time granularity to build custom reports and dashboards for LLM applications.\\nRelated:Custom Dashboards·Public API·Token\\n### [Model Definition](/docs/observability/features/token-and-cost-tracking)\\nObservability\\nA configuration that stores pricing information for an LLM model. Model definitions specify the cost per input and output token, enabling Langfuse to automatically calculate the price of generations based on token usage.\\nRelated:Token·Generation·Custom Dashboards\\n## O\\n### [Observation](/docs/observability/data-model)\\nObservability\"}], \"type\": \"content\"}}, {\"type\": \"document\", \"record_type\": \"site\", \"url\": \"https://langfuse.com/changelog/2024-09-23-github-discussion-across-documentation\", \"title\": \"Documentation now integrates with GitHub Discussions (Support and Feature Requests) - Langfuse\", \"source\": {\"content\": [{\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\n[Custom Dashboard Widget: Group by custom_score metadata property](https://github.com/orgs/langfuse/discussions/9043 \\\"Langfuse Support: Custom Dashboard Widget: Group by custom_score metadata property\\\")\\n[inverted prompt Composition](https://github.com/orgs/langfuse/discussions/9041 \\\"Langfuse Support: inverted prompt Composition\\\")\\n[Support login when Keycloak/LDAP users have no valid email](https://github.com/orgs/langfuse/discussions/9036 \\\"Langfuse Support: Support login when Keycloak/LDAP users have no valid email\\\")\\n[Input Output shown not support Thai language](https://github.com/orgs/langfuse/discussions/9032 \\\"Langfuse Support: Input Output shown not support Thai language\\\")\\n[Langfuse was not capturing some of api calls.](https://github.com/orgs/langfuse/discussions/9029 \\\"Langfuse Support: Langfuse was not capturing some of api calls.\\\")\\n[Langfuse dashboard links with filters](https://github.com/orgs/langfuse/discussions/9023 \\\"Langfuse Support: Langfuse dashboard links with filters\\\")\\n[Backup of prompt table when self-hosting Langfuse](https://github.com/orgs/langfuse/discussions/9019 \\\"Langfuse Support: Backup of prompt table when self-hosting Langfuse\\\")\\n[Invalid remote run URL:Blocked IP address detected:10.11.12.250](https://github.com/orgs/langfuse/discussions/9016 \\\"Langfuse Support: Invalid remote run URL:Blocked IP address detected:10.11.12.250\\\")\\n[Unable to create Project API key even with Org Owner access](https://github.com/orgs/langfuse/discussions/9014 \\\"Langfuse Support: Unable to create Project API key even with Org Owner access\\\")\\n[Debug mode with typescript](https://github.com/orgs/langfuse/discussions/9013 \\\"Langfuse Support: Debug mode with typescript\\\")\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\n[API - /scores not respecting value when operator '='](https://github.com/orgs/langfuse/discussions/8770 \\\"Langfuse Support: API - /scores not respecting value when operator '='\\\")\\n[Langfuse v3 get all prompts](https://github.com/orgs/langfuse/discussions/8761 \\\"Langfuse Support: Langfuse v3 get all prompts\\\")\\n[Is it possible to map price per minute? Or just per token?](https://github.com/orgs/langfuse/discussions/8757 \\\"Langfuse Support: Is it possible to map price per minute? Or just per token?\\\")\\n[Langfuse Selfhosted Deployment containers sequence](https://github.com/orgs/langfuse/discussions/8748 \\\"Langfuse Support: Langfuse Selfhosted Deployment containers sequence\\\")\\n[How to merge multiple traces from client-side tool calls into a single trace](https://github.com/orgs/langfuse/discussions/8743 \\\"Langfuse Support: How to merge multiple traces from client-side tool calls into a single trace\\\")\\n[How to configure rolebased access control using Azure SSO on Self-hosted](https://github.com/orgs/langfuse/discussions/8740 \\\"Langfuse Support: How to configure rolebased access control using Azure SSO on Self-hosted\\\")\\n[How to configure Langfuse python client with CF-Access-Client-Id and CF-Access-Client-Secret headers for Langfuse running under Cloudflare?](https://github.com/orgs/langfuse/discussions/8723 \\\"Langfuse Support: How to configure Langfuse python client with CF-Access-Client-Id and CF-Access-Client-Secret headers for Langfuse running under Cloudflare?\\\")\\n[Only ~93% of the traces are being collected](https://github.com/orgs/langfuse/discussions/8721 \\\"Langfuse Support: Only ~93% of the traces are being collected\\\")\\n[langfuse-web pod failing with prisma migration failure](https://github.com/orgs/langfuse/discussions/8717 \\\"Langfuse Support: langfuse-web pod failing with prisma migration failure\\\")\"}], \"type\": \"content\"}}, {\"type\": \"document\", \"record_type\": \"documentation\", \"url\": \"https://langfuse.com/docs/prompt-management/features/link-to-traces\", \"title\": \"Link Prompts to Traces\", \"source\": {\"content\": [{\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"Link to Traces - Langfuse\\n[Docs](/docs)\\n[Prompt Management](/docs/prompt-management/overview)\\n[Features](/docs/prompt-management/features/link-to-traces)\\n[Link to Traces](/docs/prompt-management/features/link-to-traces)\\n# Link Prompts to Traces\\nLinking prompts to [traces](/docs/observability) enables tracking of metrics and evaluations per prompt version. It's the foundation of improving prompt quality over time.\\nAfter linking prompts and traces, navigating to a generation span in Langfuse will highlight the prompt that was used to generate the response. To access the metrics, navigate to your prompt and click on the `Metrics` tab.\\n## How to Link Prompts to Traces\\nPython SDKJS/TS SDKOpenAI SDK (Python)OpenAI SDK (JS/TS)Langchain (Python)Langchain (JS/TS)Vercel AI SDK\\nFor generations created with the Langfuse Python SDK, pass the prompt directly to the generation using the `prompt` keyword argument. This links the prompt only to the intended generation and is the recommended approach.\\nYou can set the prompt on a specific generation with one of the following Langfuse Python SDK methods. For more information, see the [SDK documentation](/docs/observability/sdk/python/instrumentation).\\n **Decorators**\\n \\n \\n```\\nfrom langfuse import observe, get_client\\nlangfuse = get_client()\\n@observe(as_type=\\\"generation\\\")\\ndef nested_generation():\\n prompt = langfuse.get_prompt(\\\"movie-critic\\\")\\n langfuse.update_current_generation(\\n prompt=prompt,\\n )\\n@observe()\\ndef main():\\n nested_generation()\\nmain()\\n```\\n **Context Managers**\\n \\n \\n```\\nfrom langfuse import get_client\\nlangfuse = get_client()\\nprompt = langfuse.get_prompt(\\\"movie-critic\\\")\\nwith langfuse.start_as_current_observation(\\n as_type=\\\"generation\\\",\\n name=\\\"movie-generation\\\",\\n model=\\\"gpt-4o\\\",\\n prompt=prompt\\n) as generation:\\n # Your LLM call here\\n generation.update(output=\\\"LLM response\\\")\\n```\\n **Manual observations**\\n \\n \\n```\\nfrom langfuse import get_client\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\nlangfuse = get_client()\\nprompt = langfuse.get_prompt(\\\"movie-critic\\\")\\ngeneration = langfuse.start_observation(\\n name=\\\"movie-generation\\\",\\n as_type=\\\"generation\\\",\\n model=\\\"gpt-4o\\\",\\n prompt=prompt\\n)\\n///# Your LLM call here\\ngeneration.update(output=\\\"LLM response\\\")\\ngeneration.end() ///# Important: manually end the generation\\n```\\n **Propagate a prompt to multiple generations**\\nUse `propagate_attributes(prompt=prompt)` when multiple generations created within the same context use the same prompt version. This option is available in Python SDK 4.14.0 and later.\\n \\n \\n```\\nfrom langfuse import get_client, propagate_attributes\\nlangfuse = get_client()\\nprompt = langfuse.get_prompt(\\\"movie-critic\\\")\\nwith propagate_attributes(prompt=prompt):\\n with langfuse.start_as_current_observation(\\n as_type=\\\"generation\\\",\\n name=\\\"movie-review\\\",\\n ) as generation:\\n generation.update(\\n input=prompt.compile(movie=\\\"Dune 2\\\"),\\n output=\\\"A sweeping, ambitious sequel.\\\",\\n )\\n with langfuse.start_as_current_observation(\\n as_type=\\\"generation\\\",\\n name=\\\"movie-review\\\",\\n ) as generation:\\n generation.update(\\n input=prompt.compile(movie=\\\"Arrival\\\"),\\n output=\\\"A thoughtful and moving science-fiction film.\\\",\\n )\\n```\\n **Third-party instrumentation**\\nPropagation is also useful when an instrumentation library creates generations for you and does not expose a Langfuse `prompt` argument. For example, with the [LiteLLM OpenTelemetry integration](/integrations/frameworks/litellm-sdk):\\n \\n \\n```\\nimport litellm\\nfrom langfuse import get_client, propagate_attributes\\nlangfuse = get_client()\\nprompt = langfuse.get_prompt(\\\"movie-critic\\\")\\nlitellm.callbacks = [\\\"langfuse_otel\\\"]\\nwith propagate_attributes(prompt=prompt):\\n response = litellm.completion(\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\n model=\\\"gpt-4o\\\",\\n messages=[\\n {\\n \\\"role\\\": \\\"user\\\",\\n \\\"content\\\": prompt.compile(movie=\\\"Dune 2\\\"),\\n }\\n ],\\n )\\n```\\nThis also works with the OpenAI Agents SDK and OpenInference instrumentations exported through the Langfuse Python SDK. Only generation observations are linked to the prompt. If a generation sets its own prompt explicitly, that prompt takes precedence over the propagated prompt.\\nThere are three ways to create traces with the Langfuse JS/TS SDK. For more information, see the [SDK documentation](/docs/observability/sdk/typescript/instrumentation).\\n **Observe wrapper**\\n \\n \\n```\\nimport { LangfuseClient } from \\\"@langfuse/client\\\";\\nimport { observe, updateActiveObservation } from \\\"@langfuse/tracing\\\";\\nconst langfuse = new LangfuseClient();\\nconst callLLM = async (input: string) => {\\n const prompt = await langfuse.prompt.get(\\\"my-prompt\\\");\\n updateActiveObservation({ prompt }, { asType: \\\"generation\\\" });\\n return await invokeLLM(input);\\n};\\nexport const observedCallLLM = observe(callLLM);\\n```\\n **Context manager**\\n \\n \\n```\\nimport { LangfuseClient } from \\\"@langfuse/client\\\";\\nimport { startActiveObservation } from \\\"@langfuse/tracing\\\";\\nconst langfuse = new LangfuseClient();\\nstartActiveObservation(\\n \\\"llm\\\",\\n async (generation) => {\\n const prompt = await langfuse.prompt.get(\\\"my-prompt\\\");\\n generation.update({ prompt });\\n },\\n { asType: \\\"generation\\\" },\\n);\\n```\\n **Manual observations**\\n \\n \\n```\\nimport { LangfuseClient } from \\\"@langfuse/client\\\";\\nimport { startObservation } from \\\"@langfuse/tracing\\\";\\nconst prompt = await new LangfuseClient().prompt.get(\\\"my-prompt\\\");\\nstartObservation(\\n \\\"llm\\\",\\n {\\n prompt,\\n },\\n { asType: \\\"generation\\\" },\\n);\\n```\\n \\n \\n```\\nfrom langfuse.openai import openai\\nfrom langfuse import get_client\"}], \"type\": \"content\"}}, {\"type\": \"document\", \"record_type\": \"site\", \"url\":
