{"type": "text", "text": "# Langfuse\n\n> Langfuse is an **open-source AI engineering platform** ([GitHub](https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse)) that helps teams collaboratively debug, analyze, and iterate on their LLM applications. All platform features are natively integrated to accelerate the development workflow.\n\n## Markdown Access\n\nEvery page on langfuse.com is available as plain Markdown. Append `.md` to any URL, or send an `Accept: text/markdown` header:\n\n```bash\ncurl https://langfuse.com/docs/observability/get-started.md\n```\n\nThe links in the section indexes below already point at the `.md` variants.\n\n## Docs Search API\n\nSemantic search (RAG) over the Langfuse documentation, returning an answer with the relevant pages and excerpts. No authentication required. Use this instead of guessing when a specific page does not answer the question:\n\n```bash\ncurl -sG \"https://langfuse.com/api/search-docs\" --data-urlencode \"query=How do I trace a LangGraph agent?\"\n```\n\n- **Endpoint**: `https://langfuse.com/api/search-docs?query=<question>`\n- **Documentation**: [REST endpoint](https://langfuse.com/docs/docs-mcp#rest-endpoint)\n\nAsk specific, self-contained questions in natural language. This is the same search that backs the `searchLangfuseDocs` MCP tool below.\n\n## Langfuse Docs MCP Server\n\nConnect to the Langfuse Docs MCP server to access documentation directly in your AI editor:\n\n- **Endpoint**: `https://langfuse.com/api/mcp`\n- **Transport**: `streamableHttp`\n- **Documentation**: [Langfuse Docs MCP Server](https://langfuse.com/docs/docs-mcp)\n\nThe MCP server provides tools to search Langfuse documentation, GitHub issues, and discussions. See the [installation guide](https://langfuse.com/docs/docs-mcp) for setup instructions in Cursor, VS Code, Claude Desktop, and other MCP clients.\n\n## Langfuse Skill for AI Coding Agents\n\nInstall the Langfuse skill before implementing anything with Langfuse. The skill provides up-to-date documentation, best-practice workflows for instrumentation, prompt management, and programmatic API access via the Langfuse CLI.\n\nInstall from: [github.com/langfuse/skills](https://github.com/langfuse/skills/tree/main/skills/langfuse)\n\n## Tracing Best Practices\n\nBefore instrumenting an application with Langfuse, read [What does a good trace look like?](https://langfuse.com/docs/observability/best-practices.md) — it covers trace scope, observation naming, meaningful input/output, and the attributes (metadata, tags, users, sessions) that evaluators, dashboards, and experiments rely on.\n\n## Docs\n\nFor the best results, install the [Langfuse skill](https://github.com/langfuse/skills/tree/main/skills/langfuse) before using these However, the principles of this Langfuse integration apply to other languages supported by Semantic Kernel, including [C#](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/semantic-kernel/concepts/enterprise-readiness/observability/?pivots=programming-language-csharp) and [Java](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/semantic-kernel/concepts/enterprise-readiness/observability/?pivots=programming-language-java)._\\n## Getting Started\\nLet's walk through a practical example of using Semantic Kernel and integrating it with Langfuse for comprehensive tracing.\\n### Step 1: Install Dependencies\\n \\n \\n```\\n%pip install langfuse openlit semantic-kernel\\n```\\n### Step 2: Configure Langfuse SDK\\nNext, set up your Langfuse API keys. You can get these keys by signing up for a free [Langfuse Cloud](https://langfuse.com/cloud) account or by [self-hosting Langfuse](https://langfuse.com/self-hosting). These environment variables are essential for the Langfuse client to authenticate and send data to your Langfuse project.\\n \\n \\n```\\nimport os\\n///# Get keys for your project from the project settings page: https://cloud.langfuse.com\\nos.environ.setdefault(\\\"LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY\\\", \\\"pk-lf-...\\\");\\nos.environ.setdefault(\\\"LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY\\\", \\\"sk-lf-...\\\");\\nos.environ.setdefault(\\\"LANGFUSE_BASE_URL\\\", \\\"https://cloud.langfuse.com\\\"); ///# 🇪🇺 EU region\\n///# Other Langfuse data regions include 🇺🇸 US: https://us.cloud.langfuse.com, 🇯🇵 Japan: https://jp.cloud.langfuse.com and ⚕️ HIPAA: https://hipaa.cloud.langfuse.com\\n///# Your OpenAI key\\nos.environ.setdefault(\\\"OPENAI_API_KEY\\\", \\\"sk-proj-...\\\");\\nos.environ.setdefault(\\\"OPENAI_CHAT_MODEL_ID\\\", \\\"gpt-4o\\\");\\n```\\nWith the environment variables set, we can now initialize the Langfuse client. `get_client()` initializes the Langfuse client using the credentials provided in the environment variables.\\n \\n \\n```\"}], \"type\": \"content\"}}, {\"type\": \"document\", \"record_type\": \"documentation\", \"url\": \"https://langfuse.com/docs/observability/sdk/overview\", \"title\": \"Langfuse SDKs\", \"source\": {\"content\": [{\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\n print(\\\"Authentication failed. Please check your credentials and host.\\\")\\n```\\nThe Langfuse client is a singleton. It can be accessed anywhere in your application using the [`get_client()`](https://python.reference.langfuse.com/langfuse#get_client) function.\\nAlternative: Configure via constructor\\n+\\nOptionally, you can initialize the client via [`Langfuse()`](https://python.reference.langfuse.com/langfuse#Langfuse) to pass in configuration options (see below). Otherwise, it is created automatically when you call [`get_client()`](https://python.reference.langfuse.com/langfuse#get_client) based on environment variables.\\nIf you create multiple `Langfuse` instances with the same `public_key`, the singleton instance is reused and new arguments are ignored.\\nInitialize client\\n \\n \\n```\\nfrom langfuse import Langfuse\\nlangfuse = Langfuse(\\n public_key=\\\"your-public-key\\\",\\n secret_key=\\\"your-secret-key\\\",\\n base_url=\\\"https://cloud.langfuse.com\\\", ///# 🇪🇺 EU region\\n # Other Langfuse data regions include 🇺🇸 US: https://us.cloud.langfuse.com, 🇯🇵 Japan: https://jp.cloud.langfuse.com and ⚕️ HIPAA: https://hipaa.cloud.langfuse.com\\n)\\n```\\nAll key configuration options are listed in the [Python SDK reference](https://python.reference.langfuse.com/langfuse#Langfuse).\\nInitialize the [`LangfuseClient`](https://langfuse-js-git-main-langfuse.vercel.app/classes/_langfuse_client.LangfuseClient.html) to interact with Langfuse. The client will automatically use the environment variables you set above.\\nclient.ts\\n \\n \\n```\\nimport { LangfuseClient } from \\\"@langfuse/client\\\";\\nconst langfuse = new LangfuseClient();\\n```\\nAlternative: Configure via constructor\\n+\\nYou can also pass the Langfuse credentials directly to the constructor:\\nclient.ts\\n \"}], \"type\": \"content\"}}, {\"type\": February Update - Langfuse Blog\", \"source\": {\"content\": [{\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\nPopular among Langfuse and LiteLLM users (especially in enterprise and regulated settings), this stack enables efficient observability without extensive instrumentation. LiteLLM further enhances the experience with virtual LLM keys, budgeting, failovers, and compatibility with over 100 LLMs through the OpenAI API schema.\\n\\n---\\n\\n→ **Learn more** : [oss-llmops-stack.com](https://oss-llmops-stack.com/)\\n\\n---\\n\\n## 🎁 New Features\\n\\n---\\n\\nWe’ve shipped a host of new features to simplify development workflows and help new users get started quickly:\\n\\n---\\n\\n * **Dataset CSV Upload** : Quickly create Dataset Items from CSV files.\\n\\n---\\n\\n * **Model Context Protocol (MCP) Prompt Server** : Easily integrate Langfuse prompts with LLM Agents, Claude Desktop, Cursor, and other MCP clients.\\n\\n---\\n\\n * **Graph View for LangGraph Traces** : Visually follow agent executions in an intuitive graph. (Generalized version coming soon!)\\n\\n---\\n\\n * **Typed Public API Client in SDKs** : Simplified access to Langfuse’s API with fully-typed clients.\\n\\n---\\n\\n * **Improved In-Product Onboarding** : Interactive screens highlight unused features to help you maximize Langfuse.\\n\\n---\\n\\n→ **View the full** [Changelog](/changelog)\\n\\n---\\n\\n## 👨‍💻 We’re Hiring in Berlin\\n\\n---\\n\\nLangfuse is growing fast! We’re seeking talented individuals to join our Berlin-based team. Looking for a change? Email us or forward this opportunity—there’s a USD 5K referral bonus!\\n→ [Learn more and apply](/careers)\\n\\n---\\n\\nLast updated on July 14, 2025\\n\\n---\\n\"}], \"type\": \"content\"}}, {\"type\": \"document\", \"record_type\": \"site\", \"url\": \"https://langfuse.com/blog/2025-03-19-ai-agent-comparison\", \"title\": \"Comparing Open-Source AI Agent Frameworks - Langfuse Blog\", \"source\": {\"content\": [{\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\n[CrewAI](https://github.com/crewAIInc/crewAI) is all about role-based collaboration among multiple agents. Imagine giving each agent a distinct skillset or personality, then letting them cooperate (or even debate) to solve a problem. This framework offers a higher-level abstraction called a “Crew,” which is basically a container for multiple agents that each has a role or function. The Crew coordinates workflows, allowing these agents to share context and build upon one another’s contributions. I like CrewAI as it is easy to configure while still letting you attach advanced memory and error-handling logic.\\n\\n---\\n\\n_[Example trace in Langfuse](https://cloud.langfuse.com/project/cloramnkj0002jz088vzn1ja4/traces/3b485ea0d723bab3e5e53e72c6b10a71?timestamp=2025-02-24T10%3A34%3A30.423Z&observation=0c53ff94ec9c3da9)_\\n[How to trace CrewAI agents with Langfuse →](/integrations/frameworks/crewai)\\nIf your use case calls for a multi-agent approach—like a “Planner” agent delegating tasks to a “Researcher” and “Writer” agent—CrewAI makes that easy. The built-in memory modules and fluid user experience have led to growing adoption where collaboration and parallelization of tasks are important.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## AutoGen\\n\\n---\\n\\n[AutoGen](https://github.com/microsoft/autogen), born out of Microsoft Research, frames everything as an asynchronous conversation among specialized agents. Each agent can be a ChatGPT-style assistant or a tool executor, and you orchestrate how they pass messages back and forth. This asynchronous approach reduces blocking, making it well-suited for longer tasks or scenarios where an agent needs to wait on external events. Developers who like the idea of “multiple LLMs in conversation” may find AutoGen’s event-driven approach nice, especially for dynamic dialogues that need real-time concurrency or frequent role switching.\\n\\n---\\n\"}], \"type\": \"content\"}}, {\"type\": \"document\", \"record_type\": \"site\", \"url\": \"https://langfuse.com/resources/engineering/opentelemetry-languages\", \"title\": \"Use Langfuse from Go, Java, C#, and Ruby via OpenTelemetry - Langfuse\", \"source\": {\"content\": [{\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"---\\n\\n * testcookie\\n * 17 minutes\\n * This cookie is used to test whether the browser accepts cookies.\\n\\n---\\n\\n * ytidb::LAST_RESULT_ENTRY_KEY\\n * The cookie ytidb::LAST_RESULT_ENTRY_KEY is used by YouTube to store the last search result entry that was clicked by the user. This information is used to improve the user experience by providing more relevant search results in the future.\\n\\n---\\n\\n * cookietest\\n * The cookietest cookie is typically used to determine whether the user's browser accepts cookies, essential for website functionality and user experience.\\n\\n---\\n\\n * GFE_RTT\\n * 5 minutes\\n\\n---\\n\\n * dmn_chk_*\\n * This cookie is set to track user activity across the website.\\n\\n---\\n\\n * loom_anon_comment\\n\\n---\\n\\n * li_gc\\n * Linkedin set this cookie for storing visitor's consent regarding using cookies for non-essential purposes.\\n\\n---\\n\\n * lidc\\n * 1 day\\n * LinkedIn sets the lidc cookie to facilitate data center selection.\\n\\n---\\n\\n * metabase.DEVICE\\n * 1 year 1 month 4 days\\n * Stores a unique device identifier to maintain session continuity for embedded analytics dashboards, improving authentication, usage tracking, and visualization performance.\\n\\n---\\n\\n * loom_referral_video\\n * Stores referral source and engagement data for embedded Loom video, enabling attribution, playback optimization, and analytics of views, interactions, conversions.\\n\\n---\\n\\n * __Host-psifi.analyticsTrace\\n * 6 hours\\n * Stores diagnostic traces for embedded Loom videos, tracking interactions, playback performance, and errors to improve analytics, troubleshooting, and user experience.\\n\\n---\\n\\n * __Host-psifi.analyticsTraceV2\\n * 6 hours\\n * Tracks interactions and performance of embedded Loom video player, capturing session traces, errors, and usage metrics to improve service reliability.\\n\\n---\\n\\n * ajs_anonymous_id\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\nexp, err := otlptracehttp.New(ctx) // reads OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_* env vars\\n\\n\\ntp := trace.NewTracerProvider(trace.WithBatcher(exp))\\n\\n\\notel.SetTracerProvider(tp)\\n\\n\\ndefer tp.Shutdown(ctx) // flush before exit; short-lived programs lose spans otherwise\\n\\n\\n```\\n\\n---\\n\\nInstrument LLM calls by setting `gen_ai.*` attributes on the spans you create around them. For automatic LLM instrumentation in Go, [OpenLIT](/docs/opentelemetry/example-openlit) provides library support that exports to Langfuse the same way.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Java\\nThe zero-code path is the OpenTelemetry Java agent: attach it to the JVM and configure it entirely through the environment variables above.\\n\\n---\\n\\n \\n \\n```\\n\\n\\nOTEL_TRACES_EXPORTER=otlp \\\\\\n\\n\\nOTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL=http/protobuf \\\\\\n\\n\\njava -javaagent:opentelemetry-javaagent.jar -jar app.jar\\n\\n\\n```\\n\\n---\\n\\nThe agent instruments HTTP calls automatically; wrap your LLM client calls in spans with `gen_ai.*` attributes (or use [OpenLLMetry](/docs/opentelemetry/example-openllmetry), which extends automatic LLM instrumentation to Java) so model calls render as generations rather than generic HTTP spans.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## C# / .NET\\nUse the OpenTelemetry .NET SDK with the OTLP exporter set to the HTTP protocol:\\n\\n---\\n\\n \\n \\n```\\n\\n\\nusing OpenTelemetry;\\n\\n\\nusing OpenTelemetry.Trace;\\n\\n\\nusing OpenTelemetry.Exporter;\\n\\n\\nusing var tracerProvider = Sdk.CreateTracerProviderBuilder()\\n\\n\\n .AddSource(\\\"my-llm-app\\\")\\n\\n\\n .AddOtlpExporter(o => o.Protocol = OtlpExportProtocol.HttpProtobuf) // reads OTLP env vars\\n\\n\\n .Build();\\n\\n\\n```\\n\\n---\\n\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\nCreate an `ActivitySource` for your LLM calls and set `gen_ai.*` tags on those activities. Teams using Semantic Kernel or similar frameworks can also route that telemetry to Langfuse through the OTel-based instrumentation libraries listed in the [OpenTelemetry docs](/integrations/native/opentelemetry).\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Ruby\\nThe OTel Ruby SDK exports OTLP over HTTP by default and honors the shared environment variables:\\n\\n---\\n\\n \\n \\n```\\n\\n\\nrequire \\\"opentelemetry/sdk\\\"\\n\\n\\nrequire \\\"opentelemetry/exporter/otlp\\\"\\n\\n\\nOpenTelemetry::SDK.configure # reads OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_* env vars\\n\\n\\ntracer = OpenTelemetry.tracer_provider.tracer(\\\"my-llm-app\\\")\\n\\n\\ntracer.in_span(\\\"chat-completion\\\", attributes: {\\n\\n\\n \\\"gen_ai.system\\\" => \\\"openai\\\",\\n\\n\\n \\\"gen_ai.request.model\\\" => \\\"gpt-4.1\\\",\\n\\n\\n \\\"user.id\\\" => user_id,\\n\\n\\n}) do |span|\\n\\n\\n # call your LLM provider here, then record usage:\\n\\n\\n span.set_attribute(\\\"gen_ai.usage.input_tokens\\\", usage.prompt_tokens)\\n\\n\\n span.set_attribute(\\\"gen_ai.usage.output_tokens\\\", usage.completion_tokens)\\n\\n\\nend\\n\\n\\n```\\n\\n---\\n\\nThere is no automatic LLM instrumentation ecosystem for Ruby yet, so the manual `gen_ai.*` pattern above is the standard approach.\\n## Verifying the integration\\n\\n---\\n\\n 1. Send one traced request and flush the exporter (short-lived processes must shut down the tracer provider explicitly, or the last batch never leaves the process).\\n 2. Open the trace in Langfuse and confirm the LLM call renders as a generation with token counts, not as a generic span.\\n 3. If spans arrive but token usage or input/output are missing, compare your attribute names against the [property mapping table](/integrations/native/opentelemetry); near-miss attribute names are the most common cause.\\n\\n---\\n\"}], \"type\": \"content\"}}, {\"type\": \"document\", \"record_type\": \"github_discussion\", \"url\": \"https://github.com/orgs/langfuse/discussions/4772\", \"title\": \"Support Langfuse on Microsoft's Semantic Kernel Framework\", \"source\": {\"content\": [{\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"Title: Support Langfuse on Microsoft's Semantic Kernel Framework\\nCategory: Ideas\\nAuthor: @dprokhorov17\\nTimestamp: December 18, 2024\\nBody:\\n### Describe the feature or potential improvement\\n\\nhttps://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/semantic-kernel/overview/\\n\\n### Additional information\\n\\n_No response_\\nComments:\\n\\n Comment #1 from @marcklingen on December 18, 2024:\\n\\n thanks for sharing!\\n\\n Comment #2 from @marcklingen on March 10, 2025:\\n\\n Thanks to the Opentelemetry endpoint, Semantic Kernel can now be traced and evaluated with Langfuse. Documentation: https://langfuse.com/docs/integrations/semantic-kernel\\n\\n Replies to comment #2:\\n\\n Reply #1 to comment #2 from marcklingen on March 11, 2025:\\n\\n > Opentelemetry endpoint\\r\\n\\r\\nHey @marcklingen, thanks for the update. I’m wondering if the OpenTelemetry endpoint is the only option. Can’t we use a callback or decorator to trace?\\n\\n Reply #2 to comment #2 from marcklingen on March 11, 2025:\\n\\n Hi @marcklingen ,\\r\\n\\r\\nso, the support is only for Python? Do you plan to create a .NET dll to support Semantic Kernel natively in C#?\\n\\n Reply #3 to comment #2 from marcklingen on March 13, 2025:\\n\\n afaik, you can use the OTel integration also in C#: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/semantic-kernel/concepts/enterprise-readiness/observability/?pivots=programming-language-csharp\\n\\n Comment #3 from @DavidMarquezF on April 16, 2025:\\n\\n After following the https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/semantic-kernel/concepts/enterprise-readiness/observability/telemetry-with-app-insights?tabs=Powershell&pivots=programming-language-csharp tutorial but replacing `.AddAzureMonitorTraceExporter(options => options.ConnectionString = connectionString)` for \\r\\n```\\r\\nAddOtlpExporter((OtlpExporterOptions options) => {\\r\\n options.Endpoint = new Uri(langfuseHost + \\\"/api/public/otel\\\");\\r\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \" options.Headers = $\\\"Authorization=Basic {LANGFUSE_AUTH}\\\";\\r\\n })\\r\\n```\\r\\nwhere `LANGFUSE_AUTH` is:\\r\\n```\\r\\n var LANGFUSE_AUTH = Convert.ToBase64String(Encoding.UTF8.GetBytes(pubkey + \\\":\\\" + privkey));\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\nI'm not getting any traces in LangFuse. For debugging i also added the `AddConsoleExporter` and everything seems to be working properly. It's just not getting traced in Langfuse. Public and private key work (i tried with curl), so i'm not sure if the [docs](https://langfuse.com/docs/integrations/semantic-kernel) are missing some initial step? \\r\\n\\r\\nI've basically just created a Langfuse project from scratch so there's nothing in it\\r\\n\\n\\n Replies to comment #3:\\n\\n Reply #1 to comment #3 from DavidMarquezF on April 16, 2025:\\n\\n I also tested with Azure Insights and it works properly\\n\\n Reply #2 to comment #3 from DavidMarquezF on April 17, 2025:\\n\\n Do you get any debugging logs via this setup?\\r\\n\\r\\nDo you know what transport/protocol is used by default? Langfuse requires OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_PROTOCOL=http/protobuf\\n\\n Reply #3 to comment #3 from DavidMarquezF on April 18, 2025:\\n\\n It would be much appreciated if you could extend your telemetry notebook to include Azure Application Insights. I am also trying to implement that in Python; however, the [Semantic Kernel side](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/semantic-kernel/concepts/enterprise-readiness/observability/telemetry-with-app-insights?tabs=Powershell&pivots=programming-language-python) is already complex, and I couldn't push logs there either.\\n\\n Reply #4 to comment #3 from DavidMarquezF on May 26, 2025:\\n\\n @DavidMarquezF @anu43 I just came across this today and was also struggling to get it working with Langfuse. \\r\\n\\r\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\nAfter a bit of fiddling and using Jaeger locally I was able to figure out what was wrong. Below is a full working sample with Semantic Kernel configured to send OTLP traces to Langfuse.\\r\\n\\r\\nIf you are following all the info that's out there about Langfuse it seems to be mostly right except I had to explicit set the endpoint to `https://us.cloud.langfuse.com/api/public/otel/v1/traces` instead of just `https://us.cloud.langfuse.com/api/public/otel`.\\r\\n\\r\\nThat's when it worked.\\r\\n\\r\\nHere is the full guide.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Minimal OpenTelemetry Setup for .NET Console App (Traces & Logs via OTLP/HTTP)\\r\\n\\r\\nThis guide outlines the minimum code and configuration to send OpenTelemetry traces and from Semantic Kernel in a .NET console application to an OTLP-compatible backend (e.g., Langfuse, Jaeger) using the HTTP/protobuf protocol, including proxy support and custom SSL certificate validation if you want to inspect traffic using Fiddler or a similar proxy.\\r\\n\\r\\n### 1. Project Setup (NuGet Packages)\\r\\n\\r\\nEnsure your .NET console project (`.csproj`) includes the following OpenTelemetry packages:\\r\\n\\r\\n```xml\\r\\n<Project Sdk=\\\"Microsoft.NET.Sdk\\\">\\r\\n <ItemGroup>\\r\\n <PackageReference Include=\\\"Microsoft.SemanticKernel\\\" Version=\\\"1.10.0\\\" />\\r\\n <PackageReference Include=\\\"OpenTelemetry\\\" Version=\\\"1.7.0\\\" />\\r\\n <PackageReference Include=\\\"OpenTelemetry.Exporter.OpenTelemetryProtocol\\\" Version=\\\"1.7.0\\\" />\\r\\n <PackageReference Include=\\\"OpenTelemetry.Extensions.Hosting\\\" Version=\\\"1.7.0\\\" />\\r\\n <PackageReference Include=\\\"OpenTelemetry.Instrumentation.Http\\\" Version=\\\"1.7.0\\\" />\\r\\n <PackageReference Include=\\\"Microsoft.Extensions.Logging.Console\\\" Version=\\\"8.0.0\\\" />\\r\\n </ItemGroup>\\r\\n</Project>\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\n### 2. Environment Variables (`.env` file)\\r\\n\\r\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \" {\\r\\n webProxy.Credentials = new NetworkCredential(proxyUsername, proxyPassword);\\r\\n }\\r\\n handler.Proxy = webProxy;\\r\\n handler.UseProxy = true;\\r\\n }\\r\\n else\\r\\n {\\r\\n handler.UseProxy = false;\\r\\n }\\r\\n return new HttpClient(handler);\\r\\n }\\r\\n\\r\\n // Configures OTLP Exporter options (shared for traces and logs)\\r\\n static void ConfigureOtlpExporter(OtlpExporterOptions options)\\r\\n {\\r\\n string? otlpEndpoint = Env.GetString(\\\"LANGFUSE_OTLP_ENDPOINT\\\");\\r\\n string? publicKey = Env.GetString(\\\"LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY\\\");\\r\\n string? secretKey = Env.GetString(\\\"LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY\\\");\\r\\n var plainTextBytes = System.Text.Encoding.UTF8.GetBytes($\\\"{publicKey}:{secretKey}\\\");\\r\\n string base64EncodedAuth = Convert.ToBase64String(plainTextBytes);\\r\\n\\r\\n options.Endpoint = new Uri(otlpEndpoint);\\r\\n options.Protocol = OtlpExportProtocol.HttpProtobuf;\\r\\n options.Headers = $\\\"Authorization=Basic {base64EncodedAuth}\\\"; \\r\\n options.HttpClientFactory = CreateCustomHttpClient;\\r\\n }\\r\\n\\r\\n static ILoggerFactory CreateAppLoggerFactory(ResourceBuilder resourceBuilder)\\r\\n {\\r\\n return LoggerFactory.Create(builder =>\\r\\n {\\r\\n builder\\r\\n .AddOpenTelemetry(options =>\\r\\n {\\r\\n options.SetResourceBuilder(resourceBuilder);\\r\\n options.AddOtlpExporter(ConfigureOtlpExporter);\\r\\n options.IncludeFormattedMessage = true;\\r\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \" options.IncludeScopes = true;\\r\\n \\r\\n })\\r\\n .AddConsole() // Also log to console for local debugging\\r\\n .SetMinimumLevel(LogLevel.Debug);\\r\\n });\\r\\n }\\r\\n\\r\\n static TracerProvider CreateAppTracerProvider(ResourceBuilder resourceBuilder)\\r\\n {\\r\\n var tracerProviderBuilder = Sdk.CreateTracerProviderBuilder()\\r\\n .SetResourceBuilder(resourceBuilder)\\r\\n .AddSource(MyActivitySource.Name) \\r\\n .AddConsoleExporter() // Also export traces to console for local debugging\\r\\n .AddOtlpExporter(ConfigureOtlpExporter);\\r\\n\\r\\n return tracerProviderBuilder.Build()!;\\r\\n }\\r\\n\\r\\n static async Task Main(string[] args)\\r\\n {\\r\\n Env.Load();\\r\\n\\r\\n \\r\\n AppContext.SetSwitch(\\\"Microsoft.SemanticKernel.Experimental.GenAI.EnableOTelDiagnostics\\\", true);\\r\\n AppContext.SetSwitch(\\\"Microsoft.SemanticKernel.Experimental.GenAI.EnableOTelDiagnosticsSensitive\\\", true);\\r\\n\\r\\n var resourceBuilder = ResourceBuilder.CreateDefault()\\r\\n .AddService(serviceName: \\\"MyMinimalOtelApp\\\", serviceVersion: \\\"1.0.0\\\");\\r\\n\\r\\n using var loggerFactory = CreateAppLoggerFactory(resourceBuilder);\\r\\n var logger = loggerFactory.CreateLogger<Program>();\\r\\n logger.LogInformation(\\\"Application starting...\\\");\\r\\n\\r\\n using var tracerProvider = CreateAppTracerProvider(resourceBuilder);\\r\\n\\r\\n /* DO ANYTHING WITH SEMANTIC KERNEL HERE AND TRACES WILL BE PICKED UP */\\r\\n\\r\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \" // --- Manually trigger a custom trace (Activity) ---\\r\\n using (var activity = MyActivitySource.StartActivity(\\\"SampleOperation\\\"))\\r\\n {\\r\\n logger.LogInformation(\\\"Inside SampleOperation Activity.\\\");\\r\\n activity?.SetTag(\\\"my.custom.tag\\\", \\\"TagValue123\\\");\\r\\n activity?.AddEvent(new ActivityEvent(\\\"Something interesting happened here!\\\"));\\r\\n \\r\\n try\\r\\n {\\r\\n // Simulate some work\\r\\n await Task.Delay(150);\\r\\n \\r\\n activity?.SetStatus(ActivityStatusCode.Ok, \\\"Operation completed successfully\\\");\\r\\n }\\r\\n catch (Exception ex)\\r\\n {\\r\\n activity?.SetStatus(ActivityStatusCode.Error, $\\\"Operation failed: {ex.Message}\\\");\\r\\n activity?.RecordException(ex); // Record exception details\\r\\n logger.LogError(ex, \\\"Error during SampleOperation\\\");\\r\\n throw;\\r\\n }\\r\\n }\\r\\n logger.LogInformation(\\\"SampleOperation finished.\\\");\\r\\n // --- End of custom trace ---\\r\\n\\r\\n\\r\\n logger.LogInformation(\\\"Application finished. Flushing telemetry...\\\");\\r\\n\\r\\n // Explicitly flush telemetry data before application exits\\r\\n // This is crucial for console apps to ensure data is sent.\\r\\n tracerProvider.ForceFlush();\\r\\n // For logs, flushing is often handled by disposing the logger factory or specific log processors,\\r\\n // but ForceFlush on tracerProvider is the most direct for traces.\\r\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \" // You might need to wait briefly for asynchronous export:\\r\\n // await Task.Delay(5000); // Adjust delay as needed if flushing seems incomplete\\r\\n\\r\\n Console.WriteLine(\\\"Press any key to exit...\\\");\\r\\n Console.ReadKey();\\r\\n }\\r\\n }\\r\\n}\\r\\n```\\n\\n Comment #4 from @aiakubovich on May 14, 2025:\\n\\n @marcklingen Any plans to add langfuse docs for Semantic Kernel on #C? \\n\\n Comment #5 from @ouvreboite on July 23, 2025:\\n\\n @marcklingen what would be a good minimal set of features for a C# / OTEL Langfuse SDK?\\r\\n\\r\\n- Helpers for using the Langfuse OTEL endpoint\\r\\n- Helpers to add Langfuse-specific trace/span [attributes](https://langfuse.com/integrations/native/opentelemetry#property-mapping) to an Activity (C# internal representation of a span)\\r\\n- a `CreateScore` method to send scores to the API\\r\\n- a `GetPrompt` method (with TTL based caching) to fetch prompts from the API\\r\\n\\r\\nAnything else?\\n\\n Comment #6 from @joshuabrewer13 on September 24, 2025:\\n\\n This thread got me part of the way there. Was still having some hard to diagnose issues sending protobuf requests from our .net service layer to the langfuse 3 OTEL endpoints. This is for a self hosted Langfuse 3 instance. The current \\\"working-okay\\\" version is:\\r\\n\\r\\n#### Program.cs\\r\\n\\r\\n\\r\\n```C#\\r\\nvar resourceBuilder = ResourceBuilder.CreateDefault().\\r\\n AddService(serviceName: \\\"SemanticKernelTelemetry\\\", serviceVersion: \\\"1.0.0\\\");\\r\\n \\r\\n*snip*\\r\\n \\r\\n using var traceProvider = Sdk.CreateTracerProviderBuilder()\\r\\n .SetSampler(new AlwaysOnSampler())\\r\\n .SetResourceBuilder(resourceBuilder)\\r\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \" .AddProcessor(new HttpContextEnrichingProcessor(new HttpContextAccessor())) // this is a custom class you can debug what's being sent and add global headers\\r\\n .AddSource(\\\"Microsoft.SemanticKernel*\\\")\\r\\n .AddSource(\\\"GblChatController\\\") // Add your custom ActivitySource name here\\r\\n .AddConsoleExporter()\\r\\n .AddOtlpExporter(options =>\\r\\n {\\r\\n options.Endpoint = new Uri(otlpEndpoint);\\r\\n options.Protocol = OtlpExportProtocol.HttpProtobuf;\\r\\n options.Headers = $\\\"Authorization=Basic {base64EncodedAuth}\\\";\\r\\n })\\r\\n .Build();\\r\\n \\r\\n*snip*\\r\\n \\r\\n using var skOtelLoggerFactory = LoggerFactory.Create(builder =>\\r\\n{\\r\\n // Add OpenTelemetry as a logging provider\\r\\n builder.AddOpenTelemetry(options =>\\r\\n {\\r\\n options.SetResourceBuilder(resourceBuilder);\\r\\n\\r\\n options.AddConsoleExporter();\\r\\n \\r\\n // Format log messages. This is default to false.\\r\\n options.IncludeFormattedMessage = true;\\r\\n options.IncludeScopes = true;\\r\\n options.AddOtlpExporter(optionsx =>\\r\\n {\\r\\n optionsx.Endpoint = new Uri(otlpEndpoint);\\r\\n optionsx.Protocol = OtlpExportProtocol.HttpProtobuf;\\r\\n optionsx.Headers = $\\\"Authorization=Basic {base64EncodedAuth}\\\";\\r\\n \\r\\n // Custom HttpClientFactory to intercept and log request bodies - optional\\r\\n optionsx.HttpClientFactory = () =>\\r\\n {\\r\\n var handler = new HttpClientHandler();\\r\\n var loggingHandler = new OtlpLoggingHandler(handler, otlpEndpoint);\\r\\n return new HttpClient(loggingHandler);\\r\\n };\\r\\n });\\r\\n });\\r\\n builder.SetMinimumLevel(LogLevel.Debug);\\r\\n});\\r\\n\\r\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"*snip*\\r\\n\\r\\nvar kernelBuilder = Kernel.CreateBuilder();\\r\\n \\r\\n kernelBuilder.Services.AddSingleton(skOtelLoggerFactory);\\r\\n //rest of kernel config\\r\\n```\\r\\n#### Processors and Other Debuggers\\r\\n\\r\\n```C#\\r\\n// Custom DelegatingHandler to log OTLP request bodies\\r\\n public class OtlpLoggingHandler : DelegatingHandler\\r\\n {\\r\\n private readonly string _otlpEndpoint;\\r\\n\\r\\n public OtlpLoggingHandler(HttpMessageHandler innerHandler, string otlpEndpoint)\\r\\n : base(innerHandler)\\r\\n {\\r\\n _otlpEndpoint = otlpEndpoint;\\r\\n Console.WriteLine($\\\"[OTEL OTLP] OtlpLoggingHandler initialized for endpoint: {_otlpEndpoint}\\\");\\r\\n }\\r\\n\\r\\n protected override void Dispose(bool disposing)\\r\\n {\\r\\n // Console.WriteLine(\\\"[OTEL OTLP] OtlpLoggingHandler disposed\\\");\\r\\n base.Dispose(disposing);\\r\\n }\\r\\n\\r\\n protected override HttpResponseMessage Send(HttpRequestMessage request, CancellationToken cancellationToken)\\r\\n {\\r\\n // put whatever debug here to inspect the request\\r\\n return base.SendAsync(request, cancellationToken).GetAwaiter().GetResult();\\r\\n }\\r\\n\\r\\n protected override async Task<HttpResponseMessage> SendAsync(HttpRequestMessage request, CancellationToken cancellationToken)\\r\\n {\\r\\n // put whatever debug here to inspect the request\\r\\n return await base.SendAsync(request, cancellationToken);\\r\\n }\\r\\n }\\r\\n\\r\\n public class HttpContextEnrichingProcessor : BaseProcessor<Activity>\\r\\n {\\r\\n private readonly ingestion to Langfuse v4\", \"source\": {\"content\": [{\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"Migrate custom ingestion to Langfuse v4 - Langfuse\\n[Integrations](/integrations)\\n[Native](/docs/sdk/python/sdk-v3)\\n[OpenTelemetry](/integrations/native/opentelemetry)\\n[Migrate ingestion to v4](/integrations/native/opentelemetry/migration-to-v4)\\n# Migrate custom ingestion to Langfuse v4\\nUse this guide if you send tracing data to Langfuse through a custom integration. It covers both migrations from the legacy `/api/public/ingestion` endpoint and updates to existing OpenTelemetry (OTEL) pipelines.\\n**Using Python or JavaScript/TypeScript?** Use the [Langfuse SDK](/docs/observability/sdk/overview) instead of building directly on the OTEL API. The SDK handles Langfuse attributes, propagation, media, filtering, and export for you. Follow the [Python v3 → v4](/docs/observability/sdk/upgrade-path/python-v3-to-v4) or [JS/TS v4 → v5](/docs/observability/sdk/upgrade-path/js-v4-to-v5) migration guide. For other languages, use the [native OpenTelemetry API for your language](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/languages/) and export spans to Langfuse.\\n## Choose your migration path\\nCurrent setup| Migration path \\n---|--- \\nCustom events sent to `/api/public/ingestion`| Replace legacy ingestion events with OTEL spans \\nOTEL without `x-langfuse-ingestion-version: 4`| Update the exporter and audit the span format \\nOTEL with trace context only on the root span| Propagate context to every relevant span \\nOTEL using `langfuse.trace.input` or `langfuse.trace.output`| Move the overall input and output to the root observation \\nOTEL that re-exports a span to update data already accepted by Langfuse| Export one complete span \\n \\nAdding the `x-langfuse-ingestion-version: 4` header selects the v4 ingestion path, but the header alone does not make a legacy or incomplete span format v4-ready. Complete the applicable migration steps below before switching production traffic.\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\n## V4-ready ingestion checklist\\nYour integration is ready for the observations-first Langfuse v4 data model when it:\\n * sends traces via OTLP over HTTP to `/api/public/otel/v1/traces`;\\n * authenticates with Langfuse project keys via Basic Auth and sends `x-langfuse-ingestion-version: 4`;\\n * represents every operation as one complete OTEL span with valid trace ID, span ID, timing, and parent context;\\n * puts each operation's input and output on its observation, including the overall request and response on the root observation;\\n * copies trace-wide context needed for filtering or aggregation to every relevant span;\\n * uses explicit Langfuse metadata attributes for metadata that must be filterable;\\n * exports a span once rather than re-ingesting the same ID to update it; and\\n * targets observations, rather than legacy trace input/output, for evaluations.\\nSee the [OTEL endpoint configuration](/integrations/native/opentelemetry#opentelemetry-endpoint) and [complete attribute mapping](/integrations/native/opentelemetry#property-mapping) for the stable transport and schema reference.\\n## Migrate from the legacy ingestion API\\nThe legacy `/api/public/ingestion` endpoint accepts Langfuse-specific create and update events. The OTEL endpoint instead accepts standard OTLP spans. Use your language's [native OpenTelemetry API](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/languages/) to create and finish spans, and configure its OTLP/HTTP exporter to send them to Langfuse.\\nDo not translate each legacy API request into a separate OTEL export. Build the operation locally, set its final attributes, end it, and let the OTEL SDK export the completed span.\\n### Map legacy events to OTEL spans\\nLegacy ingestion concept| V4-ready OTEL representation \\n---|--- \\nTrace record| One OTEL trace ID shared by all observations. There is no separately ingested trace entity. \"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\nTrace name| `langfuse.trace.name`, copied to every span where the name must be queryable \\nTrace user, session, tags, release, version, environment| Corresponding `langfuse.*` attributes copied to every relevant span \\nTrace metadata| `langfuse.trace.metadata.<key>` copied to every relevant span \\nTrace input and output (deprecated)| Trace input/output is deprecated. Use `langfuse.observation.input` and `langfuse.observation.output` on the root span instead. \\nSpan, generation, or event| An OTEL span with `langfuse.observation.type` set to `span`, `generation`, or `event` \\nParent observation ID| OTEL parent span context \\nObservation input and output| `langfuse.observation.input` and `langfuse.observation.output` on that span \\nObservation metadata| `langfuse.observation.metadata.<key>` \\nModel, model parameters, usage, cost, or prompt link| The matching [Langfuse OTEL attributes](/integrations/native/opentelemetry#observation-level-attributes) \\nCreate followed by update events| One span assembled in memory and exported after it ends \\nScore event| The dedicated [Scores SDK or API](/docs/evaluation/evaluation-methods/scores-via-sdk), not an OTLP trace span \\n \\nOTEL attributes support scalar values and arrays of scalar values. Serialize structured input, output, model parameters, usage, cost, and metadata values as JSON strings where required by the [attribute mapping](/integrations/native/opentelemetry#property-mapping).\\n### Configure the OTLP exporter\\nThe exact setup depends on the OpenTelemetry SDK for your language. At minimum, configure:\\n \\n \\n```\\nOTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=\\\"https://cloud.langfuse.com/api/public/otel\\\"\"}], \"type\": \"content\"}}, {\"type\": \"document\", \"record_type\": \"documentation\", \"url\": \"https://langfuse.com/integrations\", \"title\": \"Overview\", \"source\": {\"content\": [{\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\n * [30votesLivekit integrationNikoLandgraf•1/27/2025•12Done](https://github.com/orgs/langfuse/discussions/5235)\\n * [22votesClaude Code Integrationmarcklingen•9/11/2025•5Done](https://github.com/orgs/langfuse/discussions/9088)\\n * [21votesTruefoundry Integrationeeshan-d•7/30/2025•2Done](https://github.com/orgs/langfuse/discussions/8202)\\n * [21votesSupport OpenTelemetry-based instrumentation (openllmetry and others)gyliu513•7/1/2024•17Done](https://github.com/orgs/langfuse/discussions/2509)\\n * [20votesLlamaIndex integration (Python)marcklingen•1/6/2024•7Done](https://github.com/orgs/langfuse/discussions/828)\\n * Previous\\n * 1\\n * 2\\n * More pages\\n * 8\\n * Next\\nDiscussions last updated: 9/1/2026, 8:17:44 AM (1 hour ago)\\n* * *\\n* * *\\nLast edited 8/31/2026\\n\"}], \"type\": \"content\"}}, {\"type\": \"document\", \"record_type\": \"github_issue\", \"url\": \"https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse/issues/8173\", \"title\": \"bug: AsyncStream' object has no attribute 'usage' when integrated with Semantic Kernel and Openlit\", \"source\": {\"content\": [{\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"Github Issue by @ssubburaj2301 created on July 28, 2025. The current state of the issue is: open\\n\\n### Describe the bug\\n\\nAsyncStream' object has no attribute 'usage' when integrated with Semantic Kernel and Openlit\\nWhen integrating Semantic Kernel's OpenAIChatCompletion with Langfuse and OpenLIT, an error occurs during streaming calls using invoke_stream(). The kernel expects a usage attribute on the returned response, but receives an AsyncStream generator instead, causing an AttributeError.\\n\\nError: (\\\"<class 'semantic_kernel.connectors.ai.open_ai.services.open_ai_chat_completion.OpenAIChatCompletion'> service failed to complete the prompt\\\", AttributeError(\\\"'AsyncStream' object has no attribute 'usage'\\\"))\\n\\nopenlit.init(tracer=langfuse._otel_tracer, disable_batch=False)\\n\\n<img width=\\\"1113\\\" height=\\\"745\\\" alt=\\\"Image\\\" src=\\\"https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8ba436e1-b914-4d19-86e9-d9ae7ea566e8\\\" />\\n\\n\\n### To reproduce\\n\\n# Initialize Langfuse client\\nlangfuse = Langfuse(\\n secret_key=os.getenv(\\\"LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY\\\",\\\"\\\"),\\n public_key=os.getenv(\\\"LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY\\\",\\\"\\\"),\\n host=os.getenv(\\\"LANGFUSE_HOST\\\",\\\"\\\")\\n)\\nLANGFUSE_AUTH = base64.b64encode(\\n f\\\"{os.environ.get('LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY')}:{os.environ.get('LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY')}\\\".encode()\\n).decode()\\n\\nos.environ[\\\"OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT\\\"] = os.environ.get(\\\"LANGFUSE_HOST\\\") + \\\"/api/public/otel\\\"\\nos.environ[\\\"OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS\\\"] = f\\\"Authorization=Basic {LANGFUSE_AUTH}\\\"\\nos.environ[\\\"OPENAI_API_KEY\\\"] = os.environ.get('AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY',\\\"\\\")\\nos.environ[\\\"OPENAI_CHAT_MODEL_ID\\\"] = \\\"gpt-4o\\\"\\n\\nlangfuse_context = get_client()\\nopenlit.init(tracer=langfuse._otel_tracer, disable_batch=False)\\nkernel_args = KernelArguments(\\n input=rewritten_query,\\n context=context_str,\\n system_prompt=self.system_prompt,\\n max_tokens=800, \\n stream=True\\n )\\n \"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\n result = self.kernel.invoke_stream(\\n plugin_name=\\\"content_recommender_plugin\\\",\\n function_name=\\\"content_recommender_plugin\\\",\\n arguments=kernel_args,\\n )\\nWhen using Semantic Kernel with streaming and Langfuse for tracing, spans are not completed correctly when I commented openlit initiaization openlit.init(tracer=langfuse._otel_tracer) . Without this line, the span does not capture streaming duration, output and multiple POST /api/chat http send spans are created with 0ms latency and empty usage/cost data.\\n\\n\\n {\\n \\\"id\\\": \\\"a1a3d2cbf7844c2d\\\",\\n \\\"traceId\\\": \\\"84277a19d5d23db42eb19a398d54a1c2\\\",\\n \\\"projectId\\\": \\\"cmcme80hi0008mj07a9i8obzb\\\",\\n \\\"type\\\": \\\"SPAN\\\",\\n \\\"environment\\\": \\\"dev\\\",\\n \\\"parentObservationId\\\": null,\\n \\\"startTime\\\": \\\"2025-07-28T21:49:25.280Z\\\",\\n \\\"endTime\\\": \\\"2025-07-28T21:49:25.280Z\\\",\\n \\\"name\\\": \\\"POST /api/chat http send\\\",\\n \\\"metadata\\\": \\\"{}\\\",\\n \\\"level\\\": \\\"DEFAULT\\\",\\n \\\"statusMessage\\\": null,\\n \\\"version\\\": null,\\n \\\"modelParameters\\\": null,\\n \\\"completionStartTime\\\": null,\\n \\\"promptId\\\": null,\\n \\\"createdAt\\\": \\\"2025-07-28T21:49:28.566Z\\\",\\n \\\"updatedAt\\\": \\\"2025-07-28T21:49:28.664Z\\\",\\n \\\"usageDetails\\\": {},\\n \\\"costDetails\\\": {},\\n \\\"providedCostDetails\\\": {},\\n \\\"model\\\": null,\\n \\\"internalModelId\\\": null,\\n \\\"promptName\\\": null,\\n \\\"promptVersion\\\": null,\\n \\\"latency\\\": 0,\\n \\\"timeToFirstToken\\\": null,\\n \\\"inputCost\\\": null,\\n \\\"outputCost\\\": null,\\n \\\"totalCost\\\": 0,\\n \\\"inputUsage\\\": 0,\\n \\\"outputUsage\\\": 0,\\n \\\"totalUsage\\\": 0\\n },\\n\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\n### SDK and container versions\\n\\n_No response_\\n\\n### Additional information\\n\\n_No response_\\n\\n### Are you interested to contribute a fix for this bug?\\n\\nNo\\n---\\nComment #1 by @dosubot[bot]:\\n\\n<!-- Greeting -->\\nHi @ssubburaj2301! I'm [Dosu](https://go.dosu.dev/dosubot) and I’m helping the langfuse team.\\n\\n<!-- Answer -->\\nThe AttributeError occurs because, during streaming with Semantic Kernel and OpenLit, the response object is an AsyncStream generator, which doesn't have a usage attribute. Semantic Kernel expects a usage attribute for cost/usage tracking, but this is typically only present on non-streaming responses.\\n\\nLangfuse relies on the client or integration layer to aggregate and attach usage/cost data at the end of a request. In streaming scenarios, this aggregation doesn't happen automatically—so usage, cost, and latency fields remain empty or zero in Langfuse, and spans may not be completed correctly. This is a known limitation in the current SDK/client integration layer, not in the Langfuse backend itself. The recommended approach is to aggregate usage/cost information after the stream completes and then attach it to the span or observation before closing it. If the integration or wrapper you use doesn't do this, you'll need to implement this aggregation manually or monitor for updates in the SDKs that address this gap.\\n\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\nFor more details on how Langfuse expects usage and cost data to be ingested and why this is most accurate when included in the LLM response, see the documentation on [model usage and cost tracking](https://langfuse.com/docs/model-usage-and-cost). For integration details with Semantic Kernel and OpenLit, see the [integration guide](https://langfuse.com/docs/integrations/semantic-kernel).\\n\\nThere is no backend fix for this; the solution must be implemented in the client or tracing wrapper layer that handles streaming responses and span completion.\\n\\n\\n<!-- Dosu Comment Footer -->\\n*To reply, just mention [@dosu](https://go.dosu.dev/dosubot?utm_source=github&utm_medium=bot-comment&utm_campaign=github-comment-footer-20260415&utm_content=reply-with-mention&utm_term=langfuse%2Flangfuse).*\\n\\n---\\n\\nShare context across your team and agents. #3 by @dosubot[bot]:\\n\\n<!-- Answer -->\\nThis happens because Semantic Kernel’s streaming (with `invoke_stream`) breaks the OpenTelemetry span context: the span is closed before the stream finishes, so usage/cost and output can’t be attached at the right time. Direct OpenAI calls (non-streaming) work because the SDK can aggregate usage/cost and close the span after the response, but with Semantic Kernel streaming, the response is an async generator and the context is lost after the first yield—so even if you wrap with a span, updates after streaming ends don’t reach Langfuse.\\n\\nLangfuse expects all usage/cost data to be attached to the span before it ends. In streaming scenarios, this means you need to aggregate usage/cost as you stream and attach it before the span closes, but the current Python tracing and OpenTelemetry context propagation don’t support this well with async generators or streaming handlers. This is a known limitation and affects not just Semantic Kernel but any async streaming integration using OpenTelemetry and Langfuse ([reference](https://github.com/orgs/langfuse/discussions/7652)).\\n\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\nThere’s no backend fix or post-hoc patching—any workaround must happen in the client or integration layer. Some users manually set token counts or usage/cost attributes on the span before it ends, following Langfuse’s semantic conventions ([reference](https://github.com/orgs/langfuse/discussions/7612)). However, with Semantic Kernel streaming, there’s currently no supported way to update the span after the stream completes.\\n\\nIf you need full usage/cost tracking and span completion, you’ll need to avoid streaming or use direct SDK calls where possible. Otherwise, you can try to manually aggregate usage/cost and set them as span attributes before the span closes, but this is tricky with current async streaming patterns. Langfuse maintainers are aware of this limitation and plan improvements, but for now, this is a known gap ([reference](https://github.com/orgs/langfuse/discussions/7652)).\\n\\n\\n<!-- Dosu Comment Footer -->\\n*To reply, just mention [@dosu](https://go.dosu.dev/dosubot?utm_source=github&utm_medium=bot-comment&utm_campaign=github-comment-footer-20260415&utm_content=reply-with-mention&utm_term=langfuse%2Flangfuse).*\\n\\n---\\n\\nDocs are dead. - Langfuse\\n[Docs](/docs)\\n[Observability](/docs/observability/overview)\\n[SDKs](/docs/observability/sdk/overview)\\n[Instrumentation](/docs/observability/sdk/instrumentation)\\n# Instrumentation\\nThere are two main ways to instrument your application with the Langfuse SDKs:\\n * Using our **[native integrations](/integrations)** for popular LLM and agent libraries such as OpenAI, LangChain or the Vercel AI SDK. They automatically create observations and traces and capture prompts, responses, usage, and errors.\\n * Manually instrumenting your application with the Langfuse SDK. The SDKs provide 3 ways to create observations: \\n * **Context manager**\\n * **Observe wrapper**\\n * **Manual observations**\\nAll approaches are interoperable. You can nest a decorator-created observation inside a context manager or mix manual spans with our [native integrations](/integrations).\\n## Custom instrumentation\\nInstrument your application with the Langfuse SDK using the following methods:\\n### Context manager\\nThe context manager allows you to create a new span and set it as the currently active observation in the OTel context for its duration. All new observations created within this block will automatically be its children.\\nPython SDKJS/TS SDK\\n[`start_as_current_observation()`](https://python.reference.langfuse.com/langfuse#Langfuse.start_as_current_observation) is the primary way to create observations while ensuring the active OpenTelemetry context is updated. Any child observations created inside the `with` block inherit the parent automatically.\\nObservations can have different [types](/docs/observability/features/observation-types) by setting the `as_type` parameter.\\n \\n \\n```\\nfrom langfuse import get_client, propagate_attributes\\nlangfuse = get_client()\\nwith langfuse.start_as_current_observation(\\n as_type=\\\"span\\\",\\n name=\\\"user-request-pipeline\\\",\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\n input={\\\"user_query\\\": \\\"Tell me a joke\\\"},\\n) as root_span:\\n with propagate_attributes(user_id=\\\"user_123\\\", session_id=\\\"session_abc\\\"):\\n with langfuse.start_as_current_observation(\\n as_type=\\\"generation\\\",\\n name=\\\"joke-generation\\\",\\n model=\\\"gpt-4o\\\",\\n ) as generation:\\n generation.update(output=\\\"Why did the span cross the road?\\\")\\n root_span.update(output={\\\"final_joke\\\": \\\"...\\\"})\\n```\\n[`startActiveObservation`](https://langfuse-js-git-main-langfuse.vercel.app/functions/_langfuse_tracing.startActiveObservation.html) accepts a callback, makes the new span active for the callback scope, and ends it automatically, even across async boundaries.\\nObservations can have different [types](/docs/observability/features/observation-types) by setting the `asType` parameter.\\n \\n \\n```\\nimport { startActiveObservation, startObservation } from \\\"@langfuse/tracing\\\";\\nawait startActiveObservation(\\\"user-request\\\", async (span) => {\\n span.update({ input: { query: \\\"Capital of France?\\\" } });\\n const generation = startObservation(\\n \\\"llm-call\\\",\\n { model: \\\"gpt-4\\\", input: [{ role: \\\"user\\\", content: \\\"Capital of France?\\\" }] },\\n { asType: \\\"generation\\\" }\\n );\\n generation.update({ output: { content: \\\"Paris.\\\" } }).end();\\n span.update({ output: \\\"Answered.\\\" });\\n});\\n```\\n### Observe wrapper\\nThe observe decorator is an easy way to automatically capture inputs, outputs, timings, and errors of a wrapped function without modifying the function's internal logic.\\nPython SDKJS/TS SDK\\nUse [`observe()`](https://python.reference.langfuse.com/langfuse#observe) to decorate a function and automatically capture inputs, outputs, timings, and errors.\\nObservations can have different [types](/docs/observability/features/observation-types) by setting the `as_type` parameter.\\n \\n \\n```\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\n// Create a nested span for, e.g., a tool call\\nconst toolCall = span.startObservation(\\n // name\\n \\\"fetch-weather\\\",\\n // params\\n {\\n input: { city: \\\"Paris\\\" },\\n },\\n // Specify observation type in asType\\n // This will type the attributes argument accordingly\\n // Default is 'span'\\n { asType: \\\"tool\\\" }\\n);\\n// Simulate work and end the tool call span\\nawait new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 100));\\ntoolCall.update({ output: { temperature: \\\"15°C\\\" } }).end();\\n// Create a nested generation for the LLM call\\nconst generation = span.startObservation(\\n \\\"llm-call\\\",\\n {\\n model: \\\"gpt-4\\\",\\n input: [{ role: \\\"user\\\", content: \\\"What is the capital of France?\\\" }],\\n },\\n { asType: \\\"generation\\\" }\\n);\\ngeneration.update({\\n usageDetails: { input: 10, output: 5 },\\n output: { content: \\\"The capital of France is Paris.\\\" },\\n});\\ngeneration.end();\\n// End the root span\\nspan.update({ output: \\\"Successfully answered user request.\\\" }).end();\\n```\\nManual Ending Required\\nIf you use [`startObservation()`](https://langfuse-js-git-main-langfuse.vercel.app/functions/_langfuse_tracing.startObservation.html), you are responsible for calling [`.end()`](https://langfuse-js-git-main-langfuse.vercel.app/classes/_langfuse_tracing.LangfuseSpan.html#end) on the returned observation object. Failure to do so will result in incomplete or missing observations in Langfuse.\\n## Nesting observations\\nThe Langfuse SDKs methods automatically handle the nesting of observations.\\nPython SDKJS/TS SDK\\n **Observe Decorator**\\nIf you use the observe wrapper, the function call hierarchy is automatically captured and reflected in the trace.\\n \\n \\n```\\nfrom langfuse import observe\\n@observe\\ndef my_data_processing_function(data, parameter):\\n # ... processing logic ...\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\n with propagate_attributes(\\n user_id=user_id,\\n session_id=session_id,\\n metadata={\\\"pipeline\\\": \\\"main\\\"}\\n ):\\n # All nested @observe functions inherit these attributes\\n result = call_llm()\\n return result\\n@observe()\\ndef call_llm():\\n # This automatically has user_id, session_id, metadata from parent\\n pass\\n```\\nUse [`propagateAttributes()`](https://langfuse-js-git-main-langfuse.vercel.app/functions/_langfuse_tracing.propagateAttributes.html) to add attributes to observations.\\n \\n \\n```\\nimport { startActiveObservation, propagateAttributes, startObservation } from \\\"@langfuse/tracing\\\";\\nawait startActiveObservation(\\\"user-workflow\\\", async () => {\\n await propagateAttributes(\\n {\\n userId: \\\"user_123\\\",\\n sessionId: \\\"session_abc\\\",\\n metadata: { experiment: \\\"variant_a\\\", env: \\\"prod\\\" },\\n version: \\\"1.0\\\",\\n traceName: \\\"user-workflow\\\",\\n },\\n async () => {\\n const generation = startObservation(\\\"llm-call\\\", { model: \\\"gpt-4\\\" }, { asType: \\\"generation\\\" });\\n generation.end();\\n }\\n );\\n});\\n```\\nNote on Attribute Propagation\\nWe use Attribute Propagation to propagate specific attributes (userId, sessionId, version, tags, metadata, traceName) across all observations in an execution context. We will use all observations with these attributes to calculate attribute-level metrics. Please consider the following when using Attribute Propagation:\\n * Values must be **strings ≤200 characters**\\n * Metadata keys: **Alphanumeric characters only** (no whitespace or special characters)\\n * Call **early in your trace** to ensure all observations are covered. This way you make sure that all Metrics in Langfuse are accurate.\\n * Invalid values are dropped with a warning\\n### Cross-service propagation\"}], \"type\": \"content\"}}]}"}

\"text\", \"text\": \"---\\n\\n[← Back to changelog](/changelog#2024-05-07-prompts-api-and-deployment-labels)\\nMay 7, 2024\\n# Prompt management REST API and deployment labels\\n[Hassieb Pakzad](https://twitter.com/hassiebpakzad)\\nManage prompts via the REST API and add labels to deploy prompts to different environments.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## REST API for prompt management\\n\\n---\\n\\nWe revamped the API for prompt management to allow you to fully manage prompts via the REST API. You can now fetch, create, and update prompts programmatically.\\n\\n---\\n\\nNew endpoints ([API](/docs/api)):\\n\\n---\\n\\n * `GET /api/public/v2/prompts`\\n * `GET /api/public/v2/prompts/{promptName}`\\n * `POST /api/public/v2/prompts`\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Deployment labels for prompts\\n\\n---\\n\\nYou can now add labels to prompts to deploy different versions to different environments. Thereby, you can manage the lifecycle of prompts across different environments, such as development, staging, and production. The latest version is always available under the `latest` label for local development and testing.\\n\\n---\\n\\nSee [prompt management docs](/docs/prompts) for more details.\\n\\n---\\n\\nLast updated on October 7, 2025\\n\\n---\\n\"}], \"type\": \"content\"}}, {\"type\": \"document\", \"record_type\": \"documentation\", \"url\":
