\"github_issue\", \"url\": \"https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse/issues/10511\", \"title\": \"Add REST API and SDK support for deleting prompts and prompt versions\", \"source\": {\"content\": [{\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"Github Issue by @Betensis created on November 16, 2025. The current state of the issue is: closed\\n\\nI use Langfuse prompt management across multiple Langfuse instances. To keep our prompt libraries in sync, I need to remove outdated prompts before importing updated ones. Currently the public API and Python SDK let me create, update and fetch prompts but there is no way to delete them. That makes automated synchronisation impossible.\\n\\nPlease consider adding a DELETE /api/public/v2/prompts/{promptName} endpoint with optional label and version query parameters to remove either an entire prompt, or just a specific version or label. Once available in the API, the Python SDK should expose a corresponding delete_prompt() method.\\n\\nIf you agree with this functionality, I plan to work on a contribution to implement it and submit a pull request.\\n\\n\"}], \"type\": \"content\"}}, {\"type\": \"document\", \"record_type\": \"github_discussion\", \"url\": \"https://github.com/orgs/langfuse/discussions/2684\", \"title\": \"Langfuse batch prompts api should return prompt configs as well\", \"source\": {\"content\": [{\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"Title: Langfuse batch prompts api should return prompt configs as well\\nCategory: Ideas\\nAuthor: @ashutoshsaboo\\nTimestamp: July 19, 2024\\nBody:\\n### Describe the feature or potential improvement\\n\\nCurrently `GET /api/public/v2/prompts` only returns a list of prompts, but doesn't return configs with it. It becomes tough to build applications with it, as the config can contain crucial metadata. For example, if I want a entire list of prompts that apply to a user based on say their country code, and multiple other params which are included in the metadata, then I can't do that. First getting all prompts, and then doing a specific prompt detail lookup `GET /api/public/v2/prompts/{promptName}` will be too costly. \\r\\n\\r\\nCan this be please added? @marcklingen \\n\\n### Additional information\\n\\n_No response_\\nComments:\\n\\n Comment #1 from @marcklingen on July 20, 2024:\\n\\n The `GET /api/public/v2/prompts` by design only returns versions/labels of a specific prompt to map which prompt versions are available. As `config` varies between versions of a prompt and can be large, we did not include it in the response.\\r\\n\\r\\nI understand that being able to filter would be really useful here, what do you think about `GET /api/public/v2/prompts/{promptName}/versions` to fetch all versions of a single prompt including the prompt and config?\\n\\n Replies to comment #1:\\n\\n Reply #1 to comment #1 from marcklingen on July 20, 2024:\\n\\n So let me explain the way we are using prompts DB in langfuse, it is something like this, \\r\\n\\r\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\nThere are a bunch of topics which users can engage with in our product. All these topics are mapped 1:1 to each of their prompts in langfuse. The thing is that such super topics list is too many in number, only subset of such topics(prompts) are shown to each user based on which cohort they belong to. The targeting details, such as which country should a topic be visible in, and so on many other such targeting params are stored in the prompt config in langfuse. \\r\\n\\r\\nSo the way we do is that, we first fetch all possible prompts from langfuse, and then we filter it based on the prompt configs to decide which prompts/topics should actually be shown to the user. \\r\\n\\r\\nIn our prod builds, we only fetch the latest prompts whichever are with \\\"production\\\" label, using `/api/public/v2/prompts?label=development`\\r\\nIn our beta builds, we fetch the latest prompts whichever are with \\\"development\\\" label (a prod prompt is also in development by default for us, based on how we promote prompts), using `/api/public/v2/prompts?label=production`. \\r\\n\\r\\nIn my opinion, for the endpoint `GET /api/public/v2/prompts` whenever a specific label as query param is passed, it would anyways only correspond to a single prompt by design in langfuse (for ex: i can't assign prod label to multiple version of same prompts in LF, similarly i also can't assign development label to multiple versions of the same prompt, this is actually a good design enforcement which simplifies things for us) -- in that case we should also return the prompt configs in the same response. For the default case, where no query label param is passed, we can keep it same as the current case. \\r\\n\\r\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"Regarding your suggestion of `/api/public/v2/prompts/{promptName}/versions`, as explained above, the thing is that we want to avoid multiple redundant calls for various prompts (topics in our case) to LF. It adds to significant latency, we have 100s of prompts in our LF (soon to reach in the order of 1000s), imagine making so many calls to LF - it'd be sheer catastrophic. Beside as I explained earlier given the fact that for a single label only single version corresponds, then why even waste resources, best is to return config in the same response itself! I'm also cool if you want to give the exact same functionality in a separate named endpoint, as long as the functionality is sufficed (I'm not sure why that's needed though). \\r\\n\\r\\nI had one more request if possible for the same `GET /api/public/v2/prompts` endpoint, for all the latest matching prompt versions that it returns based on the query label params that were passed, we should add some sort of lastUpdatedTimestamp in the final response to allow for clients to build their own caching logic on top of it, to reduce redundant calls. This can be added for the entire `GET /api/public/v2/prompts` endpoint, i.e, no need to just add for the case where label query param was passed. I'm sure each prompt version's timestamp is stored in the db anyways, we just have to return it appropriately for the correct matched latest versions based on the request params. Subsequently, we can add a query param timestamp to both the GET /prompts/ and /prompts/{promptName} apis to only return prompts that match timestamp greater than the previous one which client had already fetched for. Timestamp based caching is a very common use-case which many LF consumer clients might need in production at some point or the other (many other saas services provide this for the same reason). \\r\\n\\r\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"I hope that gives you sufficient context now on where I'm coming from? @marcklingen Happy to discuss and provide more details if needed! \\r\\n\\r\\nIt's perfectly okay if lastUpdatedTimestamp comes later on (if in case it needs more changes), but I'd truly appreciate some help with the above one of returning configs in the same request. \\n\\n Reply #2 to comment #1 from marcklingen on July 22, 2024:\\n\\n Hi Marc, just checking if you got a chance to check this^? @marcklingen \\r\\n\\r\\n\\n\\n Reply #3 to comment #1 from marcklingen on August 05, 2024:\\n\\n sorry for the slow response, this was a great read and helped me understand your goals here!\\r\\n\\r\\nlastUpdatedAt was a quick change, added it here: https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse/pull/2820\\r\\n\\r\\nI'm yet unsure about the config, I agree that we could add it to the response especially when a filter is applied. I am just unsure whether a schema that is not stable might be confusing for some folks. Let me think about this again, will try to add to this thread later today.\\r\\n\\r\\nDo you expect the config to be stable across versions of a prompt?\\n\\n Reply #4 to comment #1 from marcklingen on August 05, 2024:\\n\\n No i dont expect stable structure across versions of a prompt - config structure can change across versions, but that shouldn't be an issue right? You can just return the dict as is, and expect clients to transform it to their respective pydantic models on their end? Not sure why you are worried about the schema changing, imo config should be just returned as a dict simply by langfuse, rest the clients can manage on their end if they wish to transform it to any model. \\n\\n Reply #5 to comment #1 from marcklingen on August 05, 2024:\\n\\n Sorry, this was confusing, let me be more clear. Schema changing = config is included in the response when label filter is provided but null otherwise on GET /prompts\\n\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\n Reply #6 to comment #1 from marcklingen on August 05, 2024:\\n\\n Wdyt about returning the last (highest version nunber) config on GET /v2/prompts for each prompt (name)? Thereby the response is consistent no matter how the api is used and this should solve for your use case\\n\\n Reply #7 to comment #1 from marcklingen on August 05, 2024:\\n\\n > Sorry, this was confusing, let me be more clear. Schema changing = config is included in the response when label filter is provided but null otherwise on GET /prompts\\r\\n\\r\\nI don't think this is an issue at all tbh. This can be clearly documented in langfuse api docs, that it won't return config when label filter is not provided - and I think it's the right design decision as well, many providers have such a design especially when they have query filter based apis etc. I don't think this is an \\\"inconsistent\\\" api output structure as well, as config would be clearly demarcated as optional in the response api docs - so for non filter based invocations it would return None, whereas for filter based invocations it would return the corresponding config. Personally, I can't think of any practical usecases as well where a user might want to query configs of all the versions of a prompt in a single api call - it doesn't make sense at all logically. So don't think this design decision should hinder any practical usecase in any way. \\r\\n\\r\\n> Wdyt about returning the last (highest version nunber) config on GET /v2/prompts for each prompt (name)? Thereby the response is consistent no matter how the api is used and this should solve for your use case\\r\\n\\r\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"Even if you return the latest version, the issue would be that I would have to query config for that specific version number. Which is costly for me, because of the number of prompts that we have stored in Langfuse. I don't think this would be scalable. My usecase would require getting configs along with prompt names for the mentioned query label filter param. If you are worried about changing structure of the existing endpoint, you can always create a new endpoint which suffices for the same usecases, but still returns configs as well in the same output (if you ask me, creating a new endpoint just for something this trivial would be extremely overkill imo), rather than forcing user to call LF APIs to get config for each prompt one at a time. The latter is not great design and not scalable for clients. Imagine if a product has an extremely high DAU, and each time we are forced to query LF so many times for each prompt to get the config. The number of LF API calls would go through the roof, and cause downtime wherever LF is deployed. \\r\\n\\n\\n Reply #8 to comment #1 from marcklingen on August 05, 2024:\\n\\n Okay, I believe I have landed on a good implementation.\\r\\n\\r\\nThe `GET /v2/prompts` endpoint always returns the `lastConfig` for each prompt. If no filters are provided, it returns the last configuration for each prompt. If you add a filter (such as label or version), it returns the configuration for each prompt with the given filter.\\r\\n\\r\\nThe relevant pull request is available here: https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse/pull/2824\\r\\n\\r\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"Could you confirm that this implementation addresses your use case? You will be able to retrieve all configurations for a given prompt label via the paginated `GET /v2/prompts` endpoint.\\n\\n Reply #9 to comment #1 from marcklingen on August 05, 2024:\\n\\n @ashutoshsaboo aiming to merge the PR later today or tomorrow, feel free to share any feedback you might have, hope this solves for your use case (which sounds really exciting)!\\n\\n Reply #10 to comment #1 from marcklingen on August 06, 2024:\\n\\n @marcklingen just replied on your linked PR. First up, thanks a bunch for all your prompt responses above. I truly appreciate it! 😄 \\r\\n\\r\\nOne additional suggestion, is it possible to add a date filter query param to the above api (which relies on the same lastUpdatedDate for each prompt)? Basically if say the client passes, `?datetime=<5th august 2024, 11:50:50 hrs (in either epoch timestamp/datetime format however you persist it in LF's Postgres)>`, then essentially LF should only return matching prompts which were last updated on or after the above timestamp. Similarly if `?datetime=xyz&label=production` is passed, then it should retrieve only the prod prompts which were last updated >= xyz timestamp whichever was passed. I.e, the datetime query filter should work with other already existing filters - label/version/both whichever the client might want to pass. I believe once this is added, this should make it feasible for almost any high-scale prod usecase to be easily built on top of LF prompts. 😄 \\r\\n\\r\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"The idea is to cache prompts locally on the client (which we already do with our existing system, where we mange all our prompts before we move to LF), and not invoke LF unnecessarily for the already fetched prompts. Again to give you clarity - the major constraint is that, because this is going to be invoked for each user - so at extremely high DAU/concurrent calls, even the best of LF deployments can have major down-times (plus, why to really query Postgres unnecessarily when it's not even needed!). I thought of mentioning this here, rather than in the PR as I wasn't aware if you'd want this to be part of the same PR, or if you would want a separate PR for the same. \\n\\n Reply #11 to comment #1 from marcklingen on August 06, 2024:\\n\\n thanks, added this to the pr\\n\\n Reply #12 to comment #1 from marcklingen on August 06, 2024:\\n\\n merged, thanks again for your feedback here!\\n\\n Reply #13 to comment #1 from marcklingen on August 06, 2024:\\n\\n 🚀 🚀 \\n\\n Comment #2 from @ashutoshsaboo on August 05, 2024:\\n\\n Hey I'll check the PR tomorrow. Thanks!\\r\\n\\r\\nOn Mon, Aug 5, 2024 at 20:30 Marc Klingen ***@***.***> wrote:\\r\\n\\r\\n> @ashutoshsaboo <https://github.com/ashutoshsaboo> aiming to merge the PR\\r\\n> later today or tomorrow, feel free to share any feedback you might have,\\r\\n> hope this solves for your use case (which sounds really exciting)!\\r\\n>\\r\\n> —\\r\\n> Reply to this email directly, view it on GitHub\\r\\n> <https://github.com/orgs/langfuse/discussions/2684#discussioncomment-10244278>,\\r\\n> or unsubscribe\\r\\n> <https://github.com/notifications/unsubscribe-auth/ACLRHEKAVINIVAZSXQA2NKDZP6HRBAVCNFSM6AAAAABLEJGXRWVHI2DSMVQWIX3LMV43URDJONRXK43TNFXW4Q3PNVWWK3TUHMYTAMRUGQZDOOA>\\r\\n> .\\r\\n> You are receiving this because you were mentioned.Message ID:\\r\\n> ***@***.***>\\r\\n>\\r\\n\\n\\n Comment #3 from @ashutoshsaboo on August 21, 2024:\\n\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \" Hey @marcklingen , one follow up thing related to the above - one sort of a bit (major) miss that I see in Langfuse is that anyone can promote prompts to prod (like even non admins can promote prompts to prod). Ideally there should be an access control mechanism to only allow \\\"admins\\\" to promote prompts to prod. Else it can be a bit too risky. I might want to grant access to multiple people to play around with our data in Langfuse, but promoting things to prod and such critical access mechanisms should probably only be reserved for select members, be it admins or a new role. \\r\\n\\r\\nWhat do you think? Can this be added please? \\n\\n Replies to comment #3:\\n\\n Reply #1 to comment #3 from ashutoshsaboo on September 06, 2024:\\n\\n This is great feedback, can you create a new idea thread for this? https://langfuse.com/ideas\\r\\n\\r\\nWe plan to add more customizable role-based access control and this seems to be a great use-case here.\\n\"}], \"type\": \"content\"}}, {\"type\": \"document\", \"record_type\": \"documentation\", \"url\": \"https://api.reference.langfuse.com\", \"title\": \"GET /api/public/projects\", \"source\": {\"content\": [{\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"## GET /api/public/projects\\n\\n`projects_get`\\n\\nGet Project associated with API key (requires project-scoped API key). You can use GET /api/public/organizations/projects to get all projects with an organization-scoped key.\\n\\n> Example responses\\n\\n> 200 Response\\n\\n```json\\n{\\n \\\"data\\\": [\\n {\\n \\\"id\\\": \\\"string\\\",\\n \\\"metadata\\\": {},\\n \\\"name\\\": \\\"string\\\",\\n \\\"organization\\\": {\\n \\\"id\\\": \\\"string\\\",\\n \\\"name\\\": \\\"string\\\"\\n },\\n \\\"retentionDays\\\": 0\\n }\\n ]\\n}\\n```\\n\\n### Responses\\n\\n|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|\\n|---|---|---|---|\\n|200|[OK](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7231#section-6.3.1)|none|[Projects](#schemaprojects)|\\n|400|[Bad Request](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7231#section-6.5.1)|none|Inline|\\n|401|[Unauthorized](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7235#section-3.1)|none|Inline|\\n|403|[Forbidden](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7231#section-6.5.3)|none|Inline|\\n|404|[Not Found](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7231#section-6.5.4)|none|Inline|\\n|405|[Method Not Allowed](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7231#section-6.5.5)|none|Inline|\\n\\n#### Response Schema\\n\\nTo perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:\\nBasicAuth\\n\"}], \"type\": \"content\"}}, {\"type\": \"document\", \"record_type\": \"documentation\", \"url\": \"https://langfuse.com/docs/prompt-management/get-started\", \"title\": \"Get Started with Prompt Management\", \"source\": {\"content\": [{\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"Get Started - Langfuse\\n[Docs](/docs)\\n[Prompt Management](/docs/prompt-management/overview)\\n[Get Started](/docs/prompt-management/get-started)\\n# Get Started with Prompt Management\\nThis guide walks you through creating and using a prompt with Langfuse. If you're looking to understand what prompt management is and why it matters, check out the [Prompt Management Overview](/docs/prompt-management/overview) first. For details on how prompts are structured in Langfuse and how it works in the background, see [Core Concepts](/docs/prompt-management/data-model).\\n## Agentic installation\\nInstall the [Langfuse Agent Skill](https://github.com/langfuse/skills) to let your coding agent access all Langfuse features.\\nAsk your coding agentCursor pluginManual installation\\nAsk your coding agent to install the skill by pointing to the [GitHub repository](https://github.com/langfuse/skills) and instruct it to migrate your prompts.\\nAgent instruction\\n \\n \\n```\\nInstall the Langfuse Agent Skill from github.com/langfuse/skills\\nand use it to migrate the prompts in this codebase to Langfuse.\\n```\\nLangfuse has a [Cursor Plugin](https://cursor.com/docs/plugins) that includes the skill automatically.\\n[Install Plugin in Cursor\\n](https://cursor.com/marketplace/langfuse)\\nThen prompt your agent:\\nAgent instruction\\n \\n \\n```\\nMigrate the prompts in this codebase to Langfuse.\\n```\\nInstall via npm ([skills CLI](https://www.npmjs.com/package/skills)):\\n \\n \\n```\\nnpx skills add langfuse/skills --skill \\\"langfuse\\\"\\n```\\nIf you want to target a specific agent directly:\\n \\n \\n```\\nnpx skills add langfuse/skills --skill \\\"langfuse\\\" --agent \\\"<agent-id>\\\"\\n```\\nAlternatively you can manually clone the skill\\n+\\n 1. Clone repo somewhere stable\\n \\n \\n```\\ngit clone https://github.com/langfuse/skills.git /path/to/langfuse-skills\\n```\\n 2. Make sure your agent's skills dir exists\\n \\n \\n```\\nmkdir -p /path/to/<agent-skill-root>/skills\\n```\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\n 3. Symlink the skill folder\\n \\n \\n```\\nln -s /path/to/langfuse-skills/skills/langfuse /path/to/<agent-skill-root>/skills/langfuse\\n```\\nThen prompt your agent:\\nAgent instruction\\n \\n \\n```\\nMigrate the prompts in this codebase to Langfuse.\\n```\\n## Manual installation\\nThis guide helps you get started with Langfuse Prompt Management manually.\\n### Get API keys\\n 1. [Create Langfuse account](https://langfuse.com/cloud) or [self-host Langfuse](/self-hosting).\\n 2. Create new API credentials in the project settings.\\n### Create a prompt\\nLangfuse UIPython SDKJS/TS SDKAPIMigrate from existing code\\nUse the Langfuse UI to create a new prompt or update an existing one. You'll need to select the [prompt type](/docs/prompt-management/data-model#text-vs-chat-prompts), you can't change this afterwards.\\n \\n \\n```\\npip install langfuse\\n```\\nAdd your Langfuse credentials as environment variables so the SDK knows which project to create the prompt in.\\n.env\\n \\n \\n```\\nLANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY = \\\"sk-lf-...\\\"\\nLANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY = \\\"pk-lf-...\\\"\\nLANGFUSE_BASE_URL = \\\"https://cloud.langfuse.com\\\" # 🇪🇺 EU region\\n///# Other Langfuse data regions include 🇺🇸 US: https://us.cloud.langfuse.com, 🇯🇵 Japan: https://jp.cloud.langfuse.com and ⚕️ HIPAA: https://hipaa.cloud.langfuse.com\\n```\\nUse the Python SDK to create a new prompt or update an existing one.\\n \\n \\n```\\n///# Create a text prompt\\nlangfuse.create_prompt(\\n name=\\\"movie-critic\\\",\\n type=\\\"text\\\",\\n prompt=\\\"As a {{criticlevel}} movie critic, do you like {{movie}}?\\\",\\n labels=[\\\"production\\\"] ///# optionally, directly promote to production\\n)\\n///# Create a chat prompt\\nlangfuse.create_prompt(\\n name=\\\"movie-critic-chat\\\",\\n type=\\\"chat\\\",\\n prompt=[\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\n { \\\"role\\\": \\\"system\\\", \\\"content\\\": \\\"You are an {{criticlevel}} movie critic\\\" },\\n { \\\"role\\\": \\\"user\\\", \\\"content\\\": \\\"Do you like {{movie}}?\\\" },\\n ],\\n labels=[\\\"production\\\"] ///# optionally, directly promote to production\\n)\\n```\\nIf you already have a prompt with the same `name`, the prompt will be added as a new version.\\n \\n \\n```\\nnpm i @langfuse/client\\n```\\nAdd your Langfuse credentials as environment variables so the SDK knows which project to create the prompt in.\\n.env\\n \\n \\n```\\nLANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY = \\\"sk-lf-...\\\"\\nLANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY = \\\"pk-lf-...\\\"\\nLANGFUSE_BASE_URL = \\\"https://cloud.langfuse.com\\\" # 🇪🇺 EU region\\n///# Other Langfuse data regions include 🇺🇸 US: https://us.cloud.langfuse.com, 🇯🇵 Japan: https://jp.cloud.langfuse.com and ⚕️ HIPAA: https://hipaa.cloud.langfuse.com\\n```\\n \\n \\n```\\nimport { LangfuseClient } from \\\"@langfuse/client\\\";\\nconst langfuse = new LangfuseClient();\\n```\\nUse the JS/TS SDK to create a new prompt or update an existing one.\\n \\n \\n```\\n// Create a text prompt\\nawait langfuse.prompt.create({\\n name: \\\"movie-critic\\\",\\n type: \\\"text\\\",\\n prompt: \\\"As a {{criticlevel}} critic, do you like {{movie}}?\\\",\\n labels: [\\\"production\\\"] // optionally, directly promote to production\\n});\\n// Create a chat prompt\\nawait langfuse.prompt.create({\\n name: \\\"movie-critic-chat\\\",\\n type: \\\"chat\\\",\\n prompt: [\\n { role: \\\"system\\\", content: \\\"You are an {{criticlevel}} movie critic\\\" },\\n { role: \\\"user\\\", content: \\\"Do you like {{movie}}?\\\" },\\n ],\\n labels: [\\\"production\\\"] // optionally, directly promote to production\\n});\\n```\\nIf you already have a prompt with the same `name`, the prompt will be added as a new version.\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\nUse the [Public API](https://api.reference.langfuse.com/#tag/prompts/post/api/public/v2/prompts) to create a new prompt or update an existing one.\\n \\n \\n```\\ncurl -X POST \\\"https://cloud.langfuse.com/api/public/v2/prompts\\\" \\\\\\n -u \\\"your-public-key:your-secret-key\\\" \\\\\\n -H \\\"Content-Type: application/json\\\" \\\\\\n -d '{\\n \\\"type\\\": \\\"chat\\\",\\n \\\"name\\\": \\\"movie-critic\\\",\\n \\\"prompt\\\": [\\n { \\\"role\\\": \\\"system\\\", \\\"content\\\": \\\"You are an {{criticlevel}} movie critic\\\" },\\n { \\\"role\\\": \\\"user\\\", \\\"content\\\": \\\"Do you like {{movie}}?\\\" }\\n ]\\n }'\\n```\\n[\\n### API Reference\\n](https://api.reference.langfuse.com/#tag/prompts/POST/api/public/v2/prompts)\\nIf you have prompts in your existing codebase, you can migrate them to Langfuse programmatically.\\n **Using the Langfuse Skill**\\n 1. Install the [Langfuse Skill](https://github.com/langfuse/skills):\\n \\n \\n```\\n///# Cursor plugin\\n/add-plugin langfuse\\n///# skills CLI\\nnpx skills add langfuse/skills --skill \\\"langfuse\\\"\\n///# Manual: clone and symlink\\ngit clone https://github.com/langfuse/skills.git /path/to/langfuse-skills\\nln -s /path/to/langfuse-skills/skills/langfuse ~/.skills/langfuse\\n```\\n 2. Ask the agent to migrate your prompts:\\n \\n \\n```\\nMigrate the hardcoded prompts in this codebase to Langfuse prompt management.\\n```\\n **Using the API**\\nYou can write a script that reads your existing prompts and creates them in Langfuse using the [Public API](https://api.reference.langfuse.com/#tag/prompts/post/api/public/v2/prompts). This is ideal for bulk migrations or CI/CD integration.\\n[\\n### API Reference\\n](https://api.reference.langfuse.com/#tag/prompts/POST/api/public/v2/prompts)\\nThings to look out for\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\n * Langfuse uses a specific syntax for [variables, prompt references, and message placeholders](/docs/prompt-management/data-model#dynamic-rendering-of-prompts). Make sure to update your prompts to use the correct format, if you want to use Langfuse's dynamic rendering capabilities.\\n### Use the prompt in your code\\nAt runtime, you can fetch the prompt from Langfuse. We recommend using the `production` label to fetch the version intentionally chosen for production. Learn more about control (versions/labels) [here](/docs/prompt-management/features/prompt-version-control).\\nPython SDKJS/TS SDKAPIOpenAI SDK (Python)OpenAI SDK (JS/TS)Langchain (Python)Langchain (JS)Vercel AI SDK\\n \\n \\n```\\nfrom langfuse import get_client\\n///# Initialize Langfuse client\\nlangfuse = get_client()\\n```\\nBelow are code examples for both a text type prompt and a chat type prompt. Learn more about prompt types [here](/docs/prompt-management/data-model#text-vs-chat-prompts).\\n **Text prompt**\\n \\n \\n```\\n///# By default, the production version is fetched.\\nprompt = langfuse.get_prompt(\\\"movie-critic\\\")\\n///# Insert variables into prompt template\\ncompiled_prompt = prompt.compile(criticlevel=\\\"expert\\\", movie=\\\"Dune 2\\\")\\n///# -> \\\"As an expert movie critic, do you like Dune 2?\\\"\\n```\\n **Chat prompt**\\n \\n \\n```\\n///# By default, the production version of a chat prompt is fetched.\\nchat_prompt = langfuse.get_prompt(\\\"movie-critic-chat\\\", type=\\\"chat\\\") ///# type arg infers the prompt type (default is 'text')\\n///# Insert variables into chat prompt template\\ncompiled_chat_prompt = chat_prompt.compile(criticlevel=\\\"expert\\\", movie=\\\"Dune 2\\\")\\n///# -> [{\\\"role\\\": \\\"system\\\", \\\"content\\\": \\\"You are an expert movie critic\\\"}, {\\\"role\\\": \\\"user\\\", \\\"content\\\": \\\"Do you like Dune 2?\\\"}]\\n```\\n \\n \\n```\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\nimport { LangfuseClient } from \\\"@langfuse/client\\\";\\n// Initialize the Langfuse client\\nconst langfuse = new LangfuseClient();\\n```\\nBelow are code examples for both a text type prompt and a chat type prompt. Learn more about prompt types [here](/docs/prompt-management/data-model#text-vs-chat-prompts).\\n **Text prompt**\\n \\n \\n```\\n// By default, the production version of a text prompt is fetched.\\nconst prompt = await langfuse.prompt.get(\\\"movie-critic\\\");\\n// Insert variables into prompt template\\nconst compiledPrompt = prompt.compile({\\n criticlevel: \\\"expert\\\",\\n movie: \\\"Dune 2\\\",\\n});\\n// -> \\\"As an expert movie critic, do you like Dune 2?\\\"\\n```\\n **Chat prompt**\\n \\n \\n```\\n// By default, the production version of a chat prompt is fetched.\\nconst chatPrompt = await langfuse.prompt.get(\\\"movie-critic-chat\\\", {\\n type: \\\"chat\\\",\\n}); // type option infers the prompt type (default is 'text')\\n// Insert variables into chat prompt template\\nconst compiledChatPrompt = chatPrompt.compile({\\n criticlevel: \\\"expert\\\",\\n movie: \\\"Dune 2\\\",\\n});\\n// -> [{\\\"role\\\": \\\"system\\\", \\\"content\\\": \\\"You are an expert movie critic\\\"}, {\\\"role\\\": \\\"user\\\", \\\"content\\\": \\\"Do you like Dune 2?\\\"}]\\n```\\nUse the [Public API](https://api.reference.langfuse.com/#tag/prompts/get/api/public/v2/prompts/%7BpromptName%7D) to fetch a prompt at runtime. By default, the prompt labeled `production` is returned.\\n \\n \\n```\\ncurl \\\"https://cloud.langfuse.com/api/public/v2/prompts/movie-critic?label=production\\\" \\\\\\n -u \\\"your-public-key:your-secret-key\\\"\\n```\\nFor fetching a specific version instead of a label:\\n \\n \\n```\\ncurl \\\"https://cloud.langfuse.com/api/public/v2/prompts/movie-critic?version=1\\\" \\\\\\n -u \\\"your-public-key:your-secret-key\\\"\\n```\\n[\\n### API Reference\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\nBelow are code examples for both a text type prompt and a chat type prompt. {"type": "text", "text": "{\"content\": [{\"type\": \"document\", \"record_type\": \"documentation\", \"url\": \"https://langfuse.com/docs/api-and-data-platform/features/scores-api\", \"title\": \"Scores API\", \"source\": {\"content\": [{\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"Scores API - Langfuse\\n[Docs](/docs)\\n[API & Data Platform](/docs/api-and-data-platform/overview)\\n[Features](/docs/api-and-data-platform/features/agent-skill)\\n[Scores API](/docs/api-and-data-platform/features/scores-api)\\n# Scores API\\nThe Scores API allows you to retrieve score data (evaluations, annotations, and API-ingested scores) from Langfuse for use in custom workflows, evaluation pipelines, and analytics.\\nIf you need aggregated score metrics (e.g., average scores grouped by trace name, user, or time period) rather than individual scores, the [Metrics API](/docs/metrics/features/metrics-api) is designed for this and avoids the need to fetch and aggregate raw data yourself.\\nFor general information about API authentication, base URLs, and SDK access, see the [Public API documentation](/docs/api-and-data-platform/features/public-api).\\nThis page covers reading scores. Scores are created via `POST /api/public/scores` or the SDK helpers; see [scores via API/SDK](/docs/evaluation/evaluation-methods/scores-via-sdk). The deprecated `GET /api/public/scores` and `GET /api/public/v2/scores` read endpoints are documented, with migration steps, in [Migration of deprecated APIs](/faq/all/deprecated-api-migration#scores).\\n## Scores API v3\\nWhere is this feature available?\\n * Hobby\\nAvailable\\n * Core\\nAvailable\\n * Pro\\nAvailable\\n * Enterprise\\nAvailable\\n * Self Hosted\\nLangfuse v3.179.0+\\n \\n \\n```\\nGET /api/public/v3/scores\\n```\\nResponses carry a single typed `value` field, and results are paginated with a cursor.\\n### `value` Field\\nEvery score carries exactly one `value`. Its type is determined by the score's `dataType`:\\n`dataType`| `value` type| Notes \\n---|---|--- \\n`NUMERIC`| number| \\n`BOOLEAN`| boolean| \\n`CATEGORICAL`| string| The category \\n`TEXT`| string| \\n`CORRECTION`| string| Empty string if no correction \\n \\nIf your pipeline handles mixed score types, branch on `dataType`.\\n### Field Groups\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"Responses always include a lean core (`id`, `projectId`, `name`, `value`, `dataType`, `source`, `timestamp`, `environment`, `createdAt`, `updatedAt`), and you opt into additional groups via a comma-separated `fields` parameter:\\n \\n \\n```\\n?fields=details,subject,annotation\\n```\\nGroup| Fields \\n---|--- \\ncore| Always included (see above) \\n`details`| comment, configId, metadata \\n`subject`| subject (the entity the score is attached to, see below) \\n`annotation`| authorUserId, queueId \\n \\nUnknown group names return HTTP 400.\\n### `subject` Object\\nEvery score is attached to exactly one entity. Request the `subject` field group to see which one; it is discriminated by `kind`:\\n \\n \\n```\\n{ \\\"kind\\\": \\\"observation\\\", \\\"id\\\": \\\"obs-1\\\", \\\"traceId\\\": \\\"trace-1\\\" }\\n```\\n * `kind: \\\"trace\\\"`: `id` is the trace ID\\n * `kind: \\\"observation\\\"`: `id` is the observation ID; includes the parent `traceId`\\n * `kind: \\\"session\\\"`: `id` is the session ID\\n * `kind: \\\"experiment\\\"`: `id` is the dataset run ID\\n### Cursor-Based Pagination\\n 1. Make your initial request with a `limit` parameter (default 50, max 100)\\n 2. If more results exist, the response includes a `cursor` in the `meta` object\\n 3. Pass this cursor via the `cursor` parameter in your next request, repeating the same filter parameters as the initial request (the cursor encodes only the read position, not your query)\\n 4. Repeat until no cursor is returned (you've reached the end)\\nFor recurring full exports to your data warehouse, use the [scheduled blob storage export](/docs/api-and-data-platform/features/export-to-blob-storage) instead of paginating through the API.\\n### Filtering\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"`experimentId`| string| Comma-separated list of dataset run IDs (experiment IDs). Mutually exclusive with `traceId`, `sessionId`, `observationId` \\n`fromTimestamp`| datetime| Inclusive lower bound on the score timestamp \\n`toTimestamp`| datetime| Exclusive upper bound on the score timestamp \\n \\n### Sample Response\\nWith `fields=details,subject,annotation`:\\n \\n \\n```\\n{\\n \\\"data\\\": [\\n {\\n \\\"id\\\": \\\"score-1\\\",\\n \\\"projectId\\\": \"https://langfuse.com/docs/evaluation/evaluation-methods/scores-via-sdk\", \"title\": \"Scores via API/SDK\", \"source\": {\"content\": [{\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"Scores via API/SDK - Langfuse\\n[Docs](/docs)\\n[Evaluation](/docs/evaluation/overview)\\n[Evaluation Methods](/docs/evaluation/evaluation-methods/llm-as-a-judge)\\n[Scores via API/SDK](/docs/evaluation/evaluation-methods/scores-via-sdk)\\n# Scores via API/SDK\\nYou can use the Langfuse SDKs or API to add [scores](/docs/evaluation/scores/overview) to traces, observations, sessions and dataset runs. This is an evaluation method that allows you to set up custom evaluation workflows and extend the scoring capabilities of Langfuse. See the [data model](/docs/evaluation/scores/data-model#scores) for full details on the score object.\\nIf you want Langfuse to run deterministic Python or TypeScript logic for you, use [code evaluators](/docs/evaluation/evaluation-methods/code-evaluators). Use this page when your application, pipeline, or CI job computes scores and sends them to Langfuse via API or SDK.\\n## Ingesting Scores via API/SDKs\\nScores can be attached at different levels of granularity: to individual traces, to specific observations within a trace, or to full sessions.\\nSee the [API reference](/docs/api) for full details on the POST and GET endpoints for scores and score configs.\\n### Trace or Observation-level Scores\\nYou can add scores via the Langfuse SDKs or API. Scores can take one of four data types: **Numeric** , **Categorical** , **Boolean** , or **Text**. See [Score Types](/docs/evaluation/scores/overview#score-types) for details.\\nIf a score is ingested manually using a `trace_id` to link the score to a trace, it is not necessary to wait until the trace has been created. The score will show up in the scores table and will be linked to the trace once the trace with the same `trace_id` is created.\\nHere are examples by `Score` data types.\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\nFor trace and observation scores, `trace_id`/`traceId` is required and `observation_id`/`observationId` is optional. If you attach a score to an observation, always provide both the observation ID and the corresponding trace ID.\\nPython SDKJS/TS SDKAPI\\nNumericCategoricalBooleanText\\nNumeric score values must be provided as float.\\n \\n \\n```\\nfrom langfuse import get_client\\nlangfuse = get_client()\\n///# Method 1: Score via low-level method\\nlangfuse.create_score(\\n name=\\\"correctness\\\",\\n value=0.9,\\n trace_id=\\\"trace_id_here\\\",\\n observation_id=\\\"observation_id_here\\\", ///# optional\\n data_type=\\\"NUMERIC\\\", ///# optional, inferred if not provided\\n comment=\\\"Factually correct\\\", ///# optional\\n)\\n///# Method 2: Score current span/generation (within context)\\nwith langfuse.start_as_current_observation(as_type=\\\"span\\\", name=\\\"my-operation\\\") as span:\\n # Score the current span\\n span.score(\\n name=\\\"correctness\\\",\\n value=0.9,\\n data_type=\\\"NUMERIC\\\",\\n comment=\\\"Factually correct\\\"\\n )\\n # Score the trace\\n span.score_trace(\\n name=\\\"overall_quality\\\",\\n value=0.95,\\n data_type=\\\"NUMERIC\\\"\\n )\\n///# Method 3: Score via the current context\\nwith langfuse.start_as_current_observation(as_type=\\\"span\\\", name=\\\"my-operation\\\"):\\n # Score the current span\\n langfuse.score_current_span(\\n name=\\\"correctness\\\",\\n value=0.9,\\n data_type=\\\"NUMERIC\\\",\\n comment=\\\"Factually correct\\\"\\n )\\n # Score the trace\\n langfuse.score_current_trace(\\n name=\\\"overall_quality\\\",\\n value=0.95,\\n data_type=\\\"NUMERIC\\\"\\n )\\n```\\nCategorical score values must be provided as strings.\\n \\n \\n```\\nfrom langfuse import get_client\\nlangfuse = get_client()\\n///# Method 1: Score via low-level method\\nlangfuse.create_score(\\n name=\\\"accuracy\\\",\\n value=\\\"partially correct\\\",\\n trace_id=\\\"trace_id_here\\\",\\n observation_id=\\\"observation_id_here\\\", ///# optional\\n data_type=\\\"CATEGORICAL\\\", ///# optional, inferred if not provided\\n comment=\\\"Some factual errors\\\", ///# optional\\n)\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\n///# Method 2: Score current span/generation (within context)\\nwith langfuse.start_as_current_observation(as_type=\\\"span\\\", name=\\\"my-operation\\\") as span:\\n # Score the current span\\n span.score(\\n name=\\\"accuracy\\\",\\n value=\\\"partially correct\\\",\\n data_type=\\\"CATEGORICAL\\\",\\n comment=\\\"Some factual errors\\\"\\n )\\n # Score the trace\\n span.score_trace(\\n name=\\\"overall_quality\\\",\\n value=\\\"partially correct\\\",\\n data_type=\\\"CATEGORICAL\\\"\\n )\\n///# Method 3: Score via the current context\\nwith langfuse.start_as_current_observation(as_type=\\\"span\\\", name=\\\"my-operation\\\"):\\n # Score the current span\\n langfuse.score_current_span(\\n name=\\\"accuracy\\\",\\n value=\\\"partially correct\\\",\\n data_type=\\\"CATEGORICAL\\\",\\n comment=\\\"Some factual errors\\\"\\n )\\n # Score the trace\\n langfuse.score_current_trace(\\n name=\\\"overall_quality\\\",\\n value=\\\"partially correct\\\",\\n data_type=\\\"CATEGORICAL\\\"\\n )\\n```\\nBoolean scores must be provided as a float, where `1` is true and `0` is false. When read via the [v3 scores API](https://api.reference.langfuse.com/#tag/scoresv3/GET/api/public/v3/scores), the value is returned as a boolean. See [API reference](/docs/api) for more details on POST/GET scores endpoints.\\n \\n \\n```\\nfrom langfuse import get_client\\nlangfuse = get_client()\\n///# Method 1: Score via low-level method\\nlangfuse.create_score(\\n name=\\\"helpfulness\\\",\\n value=0, ///# 0 or 1\\n trace_id=\\\"trace_id_here\\\",\\n observation_id=\\\"observation_id_here\\\", ///# optional\\n data_type=\\\"BOOLEAN\\\", ///# required, numeric values without data type would be inferred as NUMERIC\\n comment=\\\"Incorrect answer\\\", ///# optional\\n)\\n///# Method 2: Score current span/generation (within context)\\nwith langfuse.start_as_current_observation(as_type=\\\"span\\\", name=\\\"my-operation\\\") as span:\\n # Score the current span\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\n span.score(\\n name=\\\"helpfulness\\\",\\n value=1, ///# 0 or 1\\n data_type=\\\"BOOLEAN\\\",\\n comment=\\\"Very helpful response\\\"\\n )\\n # Score the trace\\n span.score_trace(\\n name=\\\"overall_quality\\\",\\n value=1, ///# 0 or 1\\n data_type=\\\"BOOLEAN\\\"\\n )\\n///# Method 3: Score via the current context\\nwith langfuse.start_as_current_observation(as_type=\\\"span\\\", name=\\\"my-operation\\\"):\\n # Score the current span\\n langfuse.score_current_span(\\n name=\\\"helpfulness\\\",\\n value=1, ///# 0 or 1\\n data_type=\\\"BOOLEAN\\\",\\n comment=\\\"Very helpful response\\\"\\n )\\n # Score the trace\\n langfuse.score_current_trace(\\n name=\\\"overall_quality\\\",\\n value=1, ///# 0 or 1\\n data_type=\\\"BOOLEAN\\\"\\n )\\n```\\nText score values must be provided as strings between 1 and 500 characters.\\n \\n \\n```\\nfrom langfuse import get_client\\nlangfuse = get_client()\\n///# Method 1: Score via low-level method\\nlangfuse.create_score(\\n name=\\\"reviewer_notes\\\",\\n value=\\\"The response was helpful but could be more concise.\\\",\\n trace_id=\\\"trace_id_here\\\",\\n observation_id=\\\"observation_id_here\\\", ///# optional\\n data_type=\\\"TEXT\\\", ///# optional, inferred if not provided\\n comment=\\\"Reviewed by QA team\\\", ///# optional\\n)\\n///# Method 2: Score current span/generation (within context)\\nwith langfuse.start_as_current_observation(as_type=\\\"span\\\", name=\\\"my-operation\\\") as span:\\n # Score the current span\\n span.score(\\n name=\\\"reviewer_notes\\\",\\n value=\\\"The response was helpful but could be more concise.\\\",\\n data_type=\\\"TEXT\\\",\\n comment=\\\"Reviewed by QA team\\\"\\n )\\n # Score the trace\\n span.score_trace(\\n name=\\\"overall_notes\\\",\\n value=\\\"Good quality overall, minor formatting issues.\\\",\\n data_type=\\\"TEXT\\\"\\n )\\n///# Method 3: Score via the current context\\nwith langfuse.start_as_current_observation(as_type=\\\"span\\\", name=\\\"my-operation\\\"):\\n # Score the current span\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\n langfuse.score_current_span(\\n name=\\\"reviewer_notes\\\",\\n value=\\\"The response was helpful but could be more concise.\\\",\\n data_type=\\\"TEXT\\\",\\n comment=\\\"Reviewed by QA team\\\"\\n )\\n # Score the trace\\n langfuse.score_current_trace(\\n name=\\\"overall_notes\\\",\\n value=\\\"Good quality overall, minor formatting issues.\\\",\\n data_type=\\\"TEXT\\\"\\n )\\n```\\nNumericCategoricalBooleanText\\nNumeric score values must be provided as float.\\n \\n \\n```\\nimport { LangfuseClient } from \\\"@langfuse/client\\\";\\nconst langfuse = new LangfuseClient();\\nlangfuse.score.create({\\n id: \\\"unique_id\\\", // optional, can be used as an idempotency key to update the score subsequently\\n traceId: message.traceId,\\n observationId: message.generationId, // optional\\n name: \\\"correctness\\\",\\n value: 0.9,\\n dataType: \\\"NUMERIC\\\", // optional, inferred if not provided\\n comment: \\\"Factually correct\\\", // optional\\n});\\n// Flush the scores in short-lived environments\\nawait langfuse.flush();\\n```\\nCategorical score values must be provided as strings.\\n \\n \\n```\\nimport { LangfuseClient } from \\\"@langfuse/client\\\";\\nconst langfuse = new LangfuseClient();\\nlangfuse.score.create({\\n id: \\\"unique_id\\\", // optional, can be used as an idempotency key to update the score subsequently\\n traceId: message.traceId,\\n observationId: message.generationId, // optional\\n name: \\\"accuracy\\\",\\n value: \\\"partially correct\\\",\\n dataType: \\\"CATEGORICAL\\\", // optional, inferred if not provided\\n comment: \\\"Factually correct\\\", // optional\\n});\\n// Flush the scores in short-lived environments\\nawait langfuse.flush();\\n```\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\nBoolean scores must be provided as a float, where `1` is true and `0` is false. When read via the [v3 scores API](https://api.reference.langfuse.com/#tag/scoresv3/GET/api/public/v3/scores), the value is returned as a boolean. See [API reference](/docs/api) for more details on POST/GET scores endpoints.\\n \\n \\n```\\nimport { LangfuseClient } from \\\"@langfuse/client\\\";\\nconst langfuse = new LangfuseClient();\\nlangfuse.score.create({\\n id: \\\"unique_id\\\", // optional, can be used as an idempotency key to update the score subsequently\\n traceId: message.traceId,\\n observationId: message.generationId, // optional\\n name: \\\"helpfulness\\\",\\n value: 0, // 0 or 1\\n dataType: \\\"BOOLEAN\\\", // required, numeric values without data type would be inferred as NUMERIC\\n comment: \\\"Incorrect answer\\\", // optional\\n});\\n// Flush the scores in short-lived environments\\nawait langfuse.flush();\\n```\\nText score values must be provided as strings between 1 and 500 characters.\\n \\n \\n```\\nimport { LangfuseClient } from \\\"@langfuse/client\\\";\\nconst langfuse = new LangfuseClient();\\nlangfuse.score.create({\\n id: \\\"unique_id\\\", // optional, can be used as an idempotency key to update the score subsequently\\n traceId: message.traceId,\\n observationId: message.generationId, // optional\\n name: \\\"reviewer_notes\\\",\\n value: \\\"The response was helpful but could be more concise.\\\",\\n dataType: \\\"TEXT\\\", // optional, inferred if not provided\\n comment: \\\"Reviewed by QA team\\\", // optional\\n});\\n// Flush the scores in short-lived environments\\nawait langfuse.flush();\\n```\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\nYou can also create scores directly via the [REST API](https://api.reference.langfuse.com/#tag/legacyscorev1/POST/api/public/scores). Authenticate using HTTP Basic Auth with your Langfuse Public Key as username and Secret Key as password.\\nNumericCategoricalBooleanText\\nNumeric score values must be provided as float.\\n \\n \\n```\\ncurl -X POST https://cloud.langfuse.com/api/public/scores \\\\\\n -u \\\"pk-lf-...\\\":\\\"sk-lf-...\\\" \\\\\\n -H \\\"Content-Type: application/json\\\" \\\\\\n -d '{\\n \\\"traceId\\\": \\\"trace_id_here\\\",\\n \\\"observationId\\\": \\\"observation_id_here\\\",\\n \\\"name\\\": \\\"correctness\\\",\\n \\\"value\\\": 0.9,\\n \\\"dataType\\\": \\\"NUMERIC\\\",\\n \\\"comment\\\": \\\"Factually correct\\\"\\n }'\\n```\\nCategorical score values must be provided as strings.\\n \\n \\n```\\ncurl -X POST https://cloud.langfuse.com/api/public/scores \\\\\\n -u \\\"pk-lf-...\\\":\\\"sk-lf-...\\\" \\\\\\n -H \\\"Content-Type: application/json\\\" \\\\\\n -d '{\\n \\\"traceId\\\": \\\"trace_id_here\\\",\\n \\\"observationId\\\": \\\"observation_id_here\\\",\\n \\\"name\\\": \\\"accuracy\\\",\\n \\\"value\\\": \\\"partially correct\\\",\\n \\\"dataType\\\": \\\"CATEGORICAL\\\",\\n \\\"comment\\\": \\\"Some factual errors\\\"\\n }'\\n```\\nBoolean scores must be provided as a float, where `1` is true and `0` is false. When read via the [v3 scores API](https://api.reference.langfuse.com/#tag/scoresv3/GET/api/public/v3/scores), the value is returned as a boolean.\\n \\n \\n```\\ncurl -X POST https://cloud.langfuse.com/api/public/scores \\\\\\n -u \\\"pk-lf-...\\\":\\\"sk-lf-...\\\" \\\\\\n -H \\\"Content-Type: application/json\\\" \\\\\\n -d '{\\n \\\"traceId\\\": \\\"trace_id_here\\\",\\n \\\"observationId\\\": \\\"observation_id_here\\\",\\n \\\"name\\\": \\\"helpfulness\\\",\\n \\\"value\\\": 0,\\n \\\"dataType\\\": \\\"BOOLEAN\\\",\\n \\\"comment\\\": \\\"Incorrect answer\\\"\\n }'\\n```\\nText score values must be provided as strings between 1 and 500 characters.\\n \\n \\n```\\ncurl -X POST https://cloud.langfuse.com/api/public/scores \\\\\\n -u \\\"pk-lf-...\\\":\\\"sk-lf-...\\\" \\\\\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\n -H \\\"Content-Type: application/json\\\" \\\\\\n -d '{\\n \\\"traceId\\\": \\\"trace_id_here\\\",\\n \\\"observationId\\\": \\\"observation_id_here\\\",\\n \\\"name\\\": \\\"reviewer_notes\\\",\\n \\\"value\\\": \\\"The response was helpful but could be more concise.\\\",\\n \\\"dataType\\\": \\\"TEXT\\\",\\n \\\"comment\\\": \\\"Reviewed by QA team\\\"\\n }'\\n```\\n### Browser score ingestion\\nUse `@langfuse/browser` when the score is created in frontend code, for example thumbs up/down user feedback, star ratings, or client-side quality signals. The browser SDK only needs a Langfuse public key and sends each score immediately via the ingestion API. Do not expose a secret key in browser code.\\nFor backend services, scripts, CI jobs, and evaluation pipelines, use `@langfuse/client` as shown in the JS/TS SDK examples above.\\n \\n \\n```\\nnpm install @langfuse/browser\\n```\\n \\n \\n```\\nimport { LangfuseBrowserClient } from \\\"@langfuse/browser\\\";\\nconst langfuse = new LangfuseBrowserClient({\\n publicKey: process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY!,\\n baseUrl: process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_LANGFUSE_BASE_URL, // optional, defaults to https://cloud.langfuse.com\\n});\\nawait langfuse.score({\\n traceId: message.traceId,\\n observationId: message.generationId, // optional\\n id: `user-feedback-${message.traceId}`, // optional, use as an idempotency key\\n name: \\\"user-feedback\\\",\\n value: 1, // 1 for positive, 0 for negative\\n dataType: \\\"BOOLEAN\\\",\\n comment: \\\"Helpful answer\\\", // optional\\n});\\n```\\n`score()` returns `{ id }` after ingestion succeeds. No `flush()` call is required.\\n### Session-level Scores\\nTo score an entire session (without attaching the score to a trace or observation), provide only `session_id` (Python SDK) or `sessionId` (JS/TS SDK and API).\\nPython SDKJS/TS SDKAPI\\n \\n \\n```\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\nfrom langfuse import get_client\\nlangfuse = get_client()\\nlangfuse.create_score(\\n name=\\\"session_quality\\\",\\n value=0.85,\\n session_id=\\\"session_id_here\\\",\\n data_type=\\\"NUMERIC\\\",\\n comment=\\\"Overall conversation quality\\\"\\n)\\n```\\n \\n \\n```\\nimport { LangfuseClient } from \\\"@langfuse/client\\\";\\nconst langfuse = new LangfuseClient();\\nlangfuse.score.create({\\n name: \\\"session_quality\\\",\\n value: 0.85,\\n sessionId: \\\"session_id_here\\\",\\n dataType: \\\"NUMERIC\\\",\\n comment: \\\"Overall conversation quality\\\",\\n});\\nawait langfuse.flush();\\n```\\n \\n \\n```\\ncurl -X POST https://cloud.langfuse.com/api/public/scores \\\\\\n -u \\\"pk-lf-...\\\":\\\"sk-lf-...\\\" \\\\\\n -H \\\"Content-Type: application/json\\\" \\\\\\n -d '{\\n \\\"sessionId\\\": \\\"session_id_here\\\",\\n \\\"name\\\": \\\"session_quality\\\",\\n \\\"value\\\": 0.85,\\n \\\"dataType\\\": \\\"NUMERIC\\\",\\n \\\"comment\\\": \\\"Overall conversation quality\\\"\\n }'\\n```\\n## Advanced\\n### Preventing Duplicate Scores\\nBy default, Langfuse allows for multiple scores of the same `name` on the same trace. This is useful if you'd like to track the evolution of a score over time or if e.g. you've received multiple user feedback scores on the same trace.\\nIn some cases, you want to prevent this behavior or overwrite an existing score. A score is identified by three fields — its `id`, its `name`, and its date (`toDate(timestamp)`) — and a new score only replaces an existing one when all three match. To achieve this, create an **idempotency key** and pass it as the `id` (JS/TS) / `score_id` (Python) when creating the score (for example `trace_id-score_name`), and keep the `name` and `timestamp` unchanged across calls. If any of the three differs — for example the same `id` with a different `name` — you get an additional score rather than a replacement.\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\nDo not send partial score updates (only the changed fields) and rely on Langfuse to merge them into the existing record. This merge only happens for a limited window after creation, is deprecated, and will be removed. Always send the complete score.\\nSee [How to update traces, observations, and scores](/faq/all/tracing-data-updates#updating-scores) for more details on Langfuse's immutable data model.\\n### Enforcing a Score Config\\nScore configs are helpful when you want to standardize your scores for future analysis.\\nTo enforce a score config, you can provide a `configId` when creating a score to reference a `ScoreConfig` that was previously created. `Score Configs` can be defined in the Langfuse UI or via our API. [See our guide on how to create and manage score configs](/faq/all/manage-score-configs).\\nWhenever you provide a `ScoreConfig`, the score data will be validated against the config. The following rules apply:\\n * **Score Name** : Must equal the config's name\\n * **Score Data Type** : When provided, must match the config's data type\\n * **Score Value when Type is`NUMERIC`**: Value must be within the min and max values defined in the config (if provided, min and max are optional and otherwise are assumed as -∞ and +∞ respectively)\\n * **Score Value when Type is`CATEGORICAL`**: Value must map to one of the categories defined in the config\\n * **Score Value when Type is`BOOLEAN`**: Value must equal `0` or `1`\\n * **Score Value when Type is`TEXT`**: Value must be a non-empty string of at most 500 characters\\nPython SDKJS/TS SDKAPI\\nNumeric ScoresCategorical ScoresBoolean ScoresText Scores\\nWhen ingesting numeric scores, you can provide the value as a float. If you provide a configId, the score value will be validated against the config's numeric range, which might be defined by a minimum and/or maximum value.\\n \\n \\n```\\nfrom langfuse import get_client\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\nlangfuse = get_client()\\n///# Method 1: Score via low-level method\\nlangfuse.create_score(\\n trace_id=\\\"trace_id_here\\\",\\n observation_id=\\\"observation_id_here\\\", ///# optional\\n session_id=\\\"session_id_here\\\", ///# optional, ID of the session the score relates to\\n name=\\\"accuracy\\\",\\n value=0.9,\\n comment=\\\"Factually correct\\\", ///# optional\\n score_id=\\\"unique_id\\\", ///# optional, can be used as an idempotency key to update the score subsequently\\n config_id=\\\"78545-6565-3453654-43543\\\", ///# optional, to ensure that the score follows a specific min/max value range\\n data_type=\\\"NUMERIC\\\" # optional, possibly inferred\\n)\\n///# Method 2: Score within context\\nwith langfuse.start_as_current_observation(as_type=\\\"span\\\", name=\\\"my-operation\\\") as span:\\n span.score(\\n name=\\\"accuracy\\\",\\n value=0.9,\\n comment=\\\"Factually correct\\\",\\n config_id=\\\"78545-6565-3453654-43543\\\",\\n data_type=\\\"NUMERIC\\\"\\n )\\n```\\nCategorical scores are used to evaluate data that falls into specific categories. When ingesting categorical scores, you can provide the value as a string. If you provide a configId, the score value will be validated against the config's categories.\\n \\n \\n```\\nfrom langfuse import get_client\\nlangfuse = get_client()\\n///# Method 1: Score via low-level method\\nlangfuse.create_score(\\n trace_id=\\\"trace_id_here\\\",\\n observation_id=\\\"observation_id_here\\\", ///# optional\\n name=\\\"correctness\\\",\\n value=\\\"correct\\\",\\n comment=\\\"Factually correct\\\", ///# optional\\n score_id=\\\"unique_id\\\", ///# optional, can be used as an idempotency key to update the score subsequently\\n config_id=\\\"12345-6565-3453654-43543\\\", ///# optional, to ensure that the score maps to a specific category defined in a score config\\n data_type=\\\"CATEGORICAL\\\" # optional, possibly inferred\\n)\\n///# Method 2: Score within context\\nwith langfuse.start_as_current_observation(as_type=\\\"span\\\", name=\\\"my-operation\\\") as span:\\n span.score(\\n name=\\\"correctness\\\",\\n value=\\\"correct\\\",\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\n comment=\\\"Factually correct\\\",\\n config_id=\\\"12345-6565-3453654-43543\\\",\\n data_type=\\\"CATEGORICAL\\\"\\n )\\n```\\nWhen ingesting boolean scores, you can provide the value as a float. A re-ingested score overwrites an existing one only when its `id`, `name`, and `timestamp` (at date granularity, `toDate(timestamp)`) all match — a matching `id` alone is not sufficient, and any difference creates a duplicate instead of an update.\\nTo overwrite a score without fetching existing scores first, set a stable `id` as an idempotency key when initially creating the score, and keep the `name` and `timestamp` unchanged on subsequent calls. See Preventing Duplicate Scores for details.\\n## Related guides\\nGuides\\n * [Collecting user feedback\\nCapture explicit and implicit user feedback as scores on your traces, including in-app ratings sent via our Browser SDK.\\n](/guides/user-feedback-loop)\\n * [Custom evaluation data pipeline\\nContinuously monitor quality by fetching traces, running custom evaluations, and ingesting scores back into Langfuse.\\n](/guides/cookbook/example_external_evaluation_pipelines)\\n * [Guardrails and security checks\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\nCheck whether output contains a certain keyword, matches a required structure or format, or exceeds a length limit.\\n](/guides/cookbook/security-and-guardrails)\\n * [Custom internal workflow tooling\\nBuild internal tooling for human-in-the-loop workflows, ingesting scores back into Langfuse following your custom schema.\\n](/guides/human-in-the-loop-scoring)\\n * [Session-level quality tracking\\nScore full conversations, such as support chats or agent threads, by attaching scores via sessionId in the SDK or API.\\n](/guides/cookbook/example_evaluating_multi_turn_conversations)\\n* * *\\n* * *\\nLast edited 7/22/2026\\n\"}], \"type\": \"content\"}}, {\"type\": \"document\", \"record_type\": \"site\", \"url\": \"https://langfuse.com/changelog/2026-06-10-scores-v3-api\", \"title\": \"Scores API v3 - Langfuse\", \"source\": {\"content\": [{\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\n**List filters and value ranges.** Most filters now take comma-separated lists — `id`, `name`, `source`, `dataType`, `environment`, `configId`, `queueId`, `authorUserId`, `traceId`, `sessionId`, `observationId`, and `experimentId` (previously `datasetRunId`). Values within one parameter are OR-ed, parameters are AND-ed: `name=hallucination,toxicity&source=EVAL` returns eval scores named either `hallucination` or `toxicity`. The v2 `operator`/`value` pair is replaced by an exact-match `value` list (for `NUMERIC`, `BOOLEAN`, and `CATEGORICAL` scores) plus `valueMin`/`valueMax` range bounds for numeric scores.\\n\\n---\\n\\n**Selective field retrieval.** Responses always include the core fields — `id`, `projectId`, `name`, `value`, `dataType`, `source`, `timestamp`, `environment`, `createdAt`, and `updatedAt` — and stay lean by default; opt into additional field groups via the `fields` parameter:\\n\\n---\\n\\n \\n \\n```\\nGET /api/public/v3/scores?fields=details,subject,annotation\\n```\\n\\n---\\n\\n * `details` — `comment`, `configId`, `metadata`\\n\\n---\\n\\n * `subject` — what the score is attached to, as a discriminated object (`kind`: `trace`, `observation`, `session`, or `experiment`) replacing v2's flat `traceId`/`observationId`/`sessionId`/`datasetRunId` fields\\n\\n---\\n\\n * `annotation` — `authorUserId`, `queueId`\\n\\n---\\n\"}], \"type\": \"content\"}}, {\"type\": \"document\", \"record_type\": \"documentation\", \"url\": \"https://api.reference.langfuse.com\", \"title\": \"POST /api/public/score-configs\", \"source\": {\"content\": [{\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"## POST /api/public/score-configs\\n\\n`scoreConfigs_create`\\n\\nCreate a score configuration (config). `GET /v2/scores`, `GET /v2/scores/{id}`| `GET /v3/scores`| Scores \\n`GET /datasets/{name}/runs`, `GET /datasets/{name}/runs/{runName}`| `GET /experiments`, then `GET /experiment-items`| Dataset runs \\n`GET /dataset-run-items`| `GET /experiment-items`| Dataset runs \\n`DELETE /datasets/{name}/runs/{runName}`| No direct replacement; `DELETE /traces` removes the underlying trace data| Dataset runs \\n`POST /dataset-run-items`| Experiment runner SDK or `POST /otel/v1/traces` with experiment attributes| Dataset runs \\nTrace and observation events sent to `POST /ingestion`, plus `POST /traces`, `POST /spans`, `POST /generations`, `POST /events`| `POST /otel/v1/traces` (OTLP/HTTP)| Ingestion \\n \\nAll paths are relative to `/api/public`.\\n`score-create` events sent to `POST /ingestion` by the current SDKs are not deprecated. They remain supported after the v4 cutover.\\nIf you access the public API from shell scripts or coding agents, the [Langfuse CLI](/docs/api-and-data-platform/features/cli) provides commands for all supported endpoints. Use at least langfuse-cli version `v1.1.0` to benefit from the new endpoints.\\n### SDK method quick reference\\nThese mappings cover the latest Python SDK v4 and JS/TS SDK v5 method surfaces. The examples use `client` for a Langfuse client instance and `context` for an experiment-action `RunnerContext`. Python exposes the same generated methods asynchronously under `client.async_api`; use the same replacement with `await`. Upgrade within the current major if a replacement is missing: Scores v3 requires Python `4.8.1+` or JS/TS `5.5.0+`, and experiment reads require Python `4.13.1+` or JS/TS `5.10.0+`.\\nArea| Python SDK v4| JS/TS SDK v5 \"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\n---|---|--- \\nObservations| `client.api.legacy.observations_v1.get_many(...)` / `.get(...)` → `client.api.observations.get_many(...)`| `client.api.legacy.observationsV1.getMany(...)` / `.get(...)` and `client.fetchObservation(...)` → `client.api.observations.getMany(...)` \\nTraces| `client.api.trace.list(...)` / `.get(...)` → `client.api.observations.get_many(...)`| `client.api.trace.list(...)` / `.get(...)` and `client.fetchTraces(...)` / `.fetchTrace(...)` → `client.api.observations.getMany(...)` \\nSessions| `client.api.sessions.list(...)` / `.get(...)` → `client.api.observations.get_many(...)`| `client.api.sessions.list(...)` / `.get(...)` and `client.fetchSessions(...)` → `client.api.observations.getMany(...)` \\nMetrics| `client.api.legacy.metrics_v1.metrics(...)` → `client.api.metrics.metrics(...)`. No Python v4 method calls `GET /metrics/daily`.| `client.api.legacy.metricsV1.metrics(...)` → `client.api.metrics.metrics(...)`. No JS/TS v5 method calls `GET /metrics/daily`. \\nScores| `client.api.scores.get_many(...)` / `.get_by_id(...)` → `client.api.scores_v3.get_many_v3(...)`. No Python v4 method reads Scores API v1.| `client.api.scores.getMany(...)` / `.getById(...)` → `client.api.scoresV3.getManyV3(...)`. No JS/TS v5 method reads Scores API v1. \\nDataset reads| `client.api.dataset_run_items.list(...)`, `client.api.datasets.get_runs(...)` / `.get_run(...)`, and `client.get_dataset_runs(...)` / `.get_dataset_run(...)` → `client.api.experiments.list(...)` / `.list_items(...)`| `client.api.datasetRunItems.list(...)`, `client.api.datasets.getRuns(...)` / `.getRun(...)`, and `client.getDatasetRuns(...)` / `.getDatasetRun(...)` → `client.api.experiments.list(...)` / `.listItems(...)` \"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\nThis migration applies only to score reads. Score writes remain supported through `POST /scores` and the current SDK score helpers. The SDKs batch score writes as `score-create` events through `POST /ingestion`; Langfuse v4 continues to accept those events after the cutover. This also covers evaluations created by the experiment runner and third-party integrations that use the current SDK score helpers. No client update or direct REST workaround is required for these score writes.\\n### SDK methods\\nSDK| Deprecated caller| Use instead \\n---|---|--- \\nPython v4| `client.api.scores.get_many(...)`| `client.api.scores_v3.get_many_v3(...)` \\nPython v4| `client.api.scores.get_by_id(score_id)`| `client.api.scores_v3.get_many_v3(id=score_id)` \\nJS/TS v5| `client.api.scores.getMany(...)`| `client.api.scoresV3.getManyV3(...)` \\nJS/TS v5| `client.api.scores.getById(scoreId)`| `client.api.scoresV3.getManyV3({ id: scoreId })` \\n \\nScores v3 requires Python SDK `4.8.1+` or JS/TS SDK `5.5.0+`. It always returns a list response, including when filtering by ID.\\nPython v4 and JS/TS v5 do not expose read wrappers for the v1 `GET /scores` or `GET /scores/{id}` endpoints. Calls to those routes come from direct REST usage or an older SDK. Do not migrate current score-creation helpers merely because they send supported `score-create` events through `/ingestion`.\\n### Parameter mapping\\nDeprecated (v1/v2)| v3 equivalent \\n---|--- \\n`page`| `cursor` (from the previous response's `meta`); `limit` max 100 \\n`GET /scores/{scoreId}`, `GET /v2/scores/{scoreId}`| `id=<scoreId>` filter; there is no get-by-id endpoint in v3 \"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\n`value` \\\\+ `stringValue` (split by type)| Single `value` field, typed by `dataType` \\n`operator` \\\\+ `value` (numeric comparison)| `valueMin` / `valueMax` (inclusive bounds, require `dataType=NUMERIC`) \\n`datasetRunId`| `experimentId` \\n`fromTimestamp`, `toTimestamp`| Unchanged names, but `fromTimestamp` is now inclusive and `toTimestamp` exclusive \\n`userId`, `traceTags`| Removed; for trace-level score questions, use the [Metrics API v2](/docs/metrics/features/metrics-api#v2) score views \\n`filter` (JSON, e.g. metadata conditions)| Removed; for metadata conditions, request `fields=details` and filter on `metadata` client-side \\n`name`, `source`, `dataType`, `environment`, `configId`, `queueId`| Unchanged, and now accept comma-separated lists (OR within a parameter, AND across parameters) \\n \\n### Semantic differences\\n * **One typed`value` field.** `NUMERIC` scores return a number, `BOOLEAN` scores a boolean, and `CATEGORICAL`/`TEXT`/`CORRECTION` scores a string; no more parallel `value`/`stringValue` fields.\\n * **Field groups.** Core fields are always returned; request more via `fields=details,subject,annotation`. The `subject` group replaces the flat `traceId`/`observationId`/`sessionId`/`datasetRunId` response fields with one object describing what the score is attached to (`kind`: `trace`, `observation`, `session`, or `experiment`).\\n * Use at most one of the `traceId`, `sessionId`, and `experimentId` filters; they cannot be combined. `observationId` requires `traceId` alongside it (observation IDs are scoped to a trace).\\n * `fromTimestamp` is inclusive; `toTimestamp` is exclusive.\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"`count`| Count of observations \\n`latency`| Observation duration in milliseconds \\n`totalTokens`| Total tokens used \\n`totalCost`| Total cost \\n`timeToFirstToken`| Time to first token in milliseconds \\n`countScores`| Count of related scores \\n \\n#### Score Dimensions (Common)\\nDimension| Type| Description \\n---|---|--- \\n`id`| string| Score ID \\n`name`| string| Score name \\n`environment`| string| Environment \\n`source`| string| Score source \\n`dataType`| string| Data type \\n`traceId`| string| Related trace ID \\n`traceName`| string| Related trace name \\n`userId`| string| User ID from trace \\n`sessionId`| string| Session ID from trace \\n`observationId`| string| Related observation ID \\n`observationName`| string| Related observation name \\n`observationModelName`| string| Model used in related observation \\n`observationPromptName`| string| Prompt name used in related observation \\n`observationPromptVersion`| string| Prompt version used in related observation \\n`configId`| string| Configuration ID \\n \\n#### Score Metrics\\n##### Numeric Scores\\nMetric| Description \\n---|--- \\n`count`| Count of scores \\n`value`| Numeric score value \\n \\n##### Boolean Scores\\nMetric| Description \\n---|--- \\n`count`| Count of scores \\n`value`| Numeric score value, where `0` is false and `1` is true. Use the `avg` aggregation to return the true rate \\n \\nBoolean scores have an additional dimension:\\nDimension| Type| Description \\n---|---|--- \\n`booleanValue`| boolean| Boolean value of the score for grouping and filtering \\n \\n##### Categorical Scores\\nMetric| Description \\n---|--- \\n`count`| Count of scores \\n \\nCategorical scores have an additional dimension:\\nDimension| Type| Description \\n---|---|--- \\n`stringValue`| string| String value of the categorical score \\n \"}], \"type\": \"content\"}}]}"}

Short answer: Yes. While there’s no native C# SDK, you can use all Langfuse features from .NET via:

  • Tracing/observability: send OpenTelemetry spans to Langfuse’s OTLP/HTTP endpoint
  • Prompt management: use the Public API to create/fetch prompts
  • Evaluations/scores: use the Scores API
  • Dashboards, alerts, datasets/experiments, users/sessions, etc.: work regardless of your backend language

Docs

  • OpenTelemetry to Langfuse (endpoint, attribute mapping): https://langfuse.com/integrations/native/opentelemetry
  • Use Langfuse from Go/Java/C#/Ruby via OTEL: https://langfuse.com/resources/engineering/opentelemetry-languages
  • Prompt API: https://api.reference.langfuse.com#tag/prompts
  • Scores via API/SDK: https://langfuse.com/docs/evaluation/evaluation-methods/scores-via-sdk
  • Scores API (read v3): https://langfuse.com/docs/api-and-data-platform/features/scores-api
  • OTEL v4 ingestion checklist: https://langfuse.com/integrations/native/opentelemetry/migration-to-v4

Minimal C# examples

  1. Tracing with OpenTelemetry (HTTP/protobuf) to Langfuse
  • Endpoint: https://{region}.cloud.langfuse.com/api/public/otel/v1/traces
  • Auth: Basic (PUBLIC_KEY:SECRET_KEY)
  • Headers: x-langfuse-ingestion-version: 4

using System; using System.Diagnostics; using System.Net.Http; using System.Text; using OpenTelemetry; using OpenTelemetry.Exporter; using OpenTelemetry.Resources; using OpenTelemetry.Trace;

var publicKey = Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable("LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY"); var secretKey = Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable("LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY"); var baseUrl = Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable("LANGFUSE_BASE_URL") ?? "https://us.cloud.langfuse.com"; var otlpEndpoint = $"{baseUrl}/api/public/otel/v1/traces"; var basicAuth = Convert.ToBase64String(Encoding.UTF8.GetBytes($"{publicKey}:{secretKey}"));

using var tracerProvider = Sdk.CreateTracerProviderBuilder() .SetResourceBuilder(ResourceBuilder.CreateDefault().AddService("my-dotnet-llm-app")) .AddSource("my-llm-app") .AddOtlpExporter(o => { o.Protocol = OtlpExportProtocol.HttpProtobuf; o.Endpoint = new Uri(otlpEndpoint); o.Headers = $"Authorization=Basic {basicAuth},x-langfuse-ingestion-version=4"; }) .Build();

var source = new ActivitySource("my-llm-app"); using (var span = source.StartActivity("chat-completion", ActivityKind.Client)) { // Mark this as a generation with LLM details (see property mapping in docs) span?.SetTag("langfuse.observation.type", "generation"); span?.SetTag("gen_ai.system", "openai"); span?.SetTag("gen_ai.request.model", "gpt-4o"); span?.SetTag("langfuse.observation.input", "{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Capital of France?"}]}");

// ... call your LLM client here, collect usage ... span?.SetTag("gen_ai.usage.prompt_tokens", 10); span?.SetTag("gen_ai.usage.completion_tokens", 5); span?.SetTag("langfuse.observation.output", "{"content":"Paris."}");

// Optional: attach queryable context span?.SetTag("user.id", "user_123"); span?.SetTag("langfuse.session.id", "session_abc"); span?.SetTag("langfuse.tags", new[] { "prod", "web" }); }

  1. Fetch a prompt (production label) via Public API using System.Net.Http; using System.Net.Http.Headers; using System.Text;

var http = new HttpClient { BaseAddress = new Uri(baseUrl) }; http.DefaultRequestHeaders.Authorization = new AuthenticationHeaderValue("Basic", basicAuth); var resp = await http.GetAsync($"/api/public/v2/prompts/my-prompt?label=production"); resp.EnsureSuccessStatusCode(); var promptJson = await resp.Content.ReadAsStringAsync(); // Use the returned prompt + config fields in your LLM call

API reference: GET /api/public/v2/prompts/{promptName} https://api.reference.langfuse.com#tag/prompts/GET/api/public/v2/prompts/%7BpromptName%7D

  1. Create a score (attach custom eval or user feedback) using System.Net.Http; using System.Text; using System.Text.Json;

var score = new { traceId = "your-trace-id", observationId = "optional-observation-id", name = "helpfulness", value = 1, // 0/1 for BOOLEAN dataType = "BOOLEAN", comment = "Thumbs up" };

var content = new StringContent(JsonSerializer.Serialize(score), Encoding.UTF8, "application/json"); http.DefaultRequestHeaders.Authorization = new AuthenticationHeaderValue("Basic", basicAuth); var sResp = await http.PostAsync("/api/public/scores", content); sResp.EnsureSuccessStatusCode();

API reference: POST /api/public/scores https://api.reference.langfuse.com#tag/legacyscorev1/POST/api/public/scores

Notes

  • Use the exact OTLP HTTP path with /v1/traces and set Protocol=HttpProtobuf.
  • For OTEL attributes, follow Langfuse’s property mapping so LLM spans render as generations (gen_ai.* and langfuse.*): https://langfuse.com/integrations/native/opentelemetry
  • You can also integrate Semantic Kernel telemetry and export to Langfuse via OTEL: https://langfuse.com/integrations/frameworks/semantic-kernel

assistant

Short answer: Yes. While there’s no native C# SDK, you can use all Langfuse features from .NET via:

  • Tracing/observability: send OpenTelemetry spans to Langfuse’s OTLP/HTTP endpoint
  • Prompt management: use the Public API to create/fetch prompts
  • Evaluations/scores: use the Scores API
  • Dashboards, alerts, datasets/experiments, users/sessions, etc.: work regardless of your backend language

Docs

  • OpenTelemetry to Langfuse (endpoint, attribute mapping): https://langfuse.com/integrations/native/opentelemetry
  • Use Langfuse from Go/Java/C#/Ruby via OTEL: https://langfuse.com/resources/engineering/opentelemetry-languages
  • Prompt API: https://api.reference.langfuse.com#tag/prompts
  • Scores via API/SDK: https://langfuse.com/docs/evaluation/evaluation-methods/scores-via-sdk
  • Scores API (read v3): https://langfuse.com/docs/api-and-data-platform/features/scores-api
  • OTEL v4 ingestion checklist: https://langfuse.com/integrations/native/opentelemetry/migration-to-v4

Minimal C# examples

  1. Tracing with OpenTelemetry (HTTP/protobuf) to Langfuse
  • Endpoint: https://{region}.cloud.langfuse.com/api/public/otel/v1/traces
  • Auth: Basic (PUBLIC_KEY:SECRET_KEY)
  • Headers: x-langfuse-ingestion-version: 4

using System; using System.Diagnostics; using System.Net.Http; using System.Text; using OpenTelemetry; using OpenTelemetry.Exporter; using OpenTelemetry.Resources; using OpenTelemetry.Trace;

var publicKey = Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable("LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY"); var secretKey = Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable("LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY"); var baseUrl = Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable("LANGFUSE_BASE_URL") ?? "https://us.cloud.langfuse.com"; var otlpEndpoint = $"{baseUrl}/api/public/otel/v1/traces"; var basicAuth = Convert.ToBase64String(Encoding.UTF8.GetBytes($"{publicKey}:{secretKey}"));

using var tracerProvider = Sdk.CreateTracerProviderBuilder() .SetResourceBuilder(ResourceBuilder.CreateDefault().AddService("my-dotnet-llm-app")) .AddSource("my-llm-app") .AddOtlpExporter(o => { o.Protocol = OtlpExportProtocol.HttpProtobuf; o.Endpoint = new Uri(otlpEndpoint); o.Headers = $"Authorization=Basic {basicAuth},x-langfuse-ingestion-version=4"; }) .Build();

var source = new ActivitySource("my-llm-app"); using (var span = source.StartActivity("chat-completion", ActivityKind.Client)) { // Mark this as a generation with LLM details (see property mapping in docs) span?.SetTag("langfuse.observation.type", "generation"); span?.SetTag("gen_ai.system", "openai"); span?.SetTag("gen_ai.request.model", "gpt-4o"); span?.SetTag("langfuse.observation.input", "{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Capital of France?"}]}");

// ... call your LLM client here, collect usage ... span?.SetTag("gen_ai.usage.prompt_tokens", 10); span?.SetTag("gen_ai.usage.completion_tokens", 5); span?.SetTag("langfuse.observation.output", "{"content":"Paris."}");

// Optional: attach queryable context span?.SetTag("user.id", "user_123"); span?.SetTag("langfuse.session.id", "session_abc"); span?.SetTag("langfuse.tags", new[] { "prod", "web" }); }

  1. Fetch a prompt (production label) via Public API using System.Net.Http; using System.Net.Http.Headers; using System.Text;

var http = new HttpClient { BaseAddress = new Uri(baseUrl) }; http.DefaultRequestHeaders.Authorization = new AuthenticationHeaderValue("Basic", basicAuth); var resp = await http.GetAsync($"/api/public/v2/prompts/my-prompt?label=production"); resp.EnsureSuccessStatusCode(); var promptJson = await resp.Content.ReadAsStringAsync(); // Use the returned prompt + config fields in your LLM call

API reference: GET /api/public/v2/prompts/{promptName} https://api.reference.langfuse.com#tag/prompts/GET/api/public/v2/prompts/%7BpromptName%7D

  1. Create a score (attach custom eval or user feedback) using System.Net.Http; using System.Text; using System.Text.Json;

var score = new { traceId = "your-trace-id", observationId = "optional-observation-id", name = "helpfulness", value = 1, // 0/1 for BOOLEAN dataType = "BOOLEAN", comment = "Thumbs up" };

var content = new StringContent(JsonSerializer.Serialize(score), Encoding.UTF8, "application/json"); http.DefaultRequestHeaders.Authorization = new AuthenticationHeaderValue("Basic", basicAuth); var sResp = await http.PostAsync("/api/public/scores", content); sResp.EnsureSuccessStatusCode();

API reference: POST /api/public/scores https://api.reference.langfuse.com#tag/legacyscorev1/POST/api/public/scores

Notes

  • Use the exact OTLP HTTP path with /v1/traces and set Protocol=HttpProtobuf.
  • For OTEL attributes, follow Langfuse’s property mapping so LLM spans render as generations (gen_ai.* and langfuse.*): https://langfuse.com/integrations/native/opentelemetry
  • You can also integrate Semantic Kernel telemetry and export to Langfuse via OTEL: https://langfuse.com/integrations/frameworks/semantic-kernel
